items.desc: Broken in on a long walk from Glendale after the red car stalled at Edendale. The owner arrived with blisters, a sunburn and both feet, which he counted as a win.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Bought from a heavyweight who fought Friday nights at the Legion Stadium and walked home along Selma afterward. He claimed the boots never once went down.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of the Marksman
items.desc: The nails were filed flat at the heel so the owner could stand on a rooftop without a sound. A Brute in the Hollywood Hotel learned this, briefly.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen on Poverty Row swore by hobnails for roof jumps, mostly because the studio would not pay for anything better. This pair has landed off three balconies and one moving truck.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of the Engineer
items.desc: Somebody in the Columbia electrical department pencilled amperages on the tongue and then wore the numbers off. Rubber heels, sensible around live cable.

items.name: Patched Steel-toed Boots
items.desc: Fresh leather sewn over an old steel cap that refuses to quit.

items.name: Steel-toed Boots of Strength
items.desc: Issued to a Burbank riveter before the Dome came down. He kicked a stuck hangar door open with them every morning, and lately he has found other things to kick.

items.name: Steel-toed Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Heavy enough to anchor a man in a Santa Ana wind and slow enough to get him noticed. Union men call lifting them a day's work.

items.name: Steel-toed Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Legion men say a fighter who trains in steel toes has nothing to fear in the ring at El Centro and Selma, except the bill for the canvas.

items.name: Steel-toed Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off a San Pedro longshoreman who came up to Hollywood chasing studio wages. The toes have caught more dropped crates than he cared to count.

items.name: Patched Cotton Gloves
items.desc: Mended with thread from three different spools, none of them white. Wardrobe would call it a costume choice.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of Intellect
items.desc: Issued to a script girl at Columbia who caught every continuity error on the lot, including two in her own contract. She left them on a Gower Street lunch counter and never came back for them.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Thin cotton that smells faintly of Echo Park Lake at dawn. The last owner fed the ducks every morning, Dome or no Dome, and claimed it was the only thing keeping him sane.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: A Pacific Electric conductor wore these through double shifts on the Hollywood line, taking nickels from people with nowhere left to ride. They held up longer than the timetable did.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of the Engineer
items.desc: Pulled off a studio electrician at the Christie lot who was rewiring a stage when the hive came through the wall. He finished the job first. The scorch marks on the thumbs suggest he finished it in a hurry.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of the Doctor
items.desc: Folded into the bottom of a nurse's bag at the Hollywood aid station, smelling of carbolic and cold coffee. She swears by them for stitching, and at them for everything else.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: These went to every Sunday service at Angelus Temple for six years and passed the collection plate down a great many rows. The palms shine where the brass rested.

items.name: Patched Leather Gloves
items.desc: The left glove has been patched, more or less, with a scrap of old saddle. The right one is still waiting its turn.

items.name: Leather Gloves of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch trick rider who could have his rope off the saddle horn before the director finished shouting. Then the pictures started talking and wanted fewer horses. The gloves stayed behind.

items.name: Leather Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Lineman's leather, oiled until it stopped caring about the weather. A Bureau of Power and Light crew wore them up poles along Sunset long after anyone stopped sending their pay.

items.name: Leather Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Soft kid leather that once belonged to a choir soloist at a Hollywood Methodist church. She sang straight through a hive surge without missing a note, and has been humming ever since.

items.name: Leather Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntman's gloves with the fingertips cut away for grip. The man who wore them fell off the Pantages roof eleven times for one picture and was paid for four.

items.name: Leather Gloves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a man in these could swing a cargo hook and a bad temper with equal ease. They came up to Hollywood in a crate of bananas, which is how most things from San Pedro arrive.

items.name: Leather Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday they made the long walk from Hollywood to Angelus Temple and back, a hymnal tucked under one arm. They smell of saddle soap and old pages.

items.name: Patched Canvas Work Gloves
items.desc: Mended with squares of mattress ticking and the faith of a man who could not afford new ones.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of Agility
items.desc: Cut thin at the knuckles so a rigger could feel the rope before he trusted it. The owner went up the Egyptian's fly loft faster than anything came down it.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of Strength
items.desc: Belonged to a Columbia set carpenter who hauled flats two at a time and complained that the studio only paid him for one.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Double-stitched for a labourer on the Hollywood Reservoir job, who wore them through two summers and one foreman. The canvas outlasted both.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of the Boxer
items.desc: Somebody's cornerman wore these to tape hands at the Legion Stadium on Friday nights, then to stack the folding chairs after. They still smell of liniment and cigar.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of the Marksman
items.desc: Stembridge's armourers wore pairs like this to clean the rental rifles without fingerprinting the bluing. The trigger finger on this one was trimmed short by someone who meant business.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taken off a stuntman who swung from the Pantages marquee for a two-reeler and landed in a pie cart. Grip palms, light cuffs, and one cream stain that will not wash out.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of the Engineer
items.desc: Pockets for a pencil and a fuse are sewn into the cuff, the sort of improvement studio electricians design on their lunch hour. A scorched thumb records the one time the theory was wrong.

items.name: Patched Mail-backed Gloves
items.desc: Every third ring is a washer from a hardware store on Cahuenga, wired in where the originals gave out.

items.name: Mail-backed Gloves of Strength
items.desc: A Post 43 man wore these to drag the captured German field gun back into place after every Fourth of July parade. The knuckle rings are hammered flat from the effort.

items.name: Mail-backed Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Knitted steel over horsehide, heavy enough that wearing them all day counts as exercise. The last owner held a barricade on Highland for eleven hours and said his hands were the only part of him not tired.

items.name: Mail-backed Gloves of the Boxer
items.desc: Legion Stadium promoters swore nobody ever fought in these. Nobody believed them, least of all the sparring partner with a ring pattern on his cheek.

items.name: Mail-backed Gloves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a longshoreman had the mail sewn on to keep cargo hooks out of his knuckles. Salt still crusts the seams.

items.name: Patched Braces
items.desc: Someone's wife darned the left strap with yellow thread because yellow was what she had. It holds.

items.name: Braces of Intellect
items.desc: A script reader at Paramount wore these through four thousand pages of rejected scenarios. He claimed snug trousers kept the mind sharp, and nobody in the department cared to argue.

items.name: Braces of Spirit
items.desc: Sunday braces, worn under a good jacket to Hollywood Presbyterian and taken off again before supper. A certain calm settles on whoever snaps them into place.

items.name: Braces of Stamina
items.desc: Heavy webbing cut for a red-car motorman, who stood ten hours a day on the Hollywood Boulevard line and never once sat down on the company's time.

items.name: Braces of the Engineer
items.desc: Grease on one strap, solder burns on the other. They came off a sound man at the Christie lot who held that a proper engineer keeps his trousers up and his wiring down.

items.name: Braces of the Doctor
items.desc: Left on a coat hook at Hollywood Receiving Hospital by a house surgeon. A faint smell of iodine survives every washing, and so does a habit of noticing what ails the people nearby.

items.name: Braces of the Deacon
items.desc: Two long walks a day to Angelus Temple, rain or shine, and the straps have the patient stretch to show for it. Hymnal dust has settled deep into the weave.

items.name: Patched Leather Belt
items.desc: Split once at the buckle and riveted back together by a cobbler on Cahuenga for a nickel.

items.name: Leather Belt of Agility
items.desc: Mack Sennett's stunt department wore this one through a decade of pratfalls off moving streetcars. The leather bends like willow and the buckle has never let go mid-tumble.

items.name: Leather Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Oil-field leather from Signal Hill, made for twelve-hour shifts and a man who ate his lunch standing up.

items.name: Leather Belt of Spirit
items.desc: Whoever tooled the little wild roses along this belt did it slowly, on porch evenings, for no reason but the pleasure of it. Some of that patience still clings to the leather.

items.name: Leather Belt of the Acrobat
items.desc: Traded for a sandwich behind a circus wagon parked in Edendale by a wire walker between engagements. She swore it had saved her twice when the net was only a rumour.

items.name: Leather Belt of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, salted stiff and smelling of tar and coffee sacks. The buckle carries a dent where a cargo hook found it instead of its owner.

items.name: Leather Belt of the Deacon
items.desc: Belted on each morning beneath a black coat for street-corner preaching at Hollywood and Cahuenga. The fourth hole is worn smooth; the fifth, reserved for church suppers, hardly at all.

items.name: Patched Canvas Web Belt
items.desc: Mended with sailcloth and a laundry tag from a Selma Avenue boarding house. The landlady kept the deposit anyway.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of Agility
items.desc: Cinched tight on a Gower Gulch extra who could vault a hitching rail without spilling his coffee. Central Casting kept calling him back for the falls.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of Strength
items.desc: A crate man at the Christie lot wore this hauling scenery flats two at a time. The union steward asked him to stop making the others look bad.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Survived a full week of night shoots on a Poverty Row serial, which is more than the leading lady managed.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of the Boxer
items.desc: Bought outside the Legion Stadium on a Friday night from a cornerman short of carfare home. It still smells faintly of liniment and cheap cigars.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of the Marksman
items.desc: Its pouches were sized for stripper clips by someone who counted every round and seldom needed the second one.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of the Acrobat
items.desc: Left on a trapeze rig after a circus picture wrapped. The grips swear the stunt girl who owned it walked home along a telephone wire.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of the Engineer
items.desc: Sound-stage electricians kept pliers, tape and a pencil stub in its loops, and kept the generator turning through two hive surges.

items.name: Patched Plated Belt
items.desc: Two plates are original. The rest are flattened tobacco tins, which at least keep the rust company.

items.name: Plated Belt of Strength
items.desc: Columbia's lot blacksmith built it for a strongman picture, then wore it himself after the strongman complained it was too heavy.

items.name: Plated Belt of Stamina
items.desc: The steel came off a wrecked Model T door and the leather off a saddle nobody missed. Between them they have taken more punishment than a contract player's dignity.

items.name: Plated Belt of the Boxer
items.desc: Worn under a robe by a Legion Stadium heavyweight who claimed it was for his back. The referee never checked, and the other fellow never asked twice.

items.name: Plated Belt of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks on a longshoreman who unloaded Cornero's boats and never once wondered aloud what was in the crates.

items.name: Patched Shirt Cuffs
items.desc: Mended with a square of flour-sack cotton by someone who could not afford new ones and could not bear to go without.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of Intellect
items.desc: Starched linen with a column of pencilled figures on the left cuff, the habit of a studio accountant who did his sums where the producer could not borrow the paper.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of Spirit
items.desc: Their owner wore them to the Easter sunrise service at the Hollywood Bowl every year and swore they never wrinkled before noon. The pastor called it grace; the laundry called it starch.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of Stamina
items.desc: Double-thick cotton, stitched for a court stenographer who sat through the longest trials of 1929 and outlasted two judges.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of the Engineer
items.desc: Spare fuses rode tucked into these on a Warner's sound man, which saved a picture once and his thumb twice.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of the Doctor
items.desc: Iodine never quite washed out of these. Their last owner, a studio doctor, rolled them back for stitches and forward again for the bill.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of the Deacon
items.desc: Thinned on the underside from resting on pew-backs at Angelus Temple. They still smell faintly of hymnals and the long walk up Glendale Boulevard.

items.name: Patched Leather Wrist Straps
items.desc: Somebody sewed a strip of boot tongue over the split. It holds, which is more than the boot did.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of Agility
items.desc: A Sennett stuntman buckled these on for the roof falls nobody else would take. He took a great many, and billed for every one.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of Stamina
items.desc: Thick as a saddle girth and nearly as stiff. A teamster on the Lankershim road swore by them for twelve-hour days.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of Spirit
items.desc: Hand-tooled with a sprig of white sage by a Temple volunteer who said the work kept her calm. Nobody argued with her.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taped at the seams by a trapeze man who came west with a circus and stayed for picture money. He maintained that falling was the easy part.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Stevedore
items.desc: Salt-stained from the San Pedro docks, where they held a longshoreman's wrists together through ten years of cargo hooks and crates of tinned peaches.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Deacon
items.desc: Buckled on every Sunday for the walk to service and the long afternoon of stacking chairs afterward. Faith, the deacon maintained, was mostly furniture.

items.name: Patched Canvas Wrist Wraps
items.desc: Mended so often with sailcloth and flour sacking that barely a thread of the original canvas remains.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Agility
items.desc: Taped on by a Christie comedy stuntman before every pratfall. He claimed they saved his wrists through forty takes of slipping on the same banana peel.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Strength
items.desc: A Gower Gulch blacksmith wound these on before shoeing horses for the Westerns. The canvas has gone stiff where the hammer handle rubbed, day after day.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Stamina
items.desc: Issued to a Pacific Electric track gang that worked double shifts laying rail. Not one man complained, or at least not one complained twice.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Boxer
items.desc: Smelling faintly of liniment and Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, they belonged to a welterweight who never once went down before the eighth round.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Marksman
items.desc: Stembridge's range armourer wore these behind Marathon Street, where he split playing cards edgewise for visiting directors. He never missed, and never got a screen credit for it either.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Acrobat
items.desc: From a trapeze flyer hired for a circus picture that folded after one week. She kept the wraps; the studio kept the net.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Engineer
items.desc: Studio electricians wind canvas over their cuffs to keep sleeves clear of the dynamos. The scorch marks on this pair suggest the advice arrived a little late.

items.name: Patched Steel Bracers
items.desc: Mended with a stove bolt and a strip of harness leather. Cheaper than new, and the bolt only falls out on Tuesdays.

items.name: Steel Bracers of Strength
items.desc: Hammered out in a Paramount machine shop by a blacksmith who swore he had shod every horse in every Western since 1914. He bent the second plate cold, just to make a point.

items.name: Steel Bracers of Stamina
items.desc: Lined with felt cut from an old billiard table at the Hollywood Hotel. The plates take the beating, the felt takes the sweat, and the wearer takes the rest of the night shift.

items.name: Steel Bracers of the Boxer
items.desc: Taped over at the Legion Stadium by a corner man who wanted his heavyweight to block with his forearms instead of his chin. The heavyweight lost on points but kept every tooth.

items.name: Steel Bracers of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off the San Pedro docks with salt in the rivets and a longshoreman's habit of catching cargo hooks before they caught him. Still smells faintly of tar and banana boats.

items.name: Brass Locket of Strength
items.desc: Inside is a tintype of a Bakersfield blacksmith who could lift a buggy by the axle. His granddaughter swore the picture made her arms stronger. Nobody in the family argued with her.

items.name: Brass Locket of Agility
items.desc: Found in the gutter outside the Pantages after a pickpocket was chased the length of the Boulevard. He was never caught, and left the locket behind as a sort of receipt.

items.name: Brass Locket of Stamina
items.desc: A cannery girl wore it through fourteen-hour shifts and a long red-car ride home, every day for six years. The hinge gave out before she did.

items.name: Brass Locket of Intellect
items.desc: The photograph has been swapped for a folded slip carrying a column of figures in very small handwriting. A studio bookkeeper's, by the look of it, and the figures do not add up in the studio's favour.

items.name: Brass Locket of Spirit
items.desc: Pressed violets from Hollywood Cemetery, still faintly sweet. The widow who kept it sat by the lake there every Sunday and claimed she always came home lighter than she went.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Boxer
items.desc: Engraved on the back: a date, and the round a welterweight went down at the Legion Stadium on a Friday night in 1928. His girl kept the locket. He kept the cauliflower ear.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Acrobat
items.desc: Belonged to a wire-walker from a circus that went broke in Los Angeles in '29. She worked street corners for nickels afterward, and never once looked down at the hat.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks in a longshoreman's pocket, smelling of hemp and bunker oil. The photograph inside is of a ship, which says something about the man.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Marksman
items.desc: Every notch along the rim marks a jackrabbit a Gower Gulch extra shot from the saddle at full gallop. There are a great many notches and, according to the other extras, very few rabbits.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Engineer
items.desc: Built by a grip on the Christie lot from a lamp fitting and a hinge pin, then soldered shut so nobody could see whose picture was inside. Union rules are silent on lockets.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Doctor
items.desc: Smells faintly of iodine. A nurse at a Highland Avenue aid station kept her patients' names folded inside, small enough to leave room for a photograph of her mother.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried on foot to Angelus Temple every Sunday, four miles out from Hollywood and four miles back. The hymnal page folded inside has gone soft as cloth at the creases.

items.name: Brass Ring of Strength
items.desc: Pried from the finger of a Pacific Electric brakeman who could lift a stalled red car's coupling by himself. The brass has gone a little oval from the strain.

items.name: Brass Ring of Agility
items.desc: Won at a Venice pier ring-toss, or so its last owner said, a pickpocket who worked Grauman's forecourt. He was quick enough to lift a wallet and not quite quick enough to outrun a Drone.

items.name: Brass Ring of Stamina
items.desc: Factory brass, worn by a night watchman who climbed the Taft Building's stairs twice a shift for eleven years. Neither he nor the ring ever sat down.

items.name: Brass Ring of Intellect
items.desc: Its inside is engraved with a crossword answer nobody at the Hollywood Citizen could ever confirm. The previous owner, a proofreader, considered this proof of his own genius.

items.name: Brass Ring of Spirit
items.desc: Somebody's grandmother wore it through the San Francisco quake and two husbands. It still carries a calm the Dome has not managed to crack.

items.name: Brass Ring of the Boxer
items.desc: Ringside at the Legion Stadium, a middleweight hung this on a nail before every Friday bout and swore it was why he never went down. He went down eventually. The ring held up fine.

items.name: Brass Ring of the Acrobat
items.desc: Bent from a trapeze swivel on a Christie comedy set by a stuntwoman who did her own falls and billed the studio for none of them.

items.name: Brass Ring of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from San Pedro in a longshoreman's pocket, along with a cargo hook and a grudge against the shipping line. The salt is still in the grooves.

items.name: Brass Ring of the Marksman
items.desc: Filed with a fine cross-hair by a Griffith Park ranger who hit what he aimed at and liked a reminder close to hand. He traded it for a box of .30-06 the week the Dome came down.

items.name: Brass Ring of the Engineer
items.desc: Machined from a stage-light housing in the Warner Bros. electrical shop by a juicer with time to kill during a twelve-day retake. It runs slightly warm, which he swore was a design feature.

items.name: Brass Ring of the Doctor
items.desc: A Hollywood Presbyterian nurse turned it on her finger while she counted pulses, and one side is rubbed bright from the habit. It smells faintly of carbolic.

items.name: Brass Ring of the Deacon
items.desc: Handed out at an Angelus Temple altar call, it still smells of hymnals and the long walk up from the red-car stop. Sister Aimee's people insist it has never once been near a hip flask.

items.name: Patched Pocketknife
items.desc: Someone wound friction tape round the cracked handle and called it mended. The tape is holding up better than the rest.

items.name: Pocketknife of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch extra who could whittle a clothes-peg between takes and still beat the assistant director to the lunch wagon.

items.name: Pocketknife of Stamina
items.desc: Its owner sat out three days on a stalled Pacific Electric car with nothing but this, a wedge of cheese and patience. Two of those ran out.

items.name: Pocketknife of the Acrobat
items.desc: Carried by a high-wire girl from a stranded circus troupe, tucked in her stocking where the ringmaster could not find it. She trusted it more than the net.

items.name: Pocketknife of the Marksman
items.desc: A Legion rifleman used it to scrape fouling from his Springfield and notch a tally into the stock. He stopped notching when the insects got too numerous to count.

items.name: Pocketknife of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off the San Pedro docks in a longshoreman's back pocket, good for cutting twine, prising crates and settling disputes over whose crate it was.

items.name: Patched Taped Knuckles
items.desc: Layers of new tape over old, like a studio script after the fifth rewrite.

items.name: Taped Knuckles of Agility
items.desc: Wrapped by a flyweight from the Legion Stadium undercard who won on points by never being where the other fellow swung.

items.name: Taped Knuckles of Stamina
items.desc: Worn by a sparring partner who took punches for a living at two dollars a session. He never won a round and never once went down.

items.name: Taped Knuckles of the Acrobat
items.desc: Christie lot stuntmen taped these for a saloon brawl, then went out a second-storey window in the same take. Retakes cost money.

items.name: Taped Knuckles of the Marksman
items.desc: Their last owner rode shotgun on a bootleg truck and preferred to settle matters at forty yards. These were for when the matter came closer.

items.name: Taped Knuckles of the Stevedore
items.desc: Dockside tape, tarred against salt spray. A San Pedro gang boss wore them to the hiring hall, where nobody argued with his choice of men.

items.name: Patched Cane
items.desc: Splinted with friction tape and optimism. It holds weight if asked politely.

items.name: Cane of Strength
items.desc: Topped with a blackthorn knob the size of a fist, it belonged to a Gower Gulch heavy who played villains on camera and collected debts between pictures. He found the second job steadier.

items.name: Cane of Stamina
items.desc: Its owner walked to Central Casting and back every morning for eleven years without once getting a close-up. The cane did most of the standing around for him.

items.name: Cane of the Boxer
items.desc: A cut man at the Legion Stadium rapped it on the ring apron whenever his fighter dropped his left. On Friday nights it landed more often than the fighter did.

items.name: Cane of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks with a longshoreman who swore it was cut from a cargo boom. The crook still catches on crates out of habit.

items.name: Patched Pipe Wrench
items.desc: Handle cracked and riveted back together with a strap of tin. The jaw still bites.

items.name: Pipe Wrench of Intellect
items.desc: A studio electrician's spare, its handle scratched with tidy conduit measurements. He did every sum twice and never once got bitten by a live line.

items.name: Pipe Wrench of Spirit
items.desc: Kept in the boiler room of a Cahuenga boarding house by a janitor who hummed while he worked and slept like a baby. Nobody else in the building did.

items.name: Pipe Wrench of the Engineer
items.desc: Pulled from the Christie machine shop, where it fixed a wind machine, a camera dolly and a producer's Packard in one afternoon. Only the Packard got a screen credit.

items.name: Pipe Wrench of the Doctor
items.desc: Spent the spring at an aid station on Highland opening oxygen bottles and stuck medicine cabinets. The grip still smells faintly of iodine.

items.name: Pipe Wrench of the Deacon
items.desc: Fixed the radiators at Angelus Temple through a long season of revival meetings. The choir sang loud enough that nobody ever heard the pipes knock.

items.name: Patched Prop Fencing Sabre
items.desc: Tape holds the grip on and hope holds the guard. Extras carried it through a pirate picture nobody has ever seen.

items.name: Prop Fencing Sabre of Strength
items.desc: Studio armourers sharpened it properly after the Dome came down. The prop department still wants it back by Friday.

items.name: Prop Fencing Sabre of Stamina
items.desc: Its owner fought eleven takes of a balcony duel on a Gower Street set in July heat, and the sabre held up better than the leading man.

items.name: Prop Fencing Sabre of the Boxer
items.desc: Swapped one Friday night at the Legion Stadium for a ringside seat and a cold hot dog, by a heavyweight who wanted something with more reach than his left.

items.name: Prop Fencing Sabre of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a San Pedro freighter in a crate stencilled for Paramount. The longshoreman who prised the lid off decided it counted as wages.

items.name: Patched Trench Shovel
items.desc: Wired to a hickory handle that once belonged to a broom, which explains the bristle still stuck in the joint.

items.name: Trench Shovel of Strength
items.desc: Heavy enough to crack a drone's shell at the hinge, according to the Post 43 sergeant who ground its edge sharp on the clubhouse steps.

items.name: Trench Shovel of Stamina
items.desc: Belonged to a man who dug latrines at Saint-Mihiel for a week straight, then dug house foundations in Beachwood Canyon for considerably better pay.

items.name: Trench Shovel of the Boxer
items.desc: Leaned against the Legion Stadium ropes for years, scraping up sawdust after the Friday card. A middleweight borrowed it the night the Dome came down and never brought it back.

items.name: Trench Shovel of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shovelled coal into San Pedro freighters before a dock hand brought it north for picture work, back when Hollywood still paid by the day.

items.name: Patched Colt Police Positive
items.desc: Electrician's tape holds the left grip on; prayer handles the rest. The precinct sold it surplus for less than the tape cost.

items.name: Colt Police Positive of Agility
items.desc: Carried by a Hollywood Division motorcycle patrolman who could draw, fire and still look good in the newsreel. Someone eased the hammer to a hair trigger, and they never waited for anything either.

items.name: Colt Police Positive of Stamina
items.desc: A night watchman at the Christie lot kept this through eleven years of graveyard shifts and one very long Tuesday. The grips are worn smooth by a man who simply refused to go home.

items.name: Colt Police Positive of the Acrobat
items.desc: Belonged to a stuntman who fired it upside down from a moving red car for a two-reeler nobody released. The studio kept the footage; he kept the gun and both collarbones, mostly.

items.name: Colt Police Positive of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner shot clay pigeons for money in Griffith Park and ran a respectable book on himself. A neat notch filed in the rear sight never once needed explaining.

items.name: Colt Police Positive of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from San Pedro in a longshoreman's coat pocket, alongside a cargo hook and a docked payslip. Heavy hands squeezed this trigger, and the trigger guard has the faint bend to prove it.

items.name: Patched Colt M1911
items.desc: Somebody mended the cracked grip with friction tape and optimism. The tape, at least, is holding.

items.name: Colt M1911 of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch stunt rider who could draw, fire and fall off a horse in the same second. Only the falling ever made the picture.

items.name: Colt M1911 of Stamina
items.desc: Carried through the Argonne by a corporal who outlasted his regiment, his marriage and two landlords. The grips are worn smooth where he held on.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Tucked into the waistband of a wire-walker from the Christie lot, it has spent more time upside down than right side up. It fires either way.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner, a Legion range officer, hit what he aimed at and nothing else, a rarer gift on the Boulevard than a good speaking voice. A small notch is filed beside the rear sight.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shipped north from the San Pedro docks in a crate marked machine parts, by a longshoreman who thought the label accurate enough. Faint tar still darkens the grips.

items.name: Patched Winchester Model 1894
items.desc: Somebody mended the cracked forestock with baling wire and faith. Both are holding, for now.

items.name: Winchester Model 1894 of Agility
items.desc: Light enough to swing from the hip off a running board, which is exactly how its last owner left Gower Street in a hurry.

items.name: Winchester Model 1894 of Stamina
items.desc: Carried the length of Hollywood Boulevard and back every night for a month by a night watchman who never once sat down. His feet gave out before the rifle did.

items.name: Winchester Model 1894 of the Acrobat
items.desc: A stunt rider at the Christie lot fired it upside down from under a galloping horse, for two dollars a take and a bandage.

items.name: Winchester Model 1894 of the Marksman
items.desc: Its rear sight has seven small scratches filed beside it. The owner said they were for jackrabbits, and nobody pressed him on the matter.

items.name: Winchester Model 1894 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a San Pedro lumber schooner wrapped in oilcloth, traded for a case of something the manifest described as canned peaches.

items.name: Patched Winchester Model 1897
items.desc: Sawn short by one owner and splinted back by the next. Nobody agrees on what either of them was thinking.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of Agility
items.desc: Quick on the pump and quicker out of a doorway. Its owner kept the slide slick with cold cream lifted from a Max Factor counter.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of Stamina
items.desc: This one stood guard outside the Hollywood police station for nine straight nights. The patrolman holding it managed eight.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taken off a stuntman who did his own falls at Columbia and his own shooting everywhere else. The buttplate is dented from landings.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of the Marksman
items.desc: Most men buy a shotgun so they need not aim. The fellow who owned this one aimed anyway, and the Gower Gulch extras still talk about it.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Rode shotgun on Tony Cornero's liquor trucks up from the San Pedro waterfront, which is a job description as well as a figure of speech.

items.name: Patched Trash Can Lid
items.desc: Three bottle caps and a dab of solder hold the hole shut. The landlord wants it back; the landlord can wait.

items.name: Trash Can Lid of Strength
items.desc: Lifted from an alley off Cahuenga by a teamster who used it to stop a Drone's charge, then the next one, then one more for good measure.

items.name: Trash Can Lid of Stamina
items.desc: Each dent is a story, and this lid holds enough of them to fill a Sunday supplement. Its owner walked home from Gower Gulch behind it, slowly but in one piece.

items.name: Trash Can Lid of the Boxer
items.desc: Somebody swiped it from the bins outside the Legion Stadium on a Friday night, still ringing from the crowd. It holds a guard the way a good welterweight does, chin down and patient.

items.name: Trash Can Lid of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks lashed to a fish truck, back when trucks still came up from anywhere. The longshoreman who carried it knew when to shove and when to sidestep.

items.name: Patched Work Lamp
items.desc: Wound with friction tape where the cord split and wired to a bent coat hanger for a handle. It works, mostly.

items.name: Work Lamp of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a Paramount gaffer who read the union contract by its light, cover to cover, twice. Nobody ever caught him on a technicality.

items.name: Work Lamp of Spirit
items.desc: Its glow is warm and steady, the sort that keeps a night watchman calm through the small hours while the hive hums beyond the fence.

items.name: Work Lamp of the Engineer
items.desc: Rewired from a Lockheed hangar inspection light by a man who refused to let anything stop working, himself included.

items.name: Work Lamp of the Doctor
items.desc: Hung over an aid-station cot on Vine through more long nights than the nurse cares to count. It smells faintly of iodine and carbolic.

items.name: Work Lamp of the Deacon
items.desc: Lit the long walk to Angelus Temple for a deacon who would not miss a service for any bug the hive could send. The handle smells of hymnals and Echo Park fog.

items.name: Patched Medical Bag
items.desc: Mended with harness leather from the Gower Gulch stables. It carries bandages well and horse liniment better.

items.name: Medical Bag of Intellect
items.desc: Inside the lid, a pencilled dosage table in a careful hand, corrected twice. Its owner trusted arithmetic over bedside manner, and lost fewer patients for it.

items.name: Medical Bag of Spirit
items.desc: The nurse who owned it hummed while she worked and slept soundly afterwards, which on a hive-surge night counts as a medical marvel.

items.name: Medical Bag of the Engineer
items.desc: Converted by a studio electrician who reckoned splints and fuses wanted the same tidy compartments. Gauze sits beside spare wire, and nobody has yet confused the two.

items.name: Medical Bag of the Doctor
items.desc: Bought secondhand from a Highland Avenue physician who left town just before the Dome came down. His prescription pad is still in the side pocket, half used and wholly illegible.

items.name: Medical Bag of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried door to door in Echo Park by a Temple volunteer who handed out soup, iodine and Scripture in equal measure. The leather smells faintly of hymnals.

items.name: Patched Pocket Testament
items.desc: Rebound in a scrap of tent canvas after a rainy revival meeting out in the Valley. Exodus is slightly water-stained, which seems fitting.

items.name: Pocket Testament of Intellect
items.desc: Margins crowded with cross-references in three colours of ink. Its former owner could argue Leviticus with a Red Squad sergeant and win on points.

items.name: Pocket Testament of Spirit
items.desc: Opened so often to the Psalms that it now falls there on its own. It sits easier in the hand than most things under the Dome.

items.name: Pocket Testament of the Engineer
items.desc: Found in the coat of a Lockheed riveter, with a slip of blueprint paper marking Nehemiah, the book about rebuilding walls.

items.name: Pocket Testament of the Doctor
items.desc: Belonged to a mission doctor home from China, who kept a pressed poppy in Luke because Luke was a physician too.

items.name: Pocket Testament of the Deacon
items.desc: Handed out at the Angelus Temple doors by the thousand, this one walked from Echo Park and back every Sunday. Its owner wore out three pairs of shoes before the binding showed a scratch.

items.name: Plain Newsboy Cap
items.desc: Thirty-five cents at a Boulevard haberdasher, and it looks it. Respectable enough to get a man served at the Musso & Frank counter.

items.name: Newsboy Cap of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a copy boy at the Examiner who read every edition before he sold it and could quote the box scores back to the sports editor. Nobody got the better of him on change.

items.name: Newsboy Cap of Spirit
items.desc: Worn by a paperboy on the Boulevard who whistled through every headline, good news or bad. The Dome went up and he kept whistling, which some found heartening and others did not.

items.name: Newsboy Cap of Stamina
items.desc: Sweat-stained from twelve-hour days hawking extras along the Pacific Electric platforms. The lining has outlasted three owners and one riot.

items.name: Newsboy Cap of the Engineer
items.desc: A studio grip's cap, smudged with machine oil from the Paramount electrical shop. There is a coil of fuse wire stitched into the lining, either for luck or because he ran out of pockets.

items.name: Newsboy Cap of the Doctor
items.desc: Left behind on a bench at the Highland aid station. Its owner pencilled dosages inside the brim in a hand only a pharmacist could read, and possibly not even one.

items.name: Newsboy Cap of the Deacon
items.desc: Smells of hymnals and the long walk to Angelus Temple. A deacon wore it to every Echo Park service and took it off for nobody but the Lord and Sister Aimee.

items.name: Plain Leather Flying Cap
items.desc: Sold by the dozen to motorcycle cops and delivery riders. Nobody ever looked twice at one, which suited the cops fine.

items.name: Leather Flying Cap of Agility
items.desc: Made for a Hell's Angels stunt flier who could roll a Fokker under a telegraph wire. The picture still plays nightly at Grauman's; his name was in very small type near the end.

items.name: Leather Flying Cap of Stamina
items.desc: Lined with sheepskin thick enough for an open cockpit at ten thousand feet. Nowhere under the Dome gets that cold, but the padding has taken plenty of knocks on its owner's behalf.

items.name: Leather Flying Cap of Spirit
items.desc: Traded at United Airport by an air-mail pilot for a cup of coffee and a cigarette. He says he will fly again when the Dome comes down, and he says it cheerfully every morning.

items.name: Leather Flying Cap of the Acrobat
items.desc: Wing-walkers wore these at county fairs, where a quarter bought the sight of a man strolling along a biplane at sixty miles an hour. The stitching was done by someone who expected to be looked up at.

items.name: Leather Flying Cap of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a San Pedro crane man who wore it against the wharf wind and the swinging cargo nets. He walked to Hollywood for picture work the week before the Dome went up.

items.name: Leather Flying Cap of the Deacon
items.desc: Ridden through a hundred sick calls across Echo Park on a Temple deacon's motorcycle, it kept the dust off him and the cold out. The ear flaps came in handy during rival sermons.

items.name: Plain Canvas Work Cap
items.desc: Exactly what the Gower Street hardware stores sold by the dozen to men queueing for day work. Keeps the sun off. Promises nothing else.

items.name: Canvas Work Cap of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a rigger who ran the catwalks above the Columbia stages without a rope. He hung it on a nail the day the hive moved in, and nobody has seen him come down.

items.name: Canvas Work Cap of Strength
items.desc: Stagehands who shifted flats single-handed wore caps like this, mostly so the foreman could spot them across the lot and hand them the heavier flat.

items.name: Canvas Work Cap of Stamina
items.desc: Through three double shifts and a studio fire, its owner never once took it off. His wife claims it is the only thing holding his head together.

items.name: Canvas Work Cap of the Boxer
items.desc: Ringside at the Legion Stadium every Friday night, worn by a cut man who stayed for every bout. It smells of liniment, cheap cigars and a three-dollar bet on the wrong welterweight.

items.name: Canvas Work Cap of the Marksman
items.desc: A pencil stub is still tucked behind the band, beside a row of tally marks. The camera assistant who wore it judged focus distances by eye, and later judged range on Invader Spitters the same way.

items.name: Canvas Work Cap of the Acrobat
items.desc: Fairbanks's stunt doubles favoured these for rooftop chases: snug enough to stay on through a somersault, cheap enough to lose off a ledge without telling wardrobe.

items.name: Canvas Work Cap of the Engineer
items.desc: Inside the crown, a wiring diagram for a ten-kilowatt arc lamp has been sketched in indelible pencil. The electrician who drew it kept his notes where producers would never think to look.

items.name: Plain M1917 Helmet
items.desc: Bought off a Main Street surplus table for less than a ticket to Grauman's. It stops a thrown bottle. Larger objects remain an open question.

items.name: M1917 Helmet of Strength
items.desc: Its last owner swung a sledge on the Mulholland Dam pours and dug trenches at Saint-Mihiel before that. He reckons digging under shellfire was the lighter job.

items.name: M1917 Helmet of Stamina
items.desc: Post 43 men say this one took a German rifle round in the Argonne and a falling arc lamp at Warner Bros., and its owner walked away from both.

items.name: M1917 Helmet of the Boxer
items.desc: Hung on a hook in the dressing room under the Legion Stadium, where a heavyweight from the 40th Division wore it to sparring as a joke. The joke wore off; the dent did not.

items.name: M1917 Helmet of the Stevedore
items.desc: Longshoremen at San Pedro took to army surplus after one too many cargo nets came loose overhead. Salt has eaten at the rim.

items.name: Plain Arrow Shirt and Vest
items.desc: Nothing to remark upon, which in a town full of extras in borrowed tuxedos is its own kind of distinction.

items.name: Arrow Shirt and Vest of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a script reader at Christie who could find the hole in a two-reeler's plot before the coffee cooled. Pencil shavings still turn up in the vest pocket.

items.name: Arrow Shirt and Vest of Spirit
items.desc: Laundered so often by a Selma Avenue widow that it smells of bluing and patience. She ironed it every Sunday and said the creases were a kind of prayer.

items.name: Arrow Shirt and Vest of Stamina
items.desc: A night watchman at the Hollywood Hotel wore this through three double shifts and a hive surge. The vest held its buttons. The watchman held the lobby.

items.name: Arrow Shirt and Vest of the Engineer
items.desc: Pulled off a sound-stage electrician who still owes the union three weeks' dues. Burn marks on the left cuff trace the exact route of a live cable.

items.name: Arrow Shirt and Vest of the Doctor
items.desc: Starched stiff enough to stand on its own, the way the house physician at the Roosevelt liked it. A faint smell of iodine never quite washed out.

items.name: Arrow Shirt and Vest of the Deacon
items.desc: Walked to Angelus Temple and back every Sunday, rain or shine, which in Los Angeles means shine. The watch pocket holds a folded hymn sheet and a nickel for the plate.

items.name: Plain Work Jacket
items.desc: Standard issue for studio grips: four pockets, no opinions. Nobody on a set looks twice at it, which is the point.

items.name: Work Jacket of Agility
items.desc: Cut short at the waist for a Columbia stunt rider who liked to vault onto a moving horse without snagging the saddle horn. He snagged a fence instead, but the jacket came through fine.

items.name: Work Jacket of Stamina
items.desc: The hide is thick enough to turn a coyote's teeth, as a Vermont Canyon teamster proved twice. The third coyote was a bigger one.

items.name: Work Jacket of Spirit
items.desc: Its last owner rode the Pacific Electric every morning and whistled the whole way, to the despair of the other passengers. The jacket seems to have kept the good cheer.

items.name: Work Jacket of the Acrobat
items.desc: Flexible at the shoulders from years of tumbling off Poverty Row rooftops at three dollars a fall. Stuntmen swear by it, mostly while landing.

items.name: Work Jacket of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks with a longshoreman who traded hauling banana crates for hauling film cans. Salt stains still map the shoulders.

items.name: Work Jacket of the Deacon
items.desc: Outside the Boulevard speakeasies, a street preacher wore this while calling the customers to repent. Several did, briefly, between drinks.

items.name: Plain Carhartt Chore Coat
items.desc: Bought new off a hardware store shelf on Cahuenga, worn once, and traded for a sandwich the week the Dome came down.

items.name: Carhartt Chore Coat of Agility
items.desc: A set dresser at Columbia wore this up and down scaffold ladders forty times a day. The left pocket still holds a pencil stub and a list of chairs nobody delivered.

items.name: Carhartt Chore Coat of Strength
items.desc: Hauled flats on the Christie lot for six seasons. The shoulders are stretched to the shape of a man who carried a fireplace mantel alone rather than wait for the union second.

items.name: Carhartt Chore Coat of Stamina
items.desc: Double-stitched seams, a blanket lining and a smell of wet horse from the Gower Gulch stables. It has outlasted two owners and one stampede staged for a picture never released.

items.name: Carhartt Chore Coat of the Boxer
items.desc: Folded on a ringside bench at the Legion Stadium every Friday night, it caught more spilled ginger ale than punches. Its owner swore the ginger ale was all it ever was.

items.name: Carhartt Chore Coat of the Marksman
items.desc: Stembridge's man on Marathon Street wore it when testing rentals out back. The cuff is singed where a hot casing landed, and a small cross-hair is scratched into the top button.

items.name: Carhartt Chore Coat of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen on Poverty Row favoured it because it tears instead of catching when a fall goes wrong. This one has torn twice and been sewn back by somebody's mother.

items.name: Carhartt Chore Coat of the Engineer
items.desc: Grease handprints, a slide rule in the inside pocket and a generator wiring diagram pencilled on the lining. Its electrician kept his notes where nobody could borrow them.

items.name: Plain Steel Vest
items.desc: Grey plate under black canvas, issued to a bank guard at Hollywood and Highland who preferred to keep wearing it after closing time.

items.name: Steel Vest of Strength
items.desc: Heavy as a sack of cement and twice as cheerful. Only the Legion's bigger men buckle it on without asking for help with the straps.

items.name: Steel Vest of Stamina
items.desc: Police property once, signed out at the Hollywood station and never signed back in. The desk sergeant still brings it up.

items.name: Steel Vest of the Boxer
items.desc: Post 43's heavyweight wore it under his sweater on the walk home from Selma Avenue, reasoning that a man who wins on Friday has made enemies by Saturday.

items.name: Steel Vest of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off a San Pedro freighter, where it was declared as plumbing fittings along with the forty cases of Canadian rye stacked beneath it.

items.name: Plain Wool Trousers
items.desc: Off the rack at a Boulevard haberdasher, sold without a word of salesmanship. They do what trousers do.

items.name: Wool Trousers of Intellect
items.desc: Pressed daily by a Paramount script reader who could spot a third-act problem from the lobby. One pocket still holds a stub of blue pencil and, by all accounts, a strong opinion.

items.name: Wool Trousers of Spirit
items.desc: These spent Sunday mornings in the back pew and Sunday afternoons asleep on the grass in Echo Park. The owner swore both did him equal good.

items.name: Wool Trousers of Stamina
items.desc: Cut for a Pacific Electric conductor who stood eleven hours a day and never once sat down on company time. The seat is practically new.

items.name: Wool Trousers of the Engineer
items.desc: Solder burns dot the left shin. A Warner Bros. sound man wore these up rigging ladders and through one fuse-box fire, and came out with both his trousers and his job.

items.name: Wool Trousers of the Doctor
items.desc: Left on a hook at the aid station on Highland by a surgeon who went back in for one more patient. The nurses have not found the heart to throw them out.

items.name: Wool Trousers of the Deacon
items.desc: They carried an Edendale deacon to Angelus Temple on foot every Wednesday night, a long walk that wore out two pairs of shoes and not a thread of these. Hymnal pages still turn up in the turn-ups.

items.name: Plain Leather Chaps
items.desc: Wardrobe issued these to forty extras for a cattle-drive picture. Thirty-nine came back.

items.name: Leather Chaps of Agility
items.desc: Tom Mix's stunt crew had a trick rider who jumped a fence, a parked Packard and a camera dolly in these. Only the cameraman complained.

items.name: Leather Chaps of Stamina
items.desc: Thick as a saddle and nearly as heavy. A wrangler wore them through two days of a stampede scene the director kept reshooting for the light.

items.name: Leather Chaps of Spirit
items.desc: Sun-faded from long nights in Vermont Canyon, where the coyotes sang and the cowboy who owned these sang back. He claimed it settled his nerves and the horse's.

items.name: Leather Chaps of the Acrobat
items.desc: Made for a stuntman who fell off horses for Universal at five dollars a fall. He kept the chaps and lost the receipts.

items.name: Leather Chaps of the Stevedore
items.desc: Not every pair came off a horse. These hauled cargo on the San Pedro docks before their owner traded the waterfront for a Western backlot, and they still smell faintly of tar.

items.name: Leather Chaps of the Deacon
items.desc: Before the Dome came down, a cowboy preacher rode these out to tent meetings in the Valley. The left thigh is worn smooth where his Bible rode in its holster.

items.name: Plain Levi Strauss Waist Overalls
items.desc: Fresh off the shelf of a Boulevard dry-goods store whose clerk left in a hurry when the Dome came down. The price tag is still pinned on, unpaid.

items.name: Levi Strauss Waist Overalls of Agility
items.desc: Cut loose in the seat by a Gower Gulch extra who climbed into the saddle forty times a day for three dollars and a box lunch. Still smells faintly of horse.

items.name: Levi Strauss Waist Overalls of Strength
items.desc: Bought new on Western Avenue by a grip who carried arc lamps up ladders two at a time. The back pocket has taken the shape of a pipe wrench.

items.name: Levi Strauss Waist Overalls of Stamina
items.desc: Double-stitched by a wardrobe seamstress who had seen three productions run past midnight and expected a fourth. The denim tends to give out long after its owner does.

items.name: Levi Strauss Waist Overalls of the Boxer
items.desc: Worn ringside at the Legion Stadium on Friday nights, where the owner sold peanuts between bouts and settled arguments after them. There is resin dust in the cuffs.

items.name: Levi Strauss Waist Overalls of the Marksman
items.desc: The owner shot rabbits off the Cahuenga Pass road for the pot and never needed a second cartridge. One brass casing still rattles in the watch pocket like a lucky coin.

items.name: Levi Strauss Waist Overalls of the Acrobat
items.desc: Property of a stuntman who fell off the Christie lot's rooftops for a living and swore he had never once missed the mattress. The scuffs on the denim tell it differently.

items.name: Levi Strauss Waist Overalls of the Engineer
items.desc: A studio electrician kept tie-wire, a test lamp and his union card in these. The singe along the hip is from the one live cable he forgot about.

items.name: Plain Steel-kneed Breeches
items.desc: Issued without ceremony from a Legion supply closet, the steel freshly painted to hide whatever it went through last time.

items.name: Steel-kneed Breeches of Strength
items.desc: Kept in a footlocker at Post 43 against the day they might be needed again. The man who wore them out could shift the captured German field gun's trail by himself.

items.name: Steel-kneed Breeches of Stamina
items.desc: Their first owner marched from the Argonne to the Rhine, then from Highland Avenue to the Dome wall, and complained about neither walk.

items.name: Steel-kneed Breeches of the Boxer
items.desc: Sparring partners at the Legion Stadium learned not to clinch with the man who wore these. Tape and liniment are still crusted around the straps.

items.name: Steel-kneed Breeches of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks with a longshoreman who caught the wrong red car home. The steel has knelt on more cargo hatches than church pews.

items.name: Plain Canvas Plimsolls
items.desc: Sold from a bin at a Boulevard five-and-dime, one pair to a customer, no exchanges.

items.name: Canvas Plimsolls of Intellect
items.desc: Bought for tennis at the Hollywood Athletic Club, then worn to the library on Ivar instead, where their owner read everything on radio valves twice.

items.name: Canvas Plimsolls of Spirit
items.desc: Quiet soles for early mornings. Their last owner walked around Echo Park Lake at dawn, fed the ducks, and claimed it did more for him than any doctor.

items.name: Canvas Plimsolls of Stamina
items.desc: Laced up every afternoon by a newsboy who ran the late edition from Vine to La Brea for three years and never once paid a streetcar fare.

items.name: Canvas Plimsolls of the Engineer
items.desc: Studio electricians at Warner's swore by rubber soles and no nails. One of them learned why in hobnails, on a wet stage, in front of the whole crew.

items.name: Canvas Plimsolls of the Doctor
items.desc: Night nurses at Hollywood Hospital wore these because they made no sound on the linoleum. Patients woke up anyway, mostly to complain about the food.

items.name: Canvas Plimsolls of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday they made the long walk to Angelus Temple and back for three services and a hymn sing. The canvas still smells faintly of hymnals and orange peel.

items.name: Plain Work Boots
items.desc: Ordinary hide, ordinary nails, ordinary blisters for the first week.

items.name: Work Boots of Agility
items.desc: A rigger at Columbia wore these along the catwalks forty feet above the stage. He never fell, though he did once drop a sandbag beside a director, who never forgot it.

items.name: Work Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Built for twelve-hour days laying track for the Pacific Electric. Their owner outlasted three foremen and one strike.

items.name: Work Boots of Spirit
items.desc: Owned by a Griffith Park groundskeeper who liked the hills better than people. They still carry the smell of sage and wet oak leaves.

items.name: Work Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: Gower Gulch stuntmen favoured these for rooftop chases, since the soles grip tar paper. The studio paid for the fall and docked the boots from the man's wages.

items.name: Work Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: Salt rings climb to the ankle from years on the San Pedro docks. Their owner could run a sack of coffee up a wet gangplank and be back for another before the foreman finished swearing.

items.name: Work Boots of the Deacon
items.desc: Polished every Saturday night for an usher at Angelus Temple who stood through all three Sunday services and never once sat down. He blamed his feet on the Lord and his knees on the Argonne.

items.name: Plain Hobnail Boots
items.desc: Nothing to recommend them but a full set of nails and an honest pair of laces.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of Agility
items.desc: A Christie lot grip wore these up and down catwalks forty feet above the stage floor and never once dropped a lamp on a director. He considered that restraint.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of Strength
items.desc: Hobnails were made for men who push things: wagons, pianos, scenery flats, the occasional drone back through a doorway. These have pushed all four.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Broken in on a long walk from Glendale after the red car stalled at Edendale. The owner arrived with blisters, a sunburn and both feet, which he counted as a win.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Bought from a heavyweight who fought Friday nights at the Legion Stadium and walked home along Selma afterward. He claimed the boots never once went down.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of the Marksman
items.desc: The nails were filed flat at the heel so the owner could stand on a rooftop without a sound. A Brute in the Hollywood Hotel learned this, briefly.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen on Poverty Row swore by hobnails for roof jumps, mostly because the studio would not pay for anything better. This pair has landed off three balconies and one moving truck.

items.name: Hobnail Boots of the Engineer
items.desc: Somebody in the Columbia electrical department pencilled amperages on the tongue and then wore the numbers off. Rubber heels, sensible around live cable.

items.name: Plain Steel-toed Boots
items.desc: Standard studio-shop issue, the kind every carpenter on the Paramount lot wore before the hive moved in.

items.name: Steel-toed Boots of Strength
items.desc: Issued to a Burbank riveter before the Dome came down. He kicked a stuck hangar door open with them every morning, and lately he has found other things to kick.

items.name: Steel-toed Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Heavy enough to anchor a man in a Santa Ana wind and slow enough to get him noticed. Union men call lifting them a day's work.

items.name: Steel-toed Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Legion men say a fighter who trains in steel toes has nothing to fear in the ring at El Centro and Selma, except the bill for the canvas.

items.name: Steel-toed Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off a San Pedro longshoreman who came up to Hollywood chasing studio wages. The toes have caught more dropped crates than he cared to count.

items.name: Plain Cotton Gloves
items.desc: Ordinary white gloves of the sort every usher and doorman on the Boulevard owns two pairs of. Nobody looks twice at them, which is half the point.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of Intellect
items.desc: Issued to a script girl at Columbia who caught every continuity error on the lot, including two in her own contract. She left them on a Gower Street lunch counter and never came back for them.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Thin cotton that smells faintly of Echo Park Lake at dawn. The last owner fed the ducks every morning, Dome or no Dome, and claimed it was the only thing keeping him sane.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: A Pacific Electric conductor wore these through double shifts on the Hollywood line, taking nickels from people with nowhere left to ride. They held up longer than the timetable did.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of the Engineer
items.desc: Pulled off a studio electrician at the Christie lot who was rewiring a stage when the hive came through the wall. He finished the job first. The scorch marks on the thumbs suggest he finished it in a hurry.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of the Doctor
items.desc: Folded into the bottom of a nurse's bag at the Hollywood aid station, smelling of carbolic and cold coffee. She swears by them for stitching, and at them for everything else.

items.name: Cotton Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: These went to every Sunday service at Angelus Temple for six years and passed the collection plate down a great many rows. The palms shine where the brass rested.

items.name: Plain Leather Gloves
items.desc: Sold from a barrel by the door of a hardware store on Cahuenga, two pairs for a dollar before the Dome. Prices have since gone the way of the view.

items.name: Leather Gloves of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch trick rider who could have his rope off the saddle horn before the director finished shouting. Then the pictures started talking and wanted fewer horses. The gloves stayed behind.

items.name: Leather Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Lineman's leather, oiled until it stopped caring about the weather. A Bureau of Power and Light crew wore them up poles along Sunset long after anyone stopped sending their pay.

items.name: Leather Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Soft kid leather that once belonged to a choir soloist at a Hollywood Methodist church. She sang straight through a hive surge without missing a note, and has been humming ever since.

items.name: Leather Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntman's gloves with the fingertips cut away for grip. The man who wore them fell off the Pantages roof eleven times for one picture and was paid for four.

items.name: Leather Gloves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a man in these could swing a cargo hook and a bad temper with equal ease. They came up to Hollywood in a crate of bananas, which is how most things from San Pedro arrive.

items.name: Leather Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday they made the long walk from Hollywood to Angelus Temple and back, a hymnal tucked under one arm. They smell of saddle soap and old pages.

items.name: Plain Canvas Work Gloves
items.desc: Issued by the dozen from a Gower Gulch supply tent, no questions asked and no sizes either.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of Agility
items.desc: Cut thin at the knuckles so a rigger could feel the rope before he trusted it. The owner went up the Egyptian's fly loft faster than anything came down it.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of Strength
items.desc: Belonged to a Columbia set carpenter who hauled flats two at a time and complained that the studio only paid him for one.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Double-stitched for a labourer on the Hollywood Reservoir job, who wore them through two summers and one foreman. The canvas outlasted both.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of the Boxer
items.desc: Somebody's cornerman wore these to tape hands at the Legion Stadium on Friday nights, then to stack the folding chairs after. They still smell of liniment and cigar.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of the Marksman
items.desc: Stembridge's armourers wore pairs like this to clean the rental rifles without fingerprinting the bluing. The trigger finger on this one was trimmed short by someone who meant business.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taken off a stuntman who swung from the Pantages marquee for a two-reeler and landed in a pie cart. Grip palms, light cuffs, and one cream stain that will not wash out.

items.name: Canvas Work Gloves of the Engineer
items.desc: Pockets for a pencil and a fuse are sewn into the cuff, the sort of improvement studio electricians design on their lunch hour. A scorched thumb records the one time the theory was wrong.

items.name: Plain Mail-backed Gloves
items.desc: Studio armourers made these by the gross for crusade pictures. The mail is real; the crusade was not.

items.name: Mail-backed Gloves of Strength
items.desc: A Post 43 man wore these to drag the captured German field gun back into place after every Fourth of July parade. The knuckle rings are hammered flat from the effort.

items.name: Mail-backed Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Knitted steel over horsehide, heavy enough that wearing them all day counts as exercise. The last owner held a barricade on Highland for eleven hours and said his hands were the only part of him not tired.

items.name: Mail-backed Gloves of the Boxer
items.desc: Legion Stadium promoters swore nobody ever fought in these. Nobody believed them, least of all the sparring partner with a ring pattern on his cheek.

items.name: Mail-backed Gloves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a longshoreman had the mail sewn on to keep cargo hooks out of his knuckles. Salt still crusts the seams.

items.name: Plain Braces
items.desc: Dime-store braces from the Boulevard, the kind every clerk in town wears and nobody in town notices.

items.name: Braces of Intellect
items.desc: A script reader at Paramount wore these through four thousand pages of rejected scenarios. He claimed snug trousers kept the mind sharp, and nobody in the department cared to argue.

items.name: Braces of Spirit
items.desc: Sunday braces, worn under a good jacket to Hollywood Presbyterian and taken off again before supper. A certain calm settles on whoever snaps them into place.

items.name: Braces of Stamina
items.desc: Heavy webbing cut for a red-car motorman, who stood ten hours a day on the Hollywood Boulevard line and never once sat down on the company's time.

items.name: Braces of the Engineer
items.desc: Grease on one strap, solder burns on the other. They came off a sound man at the Christie lot who held that a proper engineer keeps his trousers up and his wiring down.

items.name: Braces of the Doctor
items.desc: Left on a coat hook at Hollywood Receiving Hospital by a house surgeon. A faint smell of iodine survives every washing, and so does a habit of noticing what ails the people nearby.

items.name: Braces of the Deacon
items.desc: Two long walks a day to Angelus Temple, rain or shine, and the straps have the patient stretch to show for it. Hymnal dust has settled deep into the weave.

items.name: Plain Leather Belt
items.desc: Brown cowhide, brass buckle, five holes. Nothing about it would interest a costume designer, which is a mercy.

items.name: Leather Belt of Agility
items.desc: Mack Sennett's stunt department wore this one through a decade of pratfalls off moving streetcars. The leather bends like willow and the buckle has never let go mid-tumble.

items.name: Leather Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Oil-field leather from Signal Hill, made for twelve-hour shifts and a man who ate his lunch standing up.

items.name: Leather Belt of Spirit
items.desc: Whoever tooled the little wild roses along this belt did it slowly, on porch evenings, for no reason but the pleasure of it. Some of that patience still clings to the leather.

items.name: Leather Belt of the Acrobat
items.desc: Traded for a sandwich behind a circus wagon parked in Edendale by a wire walker between engagements. She swore it had saved her twice when the net was only a rumour.

items.name: Leather Belt of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, salted stiff and smelling of tar and coffee sacks. The buckle carries a dent where a cargo hook found it instead of its owner.

items.name: Leather Belt of the Deacon
items.desc: Belted on each morning beneath a black coat for street-corner preaching at Hollywood and Cahuenga. The fourth hole is worn smooth; the fifth, reserved for church suppers, hardly at all.

items.name: Plain Canvas Web Belt
items.desc: Nothing to look at and nothing to complain about. The Legion quartermaster hands these out without asking for a name.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of Agility
items.desc: Cinched tight on a Gower Gulch extra who could vault a hitching rail without spilling his coffee. Central Casting kept calling him back for the falls.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of Strength
items.desc: A crate man at the Christie lot wore this hauling scenery flats two at a time. The union steward asked him to stop making the others look bad.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Survived a full week of night shoots on a Poverty Row serial, which is more than the leading lady managed.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of the Boxer
items.desc: Bought outside the Legion Stadium on a Friday night from a cornerman short of carfare home. It still smells faintly of liniment and cheap cigars.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of the Marksman
items.desc: Its pouches were sized for stripper clips by someone who counted every round and seldom needed the second one.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of the Acrobat
items.desc: Left on a trapeze rig after a circus picture wrapped. The grips swear the stunt girl who owned it walked home along a telephone wire.

items.name: Canvas Web Belt of the Engineer
items.desc: Sound-stage electricians kept pliers, tape and a pencil stub in its loops, and kept the generator turning through two hive surges.

items.name: Plain Plated Belt
items.desc: Grey steel, brown leather, an iron buckle. A Post 43 man called it the only honest thing left in Hollywood.

items.name: Plated Belt of Strength
items.desc: Columbia's lot blacksmith built it for a strongman picture, then wore it himself after the strongman complained it was too heavy.

items.name: Plated Belt of Stamina
items.desc: The steel came off a wrecked Model T door and the leather off a saddle nobody missed. Between them they have taken more punishment than a contract player's dignity.

items.name: Plated Belt of the Boxer
items.desc: Worn under a robe by a Legion Stadium heavyweight who claimed it was for his back. The referee never checked, and the other fellow never asked twice.

items.name: Plated Belt of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks on a longshoreman who unloaded Cornero's boats and never once wondered aloud what was in the crates.

items.name: Plain Shirt Cuffs
items.desc: Nothing to recommend them and nothing to apologise for. Central Casting likes that in an extra too.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of Intellect
items.desc: Starched linen with a column of pencilled figures on the left cuff, the habit of a studio accountant who did his sums where the producer could not borrow the paper.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of Spirit
items.desc: Their owner wore them to the Easter sunrise service at the Hollywood Bowl every year and swore they never wrinkled before noon. The pastor called it grace; the laundry called it starch.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of Stamina
items.desc: Double-thick cotton, stitched for a court stenographer who sat through the longest trials of 1929 and outlasted two judges.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of the Engineer
items.desc: Spare fuses rode tucked into these on a Warner's sound man, which saved a picture once and his thumb twice.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of the Doctor
items.desc: Iodine never quite washed out of these. Their last owner, a studio doctor, rolled them back for stitches and forward again for the bill.

items.name: Shirt Cuffs of the Deacon
items.desc: Thinned on the underside from resting on pew-backs at Angelus Temple. They still smell faintly of hymnals and the long walk up Glendale Boulevard.

items.name: Plain Leather Wrist Straps
items.desc: Saddlery stock from Gower Gulch, sold by the dozen to cowboy extras between pictures.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of Agility
items.desc: A Sennett stuntman buckled these on for the roof falls nobody else would take. He took a great many, and billed for every one.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of Stamina
items.desc: Thick as a saddle girth and nearly as stiff. A teamster on the Lankershim road swore by them for twelve-hour days.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of Spirit
items.desc: Hand-tooled with a sprig of white sage by a Temple volunteer who said the work kept her calm. Nobody argued with her.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taped at the seams by a trapeze man who came west with a circus and stayed for picture money. He maintained that falling was the easy part.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Stevedore
items.desc: Salt-stained from the San Pedro docks, where they held a longshoreman's wrists together through ten years of cargo hooks and crates of tinned peaches.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Deacon
items.desc: Buckled on every Sunday for the walk to service and the long afternoon of stacking chairs afterward. Faith, the deacon maintained, was mostly furniture.

items.name: Plain Canvas Wrist Wraps
items.desc: Bought off a cart on Cahuenga for a dime. They do the job and ask nothing more of anyone.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Agility
items.desc: Taped on by a Christie comedy stuntman before every pratfall. He claimed they saved his wrists through forty takes of slipping on the same banana peel.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Strength
items.desc: A Gower Gulch blacksmith wound these on before shoeing horses for the Westerns. The canvas has gone stiff where the hammer handle rubbed, day after day.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Stamina
items.desc: Issued to a Pacific Electric track gang that worked double shifts laying rail. Not one man complained, or at least not one complained twice.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Boxer
items.desc: Smelling faintly of liniment and Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, they belonged to a welterweight who never once went down before the eighth round.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Marksman
items.desc: Stembridge's range armourer wore these behind Marathon Street, where he split playing cards edgewise for visiting directors. He never missed, and never got a screen credit for it either.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Acrobat
items.desc: From a trapeze flyer hired for a circus picture that folded after one week. She kept the wraps; the studio kept the net.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Engineer
items.desc: Studio electricians wind canvas over their cuffs to keep sleeves clear of the dynamos. The scorch marks on this pair suggest the advice arrived a little late.

items.name: Plain Steel Bracers
items.desc: Standard issue from a Legion supply locker, stencilled once and painted over twice. Nobody will look at them, which is rather the idea.

items.name: Steel Bracers of Strength
items.desc: Hammered out in a Paramount machine shop by a blacksmith who swore he had shod every horse in every Western since 1914. He bent the second plate cold, just to make a point.

items.name: Steel Bracers of Stamina
items.desc: Lined with felt cut from an old billiard table at the Hollywood Hotel. The plates take the beating, the felt takes the sweat, and the wearer takes the rest of the night shift.

items.name: Steel Bracers of the Boxer
items.desc: Taped over at the Legion Stadium by a corner man who wanted his heavyweight to block with his forearms instead of his chin. The heavyweight lost on points but kept every tooth.

items.name: Steel Bracers of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off the San Pedro docks with salt in the rivets and a longshoreman's habit of catching cargo hooks before they caught him. Still smells faintly of tar and banana boats.

items.name: Brass Locket of Strength
items.desc: Inside is a tintype of a Bakersfield blacksmith who could lift a buggy by the axle. His granddaughter swore the picture made her arms stronger. Nobody in the family argued with her.

items.name: Brass Locket of Agility
items.desc: Found in the gutter outside the Pantages after a pickpocket was chased the length of the Boulevard. He was never caught, and left the locket behind as a sort of receipt.

items.name: Brass Locket of Stamina
items.desc: A cannery girl wore it through fourteen-hour shifts and a long red-car ride home, every day for six years. The hinge gave out before she did.

items.name: Brass Locket of Intellect
items.desc: The photograph has been swapped for a folded slip carrying a column of figures in very small handwriting. A studio bookkeeper's, by the look of it, and the figures do not add up in the studio's favour.

items.name: Brass Locket of Spirit
items.desc: Pressed violets from Hollywood Cemetery, still faintly sweet. The widow who kept it sat by the lake there every Sunday and claimed she always came home lighter than she went.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Boxer
items.desc: Engraved on the back: a date, and the round a welterweight went down at the Legion Stadium on a Friday night in 1928. His girl kept the locket. He kept the cauliflower ear.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Acrobat
items.desc: Belonged to a wire-walker from a circus that went broke in Los Angeles in '29. She worked street corners for nickels afterward, and never once looked down at the hat.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks in a longshoreman's pocket, smelling of hemp and bunker oil. The photograph inside is of a ship, which says something about the man.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Marksman
items.desc: Every notch along the rim marks a jackrabbit a Gower Gulch extra shot from the saddle at full gallop. There are a great many notches and, according to the other extras, very few rabbits.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Engineer
items.desc: Built by a grip on the Christie lot from a lamp fitting and a hinge pin, then soldered shut so nobody could see whose picture was inside. Union rules are silent on lockets.

items.name: Brass Locket of the Doctor
