items.desc: A Sennett stuntman buckled these on for the roof falls nobody else would take. He took a great many, and billed for every one.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of Stamina
items.desc: Thick as a saddle girth and nearly as stiff. A teamster on the Lankershim road swore by them for twelve-hour days.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of Spirit
items.desc: Hand-tooled with a sprig of white sage by a Temple volunteer who said the work kept her calm. Nobody argued with her.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taped at the seams by a trapeze man who came west with a circus and stayed for picture money. He maintained that falling was the easy part.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Stevedore
items.desc: Salt-stained from the San Pedro docks, where they held a longshoreman's wrists together through ten years of cargo hooks and crates of tinned peaches.

items.name: Leather Wrist Straps of the Deacon
items.desc: Buckled on every Sunday for the walk to service and the long afternoon of stacking chairs afterward. Faith, the deacon maintained, was mostly furniture.

items.name: Pressed Canvas Wrist Wraps
items.desc: Starched and creased like a banker's trousers. Somebody in wardrobe decided the war deserved a sharp crease, and nobody had the heart to argue.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Agility
items.desc: Taped on by a Christie comedy stuntman before every pratfall. He claimed they saved his wrists through forty takes of slipping on the same banana peel.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Strength
items.desc: A Gower Gulch blacksmith wound these on before shoeing horses for the Westerns. The canvas has gone stiff where the hammer handle rubbed, day after day.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of Stamina
items.desc: Issued to a Pacific Electric track gang that worked double shifts laying rail. Not one man complained, or at least not one complained twice.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Boxer
items.desc: Smelling faintly of liniment and Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, they belonged to a welterweight who never once went down before the eighth round.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Marksman
items.desc: Stembridge's range armourer wore these behind Marathon Street, where he split playing cards edgewise for visiting directors. He never missed, and never got a screen credit for it either.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Acrobat
items.desc: From a trapeze flyer hired for a circus picture that folded after one week. She kept the wraps; the studio kept the net.

items.name: Canvas Wrist Wraps of the Engineer
items.desc: Studio electricians wind canvas over their cuffs to keep sleeves clear of the dynamos. The scorch marks on this pair suggest the advice arrived a little late.

items.name: Pressed Steel Bracers
items.desc: Stamped in one piece on a Lockheed press before the Burbank shop went quiet. Light, tight and uniform like everything the aeroplane men made, and harder to dent than they look.

items.name: Steel Bracers of Strength
items.desc: Hammered out in a Paramount machine shop by a blacksmith who swore he had shod every horse in every Western since 1914. He bent the second plate cold, just to make a point.

items.name: Steel Bracers of Stamina
items.desc: Lined with felt cut from an old billiard table at the Hollywood Hotel. The plates take the beating, the felt takes the sweat, and the wearer takes the rest of the night shift.

items.name: Steel Bracers of the Boxer
items.desc: Taped over at the Legion Stadium by a corner man who wanted his heavyweight to block with his forearms instead of his chin. The heavyweight lost on points but kept every tooth.

items.name: Steel Bracers of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off the San Pedro docks with salt in the rivets and a longshoreman's habit of catching cargo hooks before they caught him. Still smells faintly of tar and banana boats.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Strength
items.desc: Pried off the neck of a red-car motorman who swore it had carried him through the Cahuenga Pass forty times. The forty-first trip carried him nowhere, but the medal held up fine.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Agility
items.desc: Saint Christopher carried a child across a river without slipping once. A Gower Gulch trick rider wore this one through three saddle falls and a runaway buckboard, and she claims the saint did most of the work.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Stamina
items.desc: Worn by a red-car conductor who walked the Hollywood line end to end the night the Dome came down, then turned round and walked it back. He never said what he was looking for.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Intellect
items.desc: The Krotona people up Beachwood Canyon insisted the saint was really an astral symbol of the higher planes. The Catholic who owned it let them talk and kept it on anyway.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Spirit
items.desc: Twice blessed: once by a priest at Blessed Sacrament on Sunset, and once by a stagehand who had played a bishop in two reels for Universal. The owner trusted both blessings equally.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Boxer
items.desc: A welterweight kissed it before every Friday bout at the Legion Stadium and lost eleven of fourteen. He maintained the saint looked after travellers, not fighters, and that the referee was Presbyterian.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen at Gower Gulch pass these around like cigarettes. This one went off a two-storey saloon set, through a sugar-glass window and into a hay wagon, still on its chain.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from San Pedro on a longshoreman's neck, back when the studios paid better for lifting than the docks did. The salt never quite rubbed out of the links.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Marksman
items.desc: Its owner, a Legion sharpshooter, wore it tucked under his shirt so the glint would not give him away on the Beachwood ridge. He hit what he aimed at and was home by supper.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Engineer
items.desc: Hung for a year on a nail above the switchboard at Mulholland Dam, where the keeper said it watched the water better than the gauges did. He took it down the week the hive moved into the spillway.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Doctor
items.desc: Pinned inside the lid of an aid-station nurse's bag, beside the iodine and a list of names she meant to write to. It still smells faintly of carbolic.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday its owner walked from Edendale to Angelus Temple with a hymnal under one arm, and the saint went with him both ways. Sister Aimee would have preferred a plain cross, but she never turned away a traveller.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Strength
items.desc: Its last owner bent horseshoes at the Elks picnic every Fourth of July and never once paid for his own beer. The other brothers called that a fair trade, and so did his knuckles.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Agility
items.desc: Brothers of the lodge swore it never left the owner's finger, though it left plenty of card tables in a hurry. Found in a hedge below Beachwood Canyon, still warm from somebody's pocket.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Stamina
items.desc: Fifty years' membership, says the engraving inside, and not a meeting missed. The old man outlived three Grand Exalted Somethings and, by the look of the scratches, most of an invader drone.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Intellect
items.desc: Someone at the Krotona colony traded it for a book on astral bodies, then regretted the bargain. The original wearer kept the lodge minutes in shorthand for nineteen years and could recite any of them.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Spirit
items.desc: Kept polished by the brother who read the eulogies. He read a great many this autumn, and still found the heart to hum on the walk home.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Boxer
items.desc: Swung at the Legion Stadium on Friday nights, third row, while its owner shouted advice nobody in the ring had asked for. The dent came from a seat back, not a jaw.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Acrobat
items.desc: A trapeze man from the Shrine circus wore this on a ribbon round his neck during performances, which the lodge considered disrespectful and the ringmaster considered sensible.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a longshoreman's pocket and went inland the week before the Dome came down. Tar still sits in the grooves of the crest, and no amount of soap will shift it.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Marksman
items.desc: Three years running, its owner won the Burbank lodge turkey shoot and gave every bird to the widows' fund. The brothers stopped entering out of pure embarrassment.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Engineer
items.desc: Recovered from a toolbox at Mulholland Dam, beside a slide rule and a ham sandwich of uncertain age. The dam keeper says its owner knew every valve in the place by its first name.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Doctor
items.desc: Under the hinged bezel sits a folded prescription for something the druggist would only fill with a wink. Prohibition made physicians very popular lodge members.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Deacon
items.desc: Smells faintly of hymnals and shoe polish from Sunday walks to Angelus Temple. Its owner joined the lodge for the fellowship and the Temple for everything else, and saw no conflict.

items.name: Pressed Hunting Knife
items.desc: Sold in a pasteboard box with a fresh oiled shine and a crease in the sheath you could cut bread on. The Hollywoodland hardware man swears it was never used, which is not a selling point any more.

items.name: Hunting Knife of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch rider who could skin a jackrabbit at a gallop, or so he said in the stable bar. The edge is quicker than the story.

items.name: Hunting Knife of Stamina
items.desc: A deer camp in Vermont Canyon went three weeks on beans and this blade, and it still holds an edge. The owner held out a week longer, which is the part he tells.

items.name: Hunting Knife of the Acrobat
items.desc: Kept in the boot of a circus tumbler who came west for pictures and never left the ground again for less than union scale. Balanced well enough to throw, and twice it has been.

items.name: Hunting Knife of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner carried a Winchester for the shooting and this for everything after. The tally notches along the spine stop at forty, where he ran out of spine.

items.name: Hunting Knife of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off the San Pedro docks, where it opened crates, cut hawsers and settled one disagreement about overtime. Salt still lives in the hilt.

items.name: Pressed Brass Knuckles
items.desc: Machined in a studio prop shop for a gangster picture, then quietly pocketed when the Production Code trimmed the scene.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of Agility
items.desc: Light enough to leave a vest pocket before the other fellow finished his sentence. A Gower Gulch stunt double carried them through eleven pictures and never once got a credit.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of Stamina
items.desc: The previous owner was a night watchman on the Christie lot who backed three Drones down a stairwell and walked home afterward. He kept his hat on throughout.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of the Acrobat
items.desc: Belonged to a stuntwoman who made her living falling off Pacific Electric cars for two-reel comedies. She claimed the trick was landing angry.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of the Marksman
items.desc: Found in the overcoat of a Red Squad detective who hit what he aimed at, with or without a revolver. The inside of the rings is worn smooth from patient waiting.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where longshoremen settled wage disputes before the foreman finished his coffee. Still smells of tarred rope and somebody's spilled cargo.

items.name: Pressed Blackjack
items.desc: The wardrobe department pressed the leather flat and shiny and billed the picture for it. Nobody has explained what a creased blackjack is for, but it photographs well.

items.name: Blackjack of Strength
items.desc: Taken off a Crawford collector who settled accounts on the Strip with it. The lead inside has been topped up twice, and the leather has long since stopped complaining.

items.name: Blackjack of Stamina
items.desc: A night watchman's sap from the Christie lot, worn smooth by thirty years of rounds. Its owner outlasted two studio heads and a fire, and meant to outlast the bugs as well.

items.name: Blackjack of the Boxer
items.desc: Some fights at the Legion Stadium carried on in the alley afterward. The trainer who owned this swore it had a better left hook than his heavyweight, and cheaper upkeep.

items.name: Blackjack of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from San Pedro in a longshoreman's hip pocket after the strike of '23, when the docks settled arguments with something heavier than words.

items.name: Pressed Crowbar
items.desc: Somebody at Paramount had it flattened and plated for a picture about a gentleman burglar. The production folded; the crowbar kept its creases and its billing.

items.name: Crowbar of Intellect
items.desc: Kept beside a Warner Bros. drafting table to correct carpenters who misread the blueprints. Mostly the designer only had to glance at it.

items.name: Crowbar of Spirit
items.desc: Pulled from a fallen Melrose bungalow by a man who said a prayer each time he lifted a beam. He found eleven people alive and kept the bar afterward.

items.name: Crowbar of the Engineer
items.desc: Friction tape on the handle, a gaffer's initials scratched under it. He pried open junction boxes with it and carried a slide rule in the other pocket for balance.

items.name: Crowbar of the Doctor
items.desc: An ambulance driver from the Hollywood receiving hospital carried it for jammed doors and pinned legs. The armband knotted round it has never once been washed.

items.name: Crowbar of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Easter an Edendale church caretaker opened the hymnal crates with it, then walked it down to Angelus Temple when the Dome came. It still smells of pine shelving and old hymnals.

items.name: Pressed Prop Fencing Sabre
items.desc: Lacquered guard, nickel pommel, a blade straight enough for a close-up. Wardrobe insists it was only ever meant to be pointed dramatically at a villain in the third reel.

items.name: Prop Fencing Sabre of Strength
items.desc: Studio armourers sharpened it properly after the Dome came down. The prop department still wants it back by Friday.

items.name: Prop Fencing Sabre of Stamina
items.desc: Its owner fought eleven takes of a balcony duel on a Gower Street set in July heat, and the sabre held up better than the leading man.

items.name: Prop Fencing Sabre of the Boxer
items.desc: Swapped one Friday night at the Legion Stadium for a ringside seat and a cold hot dog, by a heavyweight who wanted something with more reach than his left.

items.name: Prop Fencing Sabre of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a San Pedro freighter in a crate stencilled for Paramount. The longshoreman who prised the lid off decided it counted as wages.

items.name: Pressed Pickaxe
items.desc: Lacquered and buffed to a mirror for a Western in which the miner never digs anything. The studio kept the pick and cut the miner.

items.name: Pickaxe of Strength
items.desc: Six years on the Owens Valley aqueduct went into this handle, and the man who swung it came home with shoulders like a piano mover. Granite gave way to it. Chitin, it turns out, is softer.

items.name: Pickaxe of Stamina
items.desc: Dug three miles of trench at United Airport before opening day, and was back on the job the next morning without so much as a loose wedge.

items.name: Pickaxe of the Boxer
items.desc: Legion regulars knew the groundsman who swung it between bouts to keep his arms loose. He claimed it gave him a better clinch than anyone on the card.

items.name: Pickaxe of the Stevedore
items.desc: Wilmington wharf men used the point to drag hogsheads off the lighters and the flat end to argue with the dock boss. Both ends show the wear.

items.name: Pressed Smith & Wesson .38 Military & Police
items.desc: Somebody in the wardrobe department buffed the frame and boiled the grips, on the theory that a gun should look its best in a fight.

items.name: Smith & Wesson .38 Military & Police of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch extra who practised his fast draw between takes for eleven years and never once got a close-up. The speed, at least, was real.

items.name: Smith & Wesson .38 Military & Police of Stamina
items.desc: A night-shift patrolman carried this through three hive surges on Highland and walked home after each one. The holster wore through twice; he did not.

items.name: Smith & Wesson .38 Military & Police of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen on the Pickford-Fairbanks lot passed it hand to hand across the rigging, so it has fallen from more balconies than any revolver deserves and still shoots straight.

items.name: Smith & Wesson .38 Military & Police of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner filed a notch in the grip for every Spitter he dropped at thirty yards, then stopped when he ran out of grip.

items.name: Smith & Wesson .38 Military & Police of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks in a longshoreman's coat pocket, alongside a cargo hook and a union card. The grip still smells faintly of tar and hemp.

items.name: Pressed Colt M1911
items.desc: Fresh off a studio armourer's bench, cleaned, blued and creased as sharp as a matinee idol's trousers.

items.name: Colt M1911 of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch stunt rider who could draw, fire and fall off a horse in the same second. Only the falling ever made the picture.

items.name: Colt M1911 of Stamina
items.desc: Carried through the Argonne by a corporal who outlasted his regiment, his marriage and two landlords. The grips are worn smooth where he held on.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Tucked into the waistband of a wire-walker from the Christie lot, it has spent more time upside down than right side up. It fires either way.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner, a Legion range officer, hit what he aimed at and nothing else, a rarer gift on the Boulevard than a good speaking voice. A small notch is filed beside the rear sight.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shipped north from the San Pedro docks in a crate marked machine parts, by a longshoreman who thought the label accurate enough. Faint tar still darkens the grips.

items.name: Pressed Remington Model 8
items.desc: Freshly reblued by a studio armourer who insists the forend had warped. Nobody argued with a man holding a self-loading rifle.

items.name: Remington Model 8 of Agility
items.desc: Texas Rangers swore by the type for brush-country gunfights. This one was bought for a Poverty Row Western and has seen more real brush since the Dome came down than the picture ever did.

items.name: Remington Model 8 of Stamina
items.desc: Carried up and down Beachwood Canyon by the dam keeper's nephew, who never sat down on watch. It shows the miles in its sling and nowhere else.

items.name: Remington Model 8 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Went over the side of a Hollywoodland switchback with its owner. Both landed upright in the sage, and only one of them needed a new sight.

items.name: Remington Model 8 of the Marksman
items.desc: Five rounds, five Fliers, one morning on the Pass summit. The man who did it was a county surveyor before the war and still measures distance in chains.

items.name: Remington Model 8 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Loaded onto a Cornero rum boat in a crate marked as machine parts, then unloaded at night by a deckhand who kept it as his fee.

items.name: Pressed Winchester Model 1897
items.desc: Fox's wardrobe department would not let a gun go before the camera looking slept in, so somebody ironed the sling. The hive soldiers remain unimpressed.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of Agility
items.desc: Quick on the pump and quicker out of a doorway. Its owner kept the slide slick with cold cream lifted from a Max Factor counter.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of Stamina
items.desc: This one stood guard outside the Hollywood police station for nine straight nights. The patrolman holding it managed eight.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taken off a stuntman who did his own falls at Columbia and his own shooting everywhere else. The buttplate is dented from landings.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of the Marksman
items.desc: Most men buy a shotgun so they need not aim. The fellow who owned this one aimed anyway, and the Gower Gulch extras still talk about it.

items.name: Winchester Model 1897 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Rode shotgun on Tony Cornero's liquor trucks up from the San Pedro waterfront, which is a job description as well as a figure of speech.

items.name: Pressed Thompson M1928
items.desc: Cleaned, oiled and returned to the rack at Stembridge with a rental tag still wired to the sling swivel. The studio insists it was only ever fired at extras, and only with blanks.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of Agility
items.desc: One Strip bouncer swore by it: keep the feet moving and the muzzle down. He kept both, right up until the night a Flier came through a speakeasy skylight.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of Stamina
items.desc: Belonged to a night watchman at the Christie lot who held the paint-shop door for nine hours with it, then walked home for breakfast. Nobody has managed to make him tell it differently.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Rented for a rooftop chase picture in which the double leapt from the Taft Building onto a moving truck. He did it in one take, gun and all, and the director asked for another.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Marksman
items.desc: A Prohibition agent filed the front sight to his own taste and fired it in short, thrifty bursts of two rounds apiece. The Bureau never reimbursed him for the file.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a crate marked pianos, underneath four hundred pounds of actual pianos. The longshoreman who found it decided he had earned the commission.

items.name: Pressed Trash Can Lid
items.desc: Stamped from a single sheet on a Burbank press and sold door to door as the sanitary cover of tomorrow. Tomorrow turned out to involve spitter acid, which it also turns.

items.name: Trash Can Lid of Strength
items.desc: Lifted from an alley off Cahuenga by a teamster who used it to stop a Drone's charge, then the next one, then one more for good measure.

items.name: Trash Can Lid of Stamina
items.desc: Each dent is a story, and this lid holds enough of them to fill a Sunday supplement. Its owner walked home from Gower Gulch behind it, slowly but in one piece.

items.name: Trash Can Lid of the Boxer
items.desc: Somebody swiped it from the bins outside the Legion Stadium on a Friday night, still ringing from the crowd. It holds a guard the way a good welterweight does, chin down and patient.

items.name: Trash Can Lid of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks lashed to a fish truck, back when trucks still came up from anywhere. The longshoreman who carried it knew when to shove and when to sidestep.

items.name: Pressed Carbide Lamp
items.desc: Someone in a studio prop department buffed this to a camera-ready gleam for a mining picture that never left the stage. It has never seen a real mine and would prefer to keep it that way.

items.name: Carbide Lamp of Intellect
items.desc: Its last owner read blueprints by this flame during the blackouts on the Paramount lot and could recite the wiring for a whole sound stage from memory. The light holds steady enough for fine print.

items.name: Carbide Lamp of Spirit
items.desc: Carried by a Krotona night watchman who walked the Beachwood terraces each evening and claimed the hiss of the flame kept his thoughts unhurried. He slept soundly, which in 1930 counts as a talent.

items.name: Carbide Lamp of the Engineer
items.desc: Scratched into the base is a tally of every Mulholland Dam valve its owner checked after the invaders came through. The count stops at forty-one. The lamp kept going without him.

items.name: Carbide Lamp of the Doctor
items.desc: Clipped beside the burner is a dental mirror, left by an aid-station doctor who stitched by acetylene whenever the city power failed. He said the light was honest, if not flattering.

items.name: Carbide Lamp of the Deacon
items.desc: Smells of hymnals and wet carbide. A deacon carried it ahead of the Thursday prayer walk to Angelus Temple, and the faithful followed the garlic reek of acetylene as much as the glow.

items.name: Pressed Medical Bag
items.desc: Its leather was steamed and pressed over a form until the sides stand square and proud. Wardrobe departments notice these things.

items.name: Medical Bag of Intellect
items.desc: Inside the lid, a pencilled dosage table in a careful hand, corrected twice. Its owner trusted arithmetic over bedside manner, and lost fewer patients for it.

items.name: Medical Bag of Spirit
items.desc: The nurse who owned it hummed while she worked and slept soundly afterwards, which on a hive-surge night counts as a medical marvel.

items.name: Medical Bag of the Engineer
items.desc: Converted by a studio electrician who reckoned splints and fuses wanted the same tidy compartments. Gauze sits beside spare wire, and nobody has yet confused the two.

items.name: Medical Bag of the Doctor
items.desc: Bought secondhand from a Highland Avenue physician who left town just before the Dome came down. His prescription pad is still in the side pocket, half used and wholly illegible.

items.name: Medical Bag of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried door to door in Echo Park by a Temple volunteer who handed out soup, iodine and Scripture in equal measure. The leather smells faintly of hymnals.

items.name: Pressed Pocket Testament
items.desc: Clamped overnight in a bookbinder's press until the covers lie as flat as a Production Code memo. Not a page out of place.

items.name: Pocket Testament of Intellect
items.desc: Margins crowded with cross-references in three colours of ink. Its former owner could argue Leviticus with a Red Squad sergeant and win on points.

items.name: Pocket Testament of Spirit
items.desc: Opened so often to the Psalms that it now falls there on its own. It sits easier in the hand than most things under the Dome.

items.name: Pocket Testament of the Engineer
items.desc: Found in the coat of a Lockheed riveter, with a slip of blueprint paper marking Nehemiah, the book about rebuilding walls.

items.name: Pocket Testament of the Doctor
items.desc: Belonged to a mission doctor home from China, who kept a pressed poppy in Luke because Luke was a physician too.

items.name: Pocket Testament of the Deacon
items.desc: Handed out at the Angelus Temple doors by the thousand, this one walked from Echo Park and back every Sunday. Its owner wore out three pairs of shoes before the binding showed a scratch.

items.name: Tailored Stetson Fedora
items.desc: Blocked to its owner's head by a Vine Street hatter who charged extra for listening to him talk. The owner is gone; the shape of his opinions remains.

items.name: Stetson Fedora of Intellect
items.desc: Lifted from a script reader's desk at Universal, where it sat atop a pile of rejected scenarios. A man who read four hundred plots a year learns to spot an ambush before the second act.

items.name: Stetson Fedora of Spirit
items.desc: Its last owner wore it to every service at Hollywood Cemetery, and lately that has been most days. The felt keeps a patient sort of calm that a new head can borrow.

items.name: Stetson Fedora of Stamina
items.desc: Rode the open back of a red car through the Cahuenga Pass during a dust storm, a broodling swarm and one marriage proposal. The crown never dented once.

items.name: Stetson Fedora of the Engineer
items.desc: Smells faintly of solder and machine oil from a studio electrical department, where a gaffer kept spare fuses tucked behind the band and his temper under the brim.

items.name: Stetson Fedora of the Doctor
items.desc: A house physician at the Roosevelt Hotel wore this on night calls, brim pulled low so guests could not read his face before he had read theirs.

items.name: Stetson Fedora of the Deacon
items.desc: Walked to Angelus Temple and back every Sunday for six years, gathering hymnal dust in the band and Echo Park rain on the brim. Sister Aimee once admired it, and its owner never let anyone forget.

items.name: Tailored Stetson Boss of the Plains
items.desc: Made to measure for a picture cowboy whose head, wardrobe noted, grew a size after each premiere.

items.name: Stetson Boss of the Plains of Agility
items.desc: Tom Mix's stable boys say a good hat stays on through a fall from the saddle. This one stayed on through three, and its rider walked away from all of them.

items.name: Stetson Boss of the Plains of Stamina
items.desc: Twenty summers of Valley sun bleached the crown and never once got through it. The man underneath outlasted two horses, a wife and a bank.

items.name: Stetson Boss of the Plains of Spirit
items.desc: Sweatband smells faintly of pipe smoke and pine. Its last owner sat out evenings on the Krotona steps in Beachwood Canyon and claimed the hills told him things.

items.name: Stetson Boss of the Plains of the Acrobat
items.desc: Caught in mid-air by its owner during a running mount at a Gower Gulch rodeo. The crowd cheered; the assistant director docked him a day for showing off.

items.name: Stetson Boss of the Plains of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off a cattle boat at San Pedro, by way of a longshoreman who won it at cards and wore it hauling bales just to annoy the foreman.

items.name: Stetson Boss of the Plains of the Deacon
items.desc: Doffed so often at church doors between Edendale and Angelus Temple that one side of the brim has gone soft. A folded hymn sheet still rides behind the band.

items.name: Tailored Football Helmet
items.desc: Commissioned for a studio football picture whose star refused to muss his hair, so the lining is quilted satin. The picture was shelved; the helmet was not.

items.name: Football Helmet of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a halfback who could find a gap in any line on Bovard Field, and once, on the Pass road, in a ring of Drones.

items.name: Football Helmet of Strength
items.desc: Nobody at Post 43 has managed to dent it with a fist. A Brute managed it once, and the lineman inside got up anyway, which is the whole point of linemen.

items.name: Football Helmet of Stamina
items.desc: Sixty minutes a Saturday, no substitutions, and the scuffs to prove every one of them. Its owner played both ways and complained about neither.

items.name: Football Helmet of the Boxer
items.desc: Fight night at the Legion Stadium drags between bouts, so a heavyweight took to wearing it for the walk to the ring. The promoter said it lacked dignity. The crowd disagreed.

items.name: Football Helmet of the Marksman
items.desc: Cut away at the right ear so a rifle stock would sit flush against the cheek. Its owner hit what he aimed at and saw no reason to hear the shot as well.

items.name: Football Helmet of the Acrobat
items.desc: Rolled down three flights of Hollywood Bowl seating with its owner still inside, both arriving at the bottom in good order. The usher was less composed.

items.name: Football Helmet of the Engineer
items.desc: Fitted with a cut-down lamp bracket by a studio electrician who wanted his hands free and his skull intact. The wiring runs down the back like a pigtail.

items.name: Tailored Riveted Steel Helmet
items.desc: Fitted at Universal for a war picture that will now never wrap, with a chamois liner sized to one actor's head. The actor is missing. His head, according to the studio, was generous.

items.name: Riveted Steel Helmet of Strength
items.desc: Stamped out on a Universal backlot press and worn by a grip who carried arc lamps up ladders two at a time. The dent on the crown came from a Drone. The Drone came off worse.

items.name: Riveted Steel Helmet of Stamina
items.desc: Taken off a Post 43 sentry who stood the Pass road three nights running without relief. He credits the helmet with half the work and wants it back by Armistice Day.

items.name: Riveted Steel Helmet of the Boxer
items.desc: Legion Stadium kept a crate of these by the ring for nights when the crowd's opinion of a decision turned physical. Still smells of cigar and liniment.

items.name: Riveted Steel Helmet of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off a San Pedro longshoreman who rode the last red car north before the Dome came down. He swapped it for a pint of Cornero's best and called it a fair trade.

items.name: Tailored Hart Schaffner & Marx Suit Coat
items.desc: Let out at the shoulders by a Universal wardrobe girl for a leading man who never came back from the backlot. It still hangs as if waiting for applause.

items.name: Hart Schaffner & Marx Suit Coat of Intellect
items.desc: The inside pocket held a fountain pen and a studio contract annotated in three inks. Its owner read every clause twice, which is how he noticed the studio had quietly stopped hiring people.

items.name: Hart Schaffner & Marx Suit Coat of Spirit
items.desc: Smells faintly of orange blossom and pipe tobacco. Somebody wore it to sit on a Studio City porch every evening, invasion or no invasion, and slept soundly afterward.

items.name: Hart Schaffner & Marx Suit Coat of Stamina
items.desc: Worn by a stunt double through three falls, two fires and one Hardened Drone on the Pass road. The lining was replaced twice. The man inside it, never.

items.name: Hart Schaffner & Marx Suit Coat of the Engineer
items.desc: Solder burns on the left cuff and a slide rule's ghost worn into the breast pocket. The sound man who owned it lived on coffee and would not take it off, even down in the cable vaults.

items.name: Hart Schaffner & Marx Suit Coat of the Doctor
items.desc: Taken off a hook after a house call in Toluca Lake, iodine on the sleeve and a stethoscope still curled in the side pocket. The doctor charged two dollars a visit and has not been seen since the hive reached the Valley.

items.name: Hart Schaffner & Marx Suit Coat of the Deacon
items.desc: Sunday best for a deacon who walked to Angelus Temple from the Pass each week rather than pay the fare. Hymnal dust lives in the pockets, along with a collection envelope, still sealed.

items.name: Tailored Horsehide Jacket
items.desc: Made to measure for a Universal contract player who wanted to look rugged in the commissary. He was taken from the backlot the week after his final fitting.

items.name: Horsehide Jacket of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch rider who could slide out of the saddle and under a corral fence before the director called cut. The elbows are worn to suede.

items.name: Horsehide Jacket of Stamina
items.desc: Two winters on a Cahuenga Pass road crew and one determined Spitter have not managed to finish it off. The acid scars across the back look like a map of Ventura County.

items.name: Horsehide Jacket of Spirit
items.desc: Found folded on a pew in a Beachwood Canyon chapel, with a pressed poppy in the breast pocket. Nobody came back for it, and nobody has had the heart to ask why.

items.name: Horsehide Jacket of the Acrobat
items.desc: High falls for Pickford-Fairbanks paid thirty dollars a jump, and this jacket went off the roof with its owner eleven times. The studio paid for the man's shoulder, though not the jacket's.

items.name: Horsehide Jacket of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up the coast from the San Pedro docks on the back of a man who carried a sack in each hand and never asked what was in them. It still smells of creosote and salt.

items.name: Horsehide Jacket of the Deacon
items.desc: Sister McPherson's ushers wore these on night patrols around Echo Park, and a hymnal fits the inside pocket exactly. A note in the lining asks the finder to return it to Angelus Temple, care of anyone.

items.name: Tailored Quilted Vest
items.desc: Wardrobe at Universal cut this for a Foreign Legion picture that never got made, so it fits beautifully and looks faintly Moroccan.

items.name: Quilted Vest of Agility
items.desc: A Hollywood Bowl usher wore this running between seats in the dark. The padding still holds the shape of someone who never once bumped a knee.

items.name: Quilted Vest of Strength
items.desc: Quilted by a grip's wife from a studio moving blanket, which explains why it takes a lamp stand to the chest without complaint. The grip never did say where the blanket went.

items.name: Quilted Vest of Stamina
items.desc: Every stitch is doubled, and the padding is cotton batting, horsehair and what appears to be a Saturday Evening Post. Post 43 men swear by it, and occasionally at it.

items.name: Quilted Vest of the Boxer
items.desc: Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, a cut man called Dutch wore this ringside, and the stains down the front are mostly not his. He claimed it brought luck to whoever was paying him.

items.name: Quilted Vest of the Marksman
items.desc: Its owner practised on the Stembridge range on Marathon Street and stitched a pad into the right shoulder where a Springfield's butt sits. The left side is untouched; he never once switched.

items.name: Quilted Vest of the Acrobat
items.desc: Light enough to tumble in and padded enough to land in, it belonged to a trapeze man stranded when the Dome came down over his tour. He still asks after it at the Roosevelt bar, which officially serves only coffee.

items.name: Quilted Vest of the Engineer
items.desc: Lockheed riveters wore these on the plant floor, with lining pockets for a slide rule and a pencil stub. One pocket here holds a sketch of an invader wing, carefully dimensioned.

items.name: Tailored Plate-insert Trench Coat
items.desc: Cut at Universal for a Western Front picture, then refused by the leading man because the plates added ten pounds on camera. It fits like a contract with no loopholes.

items.name: Plate-insert Trench Coat of Strength
items.desc: Took two men to carry up Cahuenga Pass and one Legion sergeant to wear. He claimed the weight kept him from blowing away in a Santa Ana, and nobody argued with him.

items.name: Plate-insert Trench Coat of Stamina
items.desc: Its last owner walked off a Warner Bros. stage with three spitter burns in the gabardine and none in himself. The plates are pitted now. The man, reportedly, is fine.

items.name: Plate-insert Trench Coat of the Boxer
items.desc: Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, a heavyweight wore this from the dressing room to the ring. He swore the plates did more for his chin than his trainer ever had, and he paid the plates less.

items.name: Plate-insert Trench Coat of the Stevedore
items.desc: The previous owner unloaded freighters at San Pedro and, on certain moonless nights, crates marked as sardines. Neither cargo ever got the better of him.

items.name: Tailored Pleated Flannel Trousers
items.desc: Fitted three times for a supporting player who wanted his legs to look longer in a medium shot. The hive took him for its next picture and left the trousers behind.

items.name: Pleated Flannel Trousers of Intellect
items.desc: Scenario writers at Warner Bros. wore the knees out of pairs like these, kneeling to retrieve rejected pages from under the desk. The pocket still holds a pencil stub and three unfinished endings.

items.name: Pleated Flannel Trousers of Spirit
items.desc: Kept for Sundays and pressed every Saturday night by an Edendale widow who held that a clean crease was a modest form of prayer.

items.name: Pleated Flannel Trousers of Stamina
items.desc: Double-stitched through the seat by a Melrose tailor who had seen what a long night on a barricade does to flannel. He charged extra, and nobody argued.

items.name: Pleated Flannel Trousers of the Engineer
items.desc: An RKO sound man wore these up and down the catwalks, which explains the scorch on one cuff and the fuse wire threaded through the belt loops.

items.name: Pleated Flannel Trousers of the Doctor
items.desc: Midnight calls at the Hollywood Hotel were made in these, by a house physician famous for discretion. The iodine on the left knee has never told a soul.

items.name: Pleated Flannel Trousers of the Deacon
items.desc: Walked to Angelus Temple and back every Sunday for years. The hems are pale with Glendale Boulevard dust, and the back pocket still smells faintly of hymnals.

items.name: Tailored Riding Breeches
items.desc: Cut to a director's own pattern, flared at the thigh for authority and tapered at the calf for the photographers. He never rode in them. The horse was billed below him anyway.

items.name: Riding Breeches of Agility
items.desc: Cowboy extras on Gower vaulted corral rails in these for a dollar a day and a box lunch. The good ones cleared the rail without spilling the lunch.

items.name: Riding Breeches of Stamina
items.desc: Stable hands at the Gower Gulch barns ride twelve hours in breeches like these, then walk the last mile when the horse gives out. The seat is triple-lined for a reason.

items.name: Riding Breeches of Spirit
items.desc: Quiet miles on the Griffith Park bridle trails, back when the worst thing in the brush was a rattler. Some of that calm stayed in the cloth.

items.name: Riding Breeches of the Acrobat
items.desc: Hung upside down from a galloping horse for a Universal serial. The stitching held, and the stuntman got a screen credit nobody stayed in their seat to read.

items.name: Riding Breeches of the Stevedore
items.desc: Somebody's cousin brought these up from San Pedro after the dock work dried up. Whipcord takes a cargo hook better than a horse takes a stranger.

items.name: Riding Breeches of the Deacon
items.desc: Circuit preachers rode the Valley in these before the red cars came. This pair arrived at Angelus Temple in a donation barrel with a gospel tract still folded in the pocket.

items.name: Tailored Canvas Work Trousers
items.desc: Fitted at the waist by a Boulevard tailor who normally cut tuxedos and wished it known. He charged tuxedo prices, too.

items.name: Canvas Work Trousers of Agility
items.desc: Rolled at the cuff and soft at the seat from years on the catwalks above the Warner stages, where a rigger learns to move quickly or learns to fall.

items.name: Canvas Work Trousers of Strength
items.desc: Property of a Universal set carpenter who carried flats two at a time because the foreman was timing him. The back pockets are torn where the hammers lived.

items.name: Canvas Work Trousers of Stamina
items.desc: Twelve-hour shifts at the Mulholland Dam pumps wore the shine off these and none of the seams. The previous owner came home every night, which up there counts as a recommendation.

items.name: Canvas Work Trousers of the Boxer
items.desc: A stagehand fought four rounds at the Legion Stadium as Kid Gower and wore these to the bout and home again. He lost the fight and kept the trousers.

items.name: Canvas Work Trousers of the Marksman
items.desc: Knees worn flat from lying prone on the Hollywoodland ridges, where a patient rifleman could drop a Spitter long before it found its range.

items.name: Canvas Work Trousers of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen on the Pickford-Fairbanks lot swore by canvas that gives at the crotch instead of tearing. These were tested off a balcony, a rooftop and once, by accident, a moving red car.

items.name: Canvas Work Trousers of the Engineer
items.desc: Every pocket holds a different gauge of wire, and one holds a slide rule. They belonged to a Universal electrician who rewired a generator by lamplight the night the hive took the backlot.

items.name: Tailored Plate-insert Trousers
items.desc: Made in the Universal costume shop for a war picture and pressed into actual service. The plates are real steel; the gold regimental piping is pure studio invention.

items.name: Plate-insert Trousers of Strength
items.desc: Worn by a Post 43 man who swung a trench shovel in the Argonne and swung it again at Cahuenga Pass, leaving the plates to worry about what swung back.

items.name: Plate-insert Trousers of Stamina
items.desc: Dents in both thigh plates, each hammered roughly flat again with a pistol butt. The owner walked out of the Hollywoodland hills on his own feet, which is the whole review.

items.name: Plate-insert Trousers of the Boxer
items.desc: Legion boxers trained in these for the stadium on El Centro, on the theory that a man who can dance in steel can dance in anything. Most danced like a filing cabinet.

items.name: Plate-insert Trousers of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks with a longshoreman who came to Hollywood for picture work and got the Dome instead. The plates were cut from a hatch cover and still smell of salt and tar.

items.name: Tailored Florsheim Oxfords
items.desc: Made to the measure of a studio executive who insisted his feet were a size smaller than the evidence suggested. The cobbler compromised, and the left shoe still pinches about it.

items.name: Florsheim Oxfords of Intellect
items.desc: A script reader at the Pickford-Fairbanks studio wore these to the story department every morning. He claimed he did his best thinking with his feet up on the desk, and his producer never once caught him at it.

items.name: Florsheim Oxfords of Spirit
items.desc: Their last owner walked from Los Feliz to the Greek Theatre most nights the autumn it opened, just to sit in the empty seats after the crowds left. He said the quiet did him more good than the program.

items.name: Florsheim Oxfords of Stamina
items.desc: Double-stitched welts and a heel that outlasted three night shifts on the Hollywoodland barricades. The man on the fourth shift fared worse, but the shoes came back.

items.name: Florsheim Oxfords of the Engineer
items.desc: Rubber-heeled, so a man can stand near live cables on a stage floor without praying about it. Recovered from the electrical department at Chaplin Studios, along with a lingering smell of hot carbon.

items.name: Florsheim Oxfords of the Doctor
items.desc: Soft-soled for ward rounds and faintly spattered with iodine at the left toe. The aid station on Sunset swears it sterilised them, and nobody has asked how.

items.name: Florsheim Oxfords of the Deacon
items.desc: Scuffed at the toes from kneeling and smelling of hymnal paper, these made the long walk to Angelus Temple every Sunday until the Echo Park road turned dangerous. Now they make it on someone else's feet.

items.name: Tailored Riding Boots
items.desc: Cut for a director who wore jodhpurs on set and had never sat a horse, on the theory that it frightened the actors. It did.

items.name: Riding Boots of Agility
items.desc: One trick rider in Tom Mix's outfit broke these in leaping between galloping horses. The boots survived the stunt; the rider's collarbone is still filing a grievance.

items.name: Riding Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Thick calfskin and a heel built for a full day in the stirrups, chasing strays up Beachwood Canyon. The strays these days include things with six legs.

items.name: Riding Boots of Spirit
items.desc: Night rides along the Griffith Park trails put the creases in this pair. Their owner said the hills settled him better than any sermon, which got him asked to leave two churches.

items.name: Riding Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: Bootheels reinforced after a fall from the second-storey balcony on the Christie lot, taken on purpose for twelve dollars and a close-up that ended up on the cutting-room floor.

items.name: Riding Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: San Pedro dockhands do not ride, but one bought these after a cargo hook tore through his work shoes. He came inland for picture work in '29 and stayed for the fighting.

items.name: Riding Boots of the Deacon
items.desc: Mud from Echo Park still clings to the heels, gathered on the walk to Sunday service. A folded tract sits in the left boot, worn soft from being read standing up.

items.name: Tailored Lineman's Boots
items.desc: Cut to measure by a wardrobe man for an actor playing a lineman. The actor never climbed anything, but the boots can.

items.name: Lineman's Boots of Agility
items.desc: Pacific Telephone linemen could go up a forty-foot pole in under a minute. The man who wore these did it with a Spitter at the bottom and still reached the crossarm first.

items.name: Lineman's Boots of Strength
items.desc: Hauling cable reels up Vermont Canyon was a two-man job until the fellow in these started doing it alone. His foreman put in for a raise on his behalf, which tells you what kind of year it was.

items.name: Lineman's Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Eleven straight days restringing wire along the red-car route, sleeping in the work truck, and the soles never split. The owner gave out first; the boots went to the next man on the crew.

items.name: Lineman's Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: On Friday nights the owner came straight off shift to sit ringside at the Legion Stadium, spurs and all. He swore he went three rounds with a heckler once and never untied them.

items.name: Lineman's Boots of the Marksman
items.desc: A lineman learns to judge distance by eye, wire to wire. This one carried a Winchester up the poles as well and settled matters with drones from the crossarm.

items.name: Lineman's Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen at the Christie lot borrowed these for a rooftop chase and returned them only under protest. One fell off a two-storey set wearing them and walked away, which the studio logged as a rehearsal.

items.name: Lineman's Boots of the Engineer
items.desc: Owned by a union electrician who sketched wiring diagrams inside the shaft in carpenter's pencil. Half of them make sense. The other half describe something the hive left humming on Western Avenue.

items.name: Tailored Trench Boots
items.desc: Colonel's property, refitted by a Wilshire bootmaker, steel plates and all, so they would not spoil the line of his jodhpurs.

items.name: Trench Boots of Strength
items.desc: Kicked in the doors of three hive-choked bungalows on Selma Avenue. The steel toes are dented. The doors fared worse.

items.name: Trench Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Marched in by a sergeant who walked from Saint-Mihiel to the Rhine in a pair just like them. Now he patrols the Cahuenga Pass road twice a night and claims it feels shorter.

items.name: Trench Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Post 43 built its stadium on fight money, and a doorman wore these working the Friday crowd for years. He maintains he never threw a punch, only a shoulder.

items.name: Trench Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from San Pedro on a fruit truck, salt-stained to the ankle, with a cargo hook's scar across one toecap. They still smell faintly of oranges and bilge.

items.name: Tailored Kid Gloves
items.desc: Cut to the measure of a director's hands, so he could point at things with real authority.

items.name: Kid Gloves of Intellect
items.desc: Script girls at Paramount wore pairs like these to turn pages without smudging the continuity notes. This one could recite every scene of the picture the hive has been reshooting since summer.

items.name: Kid Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Folded on a pew at Blessed Sacrament the morning the Dome came down. Nobody has claimed them, and the sexton swears whoever wears them sleeps the night through.

items.name: Kid Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Double-stitched at every seam by a wardrobe mistress who had watched too many leading men split a pair in one take. They have outlasted three leading men since.

items.name: Kid Gloves of the Engineer
items.desc: Sound men at Warner's wore these while splicing cable through sixteen-hour days. The fingertips are scorched, the cuffs are spotless, and the last owner kept all ten fingers.

items.name: Kid Gloves of the Doctor
items.desc: Carried in the coat pocket of a surgeon at Hollywood Receiving Hospital who liked to take a pulse in gloves. A faint smell of iodine has never washed out.

items.name: Kid Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: Ushers at Angelus Temple wore pairs like these for the Sunday crowds, five thousand hands to shake before the sermon. They still smell of hymnals and floor wax.

items.name: Tailored Riding Gauntlets
items.desc: Measured for a cowboy star who never touched a horse off camera. His stunt double wore them instead, and got no credit for that either.

items.name: Riding Gauntlets of Agility
items.desc: A trick rider swung under a galloping horse in these for a Tom Mix picture and came up with his hat still on. The palms are worn to a shine.

items.name: Riding Gauntlets of Stamina
items.desc: Saddle-sore and stubborn, like the wrangler who wore them through a nine-day location shoot in the Mojave. The leather has long since stopped complaining.

items.name: Riding Gauntlets of Spirit
items.desc: Someone stitched a tiny cross inside the left cuff. The wrangler who owned them said a prayer over every horse before a fall and never lost one.

items.name: Riding Gauntlets of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen call these lucky. Their owner jumped from a Poverty Row rooftop onto a moving horse forty times for one shot, and the director used the first take.

items.name: Riding Gauntlets of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks on a longshoreman who traded hay hooks for horses when the picture work paid better. Still smells of tar and hemp.

items.name: Riding Gauntlets of the Deacon
items.desc: Rode to Echo Park every Sunday on a deacon's hands, reins in one and a hymnal in the other. The horse knew the way to the Temple better than he did.

items.name: Tailored Lineman's Gloves
items.desc: Cut to measure for a Universal electrical foreman who held that a man should look respectable even forty feet up. The fit is snug; the bill was not.

items.name: Lineman's Gloves of Agility
items.desc: A Pacific Electric trouble-shooter wore these along the overhead wire above the Pass. He could get down a pole faster than most men fall off one.

items.name: Lineman's Gloves of Strength
items.desc: Hauled copper up the Hollywoodland slopes by hand, a full reel at a time. The palm leather is cracked white, and the wrist strap has been let out two notches.

items.name: Lineman's Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: The fellow who owned these spent nine hours up a pole by Lake Hollywood during a hive surge, splicing the dam keeper's telephone line while Fliers circled. He came down hungry and in no mood for questions.

items.name: Lineman's Gloves of the Boxer
items.desc: Left on a bench at the Legion Stadium after a Friday card. One cuff smells of liniment, the other of cheap cigars, and somebody has sewn a horseshoe nail into the lining for luck.

items.name: Lineman's Gloves of the Marksman
items.desc: Judging a hundred-foot span by eye is a lineman's trade. Their last owner judged the range to a diving Flier just as well and kept a carbine strapped beside his climbing belt.

items.name: Lineman's Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: Borrowed by a stunt double who had to dangle from a telephone wire for a Universal two-reeler. The wire held, the double held, and the studio still billed the phone company for the pole.

items.name: Lineman's Gloves of the Engineer
items.desc: Rubber-lined at the fingertips by a studio electrician who knew exactly how much current a man can carry before the man becomes the circuit. He inked the figure inside the cuff and underlined it twice.

items.name: Tailored Plated Gauntlets
items.desc: Measured to the knuckle by a Warner Bros. wardrobe man who had previously fitted only knights for costume pictures. The steel is real. The fleur-de-lis on the cuff is pure vanity.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of Strength
items.desc: Riveted together in the Columbia machine shop from a boiler hatch and the lining of two catcher's mitts. The carpenter who made them swears he bent a crowbar back straight while wearing them.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of Stamina
items.desc: Built for a Legion sergeant who held the Pass road for two nights without relief. He gave them up only when the nurse at the aid station insisted, and even then he kept the left one.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of the Boxer
items.desc: A Friday-night regular at the Legion Stadium had these made after the referee barred him from wearing them into the ring. Rosin dust from the canvas still sits in the knuckle seams.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a longshoreman wore them hooking banana crates and the occasional case of Canadian whisky that somehow never made the manifest.

items.name: Tailored Silk Sash
items.desc: Sewn to measure for a leading man at Universal who insisted his waist was two inches less than it is. The tailor put in a hidden gusset and kept his opinion.

items.name: Silk Sash of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a scenario writer on the Pickford-Fairbanks lot who wore it to think. He claimed it kept the blood near his brain, and nobody in the story department could prove otherwise.

items.name: Silk Sash of Spirit
items.desc: Smells faintly of jasmine and incense from the Krotona buildings in Beachwood Canyon, where the old Theosophists held that a calm middle makes a calm soul. The invaders have not tested the theory.

items.name: Silk Sash of Stamina
items.desc: An extra wore this through fourteen hours of a harem scene at Universal and asked for overtime. He got a sandwich, and the sash.

items.name: Silk Sash of the Engineer
items.desc: Lifted from a dance director's costume trunk by a studio electrician who needed something to hang his circuit tester from. The silk has held up better than the dance director.

items.name: Silk Sash of the Doctor
items.desc: During the first week of the Dome, a nurse at the Highland aid station tied her bandage scissors to it and never untied them. The left end is still stiff with iodine.

items.name: Silk Sash of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday it walked in the choir procession at Angelus Temple, then all the way home to Edendale. The fringe has been mended with hymnal ribbon more than once.

items.name: Tailored Gun Belt
items.desc: Made to order on the Strip for a man who wanted his pistol to sit exactly where his jacket would hide it. His tailor and his gunsmith shared an invoice.

items.name: Gun Belt of Agility
items.desc: Its last owner could clear leather faster than the cameraman could crank, which is why none of his fight scenes cut together. The studio let him go for ruining takes.

items.name: Gun Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Took a stray round from a Dragna gunman on the Strip and kept its wearer upright long enough to reach a doctor. The bullet is still lodged in the third cartridge loop, where it belongs.

items.name: Gun Belt of Spirit
items.desc: A Temple usher wore his revolver on the right and a pocket Testament on the left, and never had to explain which came out first.

items.name: Gun Belt of the Acrobat
items.desc: Built for a stunt rider who rolled off horses at a gallop for five dollars a fall. The buckle sits flat so it never caught a stirrup, and the holster snaps shut against tumbling.

items.name: Gun Belt of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off the San Pedro docks around the waist of a longshoreman who unloaded crates of 'machine parts' for Tony Cornero and asked no questions. The holster fits a flask as well as a revolver.

items.name: Gun Belt of the Deacon
items.desc: Prayed over at Angelus Temple and loaded at the Legion clubhouse, in that order. Its owner walked Echo Park after dark handing out tracts and putting down whatever would not take one.

items.name: Tailored Tool Belt
items.desc: Cut to measure for a set dresser who wanted his hammer to hang at the exact angle of a gentleman's walking stick. He billed the studio for the fitting under props.

items.name: Tool Belt of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a rigger who worked the catwalks at Universal, forty feet up with nothing under him but a painted set. The loops sit flat, so nothing snags on the way down a rope.

items.name: Tool Belt of Strength
items.desc: Built to carry a sledge, two crowbars and a lunch pail without complaint. The carpenter who wore it on the Paramount lot could lift a flat by himself, and charged the union rate for two.

items.name: Tool Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Double-stitched along every seam by a wife who expected her husband home for supper. He kept coming home, through three studio fires and one invader on the Cahuenga Pass road.

items.name: Tool Belt of the Boxer
items.desc: A grip from Poverty Row wore it to the Legion Stadium every Friday night, and once into the ring by mistake. He went two rounds before anyone noticed, and won on points.

items.name: Tool Belt of the Marksman
items.desc: Stembridge armourers fitted a row of cartridge loops beside the screwdriver pocket. Its last owner kept a running count in pencil inside the strap and was never once off by a round.

items.name: Tool Belt of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen borrowed it off the Sennett crew for fall work, since a belt that stays shut through a forty-foot tumble is worth more than the man inside it, according to the accounts department.

items.name: Tool Belt of the Engineer
items.desc: Pockets for pliers, fuse wire, a slide rule and the spare lamp bulbs nobody else remembered. The electrician who owned it rewired half the Hollywood Bowl by flashlight and kept every receipt.

items.name: Tailored Cartridge Belt
items.desc: Cut to a wardrobe man's measurements for a picture about Pancho Villa, then requisitioned when the real shooting started. The stitching is still better than the script was.

items.name: Cartridge Belt of Strength
items.desc: Loaded, it weighs about as much as a sack of cement, which was the point. A Post 43 sergeant wore it on route marches up Highland Avenue to keep his legs honest and his recruits quiet.

items.name: Cartridge Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Its last owner held the Cahuenga Pass road for two days and three nights with this buckled on. He slept in it too, judging by the smell, and nobody had the heart to tell him.

items.name: Cartridge Belt of the Boxer
items.desc: Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, a heavyweight from Pasadena hung this on his corner post between rounds. He lost on points every time and liked to say it was the only belt he ever won.

items.name: Cartridge Belt of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a crate stencilled as machine parts, alongside a good deal of Canadian whisky that was not. The longshoreman who kept it could sling a hundredweight one-handed.

items.name: Tailored French Cuffs
items.desc: Cut to measure for a fellow who meant to be seen at the Brown Derby. The booth he reserved is still waiting for him.

items.name: French Cuffs of Intellect
items.desc: Taken from a Universal script reader who kept notes in pencil on the inside of each cuff. The notes are still there, and most of them say no.

items.name: French Cuffs of Spirit
items.desc: Laundered so often at a Cahuenga Avenue laundry that the linen has gone soft as an old prayer. Their last owner slept soundly every night, which under the Dome counts as a talent.

items.name: French Cuffs of Stamina
items.desc: Double-thickness linen, starched hard enough to turn a letter opener. A Hollywood Bowl stage manager wore them through three hive surges and one complete rehearsal of Aida.

items.name: French Cuffs of the Engineer
items.desc: Rolled up more often than worn down. Their owner kept the arc lamps burning on the Universal backlot and never once let a cuff near a live terminal, which is why there are still two of them.

items.name: French Cuffs of the Doctor
items.desc: A surgeon at the Hollywood Receiving Hospital buttoned these on before rounds and off before scrubbing. A faint smell of iodine survives every wash.

items.name: French Cuffs of the Deacon
items.desc: Sunday best for an usher at Angelus Temple, worn on the long walk up from the red-car stop. Sister Aimee is said to have admired the links once, in passing, between sermons.

items.name: Tailored Roping Cuffs
items.desc: Cut to measure for a Western star who never once threw a rope on camera. The saddlery on Gower charged extra for the silver conchos and extra again for keeping quiet about it.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of Agility
items.desc: Will Rogers could make a lariat spell a girl's name in midair. These belonged to the fellow who practised beside him at the Gower Gulch stables and got as far as the initials.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of Stamina
items.desc: Survived nine straight days of the same fall from the same horse for a Columbia serial. The horse quit before the cuffs did.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of Spirit
items.desc: Smells faintly of campfire smoke and saddle soap. The last owner sang to the cattle on night watch and claimed it calmed him more than it did them.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of the Acrobat
items.desc: A trick rider in Tom Mix's outfit wore these for every hang off a galloping horse. He retired the afternoon an invader flier took an interest in the horse.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of the Stevedore
items.desc: Brought up from San Pedro by a longshoreman who roped cargo nets before he roped steers for the pictures. The leather still carries a whiff of tar.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of the Deacon
items.desc: Folded inside the left cuff was a card from Angelus Temple bearing a verse about the lost sheep. The cowhand who owned them took it as professional advice.

items.name: Tailored Quilted Cuffs
items.desc: Cut to measure by a Universal wardrobe man who still pins a chalk mark on anything that holds still long enough.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a second-unit rider who could drop from a galloping horse onto a moving stagecoach, then ask whether the take was any good. It always was.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of Strength
items.desc: A grip on the Universal backlot wore these hauling a Model T out of a hive pit by its bumper. The bumper gave up first.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of Stamina
items.desc: Padding thick as a hotel mattress and roughly as clean. The last owner stood night watch at the Universal front gate for eleven straight shifts and never once sat down.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of the Boxer
items.desc: Stitched from the wrist wraps of a Legion Stadium middleweight who took up invader work because it paid better than Friday nights and the crowd was friendlier.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of the Marksman
items.desc: Tight at the wrist so nothing shakes the sights. Found folded beside a Springfield on a Universal water tower, with forty spent casings and not one of them wasted.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of the Acrobat
items.desc: Survived four falls from the Notre Dame façade on the Universal backlot. The director wanted a fifth, with more feeling.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of the Engineer
items.desc: Grease-stained along the seams and scorched at one edge where a studio generator argued back. A Stage 28 rigger swore by them, mostly while rewiring.

items.name: Tailored Chitin Bracers
items.desc: The first chitin to pass through a Hollywood tailor's hands. He measured twice, cut once, and sharpened his shears eleven times.

items.name: Chitin Bracers of Strength
items.desc: Hammered flat on a Universal machine-shop anvil from Hardened Soldier shell. The smith says it fought back until the third blow.

items.name: Chitin Bracers of Stamina
items.desc: Thick enough to stop a mandible and heavy enough to make the walk home a long one.

items.name: Chitin Bracers of the Boxer
items.desc: Taped over at the knuckle end in Legion corner fashion. A former sparring partner wears them on the Pass road, where opponents never wait for the bell.

items.name: Chitin Bracers of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shipped up from the San Pedro docks inside a crate of bananas, which explains the smell and possibly the tarantula.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Strength
items.desc: Pried off the neck of a red-car motorman who swore it had carried him through the Cahuenga Pass forty times. The forty-first trip carried him nowhere, but the medal held up fine.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Agility
items.desc: Saint Christopher carried a child across a river without slipping once. A Gower Gulch trick rider wore this one through three saddle falls and a runaway buckboard, and she claims the saint did most of the work.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Stamina
items.desc: Worn by a red-car conductor who walked the Hollywood line end to end the night the Dome came down, then turned round and walked it back. He never said what he was looking for.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Intellect
items.desc: The Krotona people up Beachwood Canyon insisted the saint was really an astral symbol of the higher planes. The Catholic who owned it let them talk and kept it on anyway.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of Spirit
items.desc: Twice blessed: once by a priest at Blessed Sacrament on Sunset, and once by a stagehand who had played a bishop in two reels for Universal. The owner trusted both blessings equally.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Boxer
items.desc: A welterweight kissed it before every Friday bout at the Legion Stadium and lost eleven of fourteen. He maintained the saint looked after travellers, not fighters, and that the referee was Presbyterian.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen at Gower Gulch pass these around like cigarettes. This one went off a two-storey saloon set, through a sugar-glass window and into a hay wagon, still on its chain.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from San Pedro on a longshoreman's neck, back when the studios paid better for lifting than the docks did. The salt never quite rubbed out of the links.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Marksman
items.desc: Its owner, a Legion sharpshooter, wore it tucked under his shirt so the glint would not give him away on the Beachwood ridge. He hit what he aimed at and was home by supper.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Engineer
items.desc: Hung for a year on a nail above the switchboard at Mulholland Dam, where the keeper said it watched the water better than the gauges did. He took it down the week the hive moved into the spillway.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Doctor
items.desc: Pinned inside the lid of an aid-station nurse's bag, beside the iodine and a list of names she meant to write to. It still smells faintly of carbolic.

items.name: St. Christopher Medal of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday its owner walked from Edendale to Angelus Temple with a hymnal under one arm, and the saint went with him both ways. Sister Aimee would have preferred a plain cross, but she never turned away a traveller.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Strength
items.desc: Its last owner bent horseshoes at the Elks picnic every Fourth of July and never once paid for his own beer. The other brothers called that a fair trade, and so did his knuckles.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Agility
items.desc: Brothers of the lodge swore it never left the owner's finger, though it left plenty of card tables in a hurry. Found in a hedge below Beachwood Canyon, still warm from somebody's pocket.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Stamina
items.desc: Fifty years' membership, says the engraving inside, and not a meeting missed. The old man outlived three Grand Exalted Somethings and, by the look of the scratches, most of an invader drone.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Intellect
items.desc: Someone at the Krotona colony traded it for a book on astral bodies, then regretted the bargain. The original wearer kept the lodge minutes in shorthand for nineteen years and could recite any of them.

items.name: Lodge Ring of Spirit
items.desc: Kept polished by the brother who read the eulogies. He read a great many this autumn, and still found the heart to hum on the walk home.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Boxer
items.desc: Swung at the Legion Stadium on Friday nights, third row, while its owner shouted advice nobody in the ring had asked for. The dent came from a seat back, not a jaw.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Acrobat
items.desc: A trapeze man from the Shrine circus wore this on a ribbon round his neck during performances, which the lodge considered disrespectful and the ringmaster considered sensible.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a longshoreman's pocket and went inland the week before the Dome came down. Tar still sits in the grooves of the crest, and no amount of soap will shift it.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Marksman
items.desc: Three years running, its owner won the Burbank lodge turkey shoot and gave every bird to the widows' fund. The brothers stopped entering out of pure embarrassment.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Engineer
items.desc: Recovered from a toolbox at Mulholland Dam, beside a slide rule and a ham sandwich of uncertain age. The dam keeper says its owner knew every valve in the place by its first name.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Doctor
items.desc: Under the hinged bezel sits a folded prescription for something the druggist would only fill with a wink. Prohibition made physicians very popular lodge members.

items.name: Lodge Ring of the Deacon
items.desc: Smells faintly of hymnals and shoe polish from Sunday walks to Angelus Temple. Its owner joined the lodge for the fellowship and the Temple for everything else, and saw no conflict.

items.name: Tailored Hunting Knife
items.desc: A wardrobe man at Universal fitted it with a sheath of matched calfskin and monogrammed nothing, out of tact. Elegant enough for a gentleman sportsman, sharp enough for what the hills hold now.

items.name: Hunting Knife of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch rider who could skin a jackrabbit at a gallop, or so he said in the stable bar. The edge is quicker than the story.

items.name: Hunting Knife of Stamina
items.desc: A deer camp in Vermont Canyon went three weeks on beans and this blade, and it still holds an edge. The owner held out a week longer, which is the part he tells.

items.name: Hunting Knife of the Acrobat
items.desc: Kept in the boot of a circus tumbler who came west for pictures and never left the ground again for less than union scale. Balanced well enough to throw, and twice it has been.

items.name: Hunting Knife of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner carried a Winchester for the shooting and this for everything after. The tally notches along the spine stop at forty, where he ran out of spine.

items.name: Hunting Knife of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off the San Pedro docks, where it opened crates, cut hawsers and settled one disagreement about overtime. Salt still lives in the hilt.

items.name: Tailored Brass Knuckles
items.desc: Measured to one particular hand at a Hollywood Boulevard jeweller's, each ring sized like a wedding band. The client paid in cash and asked for the receipt in his mother's name.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of Agility
items.desc: Light enough to leave a vest pocket before the other fellow finished his sentence. A Gower Gulch stunt double carried them through eleven pictures and never once got a credit.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of Stamina
items.desc: The previous owner was a night watchman on the Christie lot who backed three Drones down a stairwell and walked home afterward. He kept his hat on throughout.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of the Acrobat
items.desc: Belonged to a stuntwoman who made her living falling off Pacific Electric cars for two-reel comedies. She claimed the trick was landing angry.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of the Marksman
items.desc: Found in the overcoat of a Red Squad detective who hit what he aimed at, with or without a revolver. The inside of the rings is worn smooth from patient waiting.

items.name: Brass Knuckles of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where longshoremen settled wage disputes before the foreman finished his coffee. Still smells of tarred rope and somebody's spilled cargo.

items.name: Tailored Police Nightstick
items.desc: Turned on a lathe in the Universal prop shop for a picture about honest cops, which the front office filed under fantasy. The varnish is for the camera. The hickory underneath is not.

items.name: Police Nightstick of Strength
items.desc: Patrolman Ed Brophy swung it at the Cahuenga Pass roadblock until the grip wore smooth as a church pew. He claimed it never broke anything that did not deserve breaking, invader or otherwise.

items.name: Police Nightstick of Stamina
items.desc: Carried on the night beat along Ventura Boulevard, where a shift now runs twelve hours and ends whenever the drones do. The thong is knotted twice, by a man who did not intend to drop it.

items.name: Police Nightstick of the Boxer
items.desc: The Legion Stadium's ringside bailiff kept order with this on Friday nights. He never once used it on a fighter, only on gentlemen in row nine who disputed the decision.

items.name: Police Nightstick of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks in a harbour cop's kit bag, back when the worst thing on the waterfront was a longshoreman with opinions. Salt still whitens the grain near the lanyard.

items.name: Tailored Hatchet
items.desc: Bought out of a Boulevard hardware window, where it hung beside a placard about weekend cabins in Laurel Canyon. The cabins have not been heard from since. The hatchet holds an edge.

items.name: Hatchet of Intellect
items.desc: A Universal set carpenter pencilled his measurements on the handle and did his sums on the cheek of the blade. He built three cathedrals and a Transylvanian inn with it, all on schedule and none of them with backs.

items.name: Hatchet of Spirit
items.desc: Hung on a nail by a Beachwood Canyon woodstove and split kindling every morning for a widow who hummed while she worked. Whatever she hummed seems to have stayed in the handle.

items.name: Hatchet of the Engineer
items.desc: Studio electricians carry one to cut cable runs and break through flats when a set goes up in flames. This one has notches filed in the poll for stripping wire, a trick the union only teaches inside the hall.

items.name: Hatchet of the Doctor
items.desc: Taken from the aid station at the Pass summit, where it opened crates of gauze and, on one long night, cut a splint for a Legionnaire's leg. Carbolic soap has not quite washed out the memory of the work.

items.name: Hatchet of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday a Studio City deacon split firewood for the mission stove, then carried the hatchet into the service and laid it beside his hymnal. Nobody asked him to check it at the door.

items.name: Tailored M1913 Cavalry Sabre
items.desc: Somebody in Wardrobe had the scabbard relined in velvet to match a colonel's dress uniform. The colonel was an extra on six dollars a day. The velvet is real.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of Strength
items.desc: Lieutenant Patton designed the blade for thrusting at a gallop. Without the horse, the arm has to supply all the momentum, and this one was ground for arms that could.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of Stamina
