items.desc: A Post 43 machine-gunner had these made to carry a Browning up the Pass without stopping. He stopped once, to argue about the route.

items.name: Chitin Greaves of Stamina
items.desc: Elder Brute knockbacks dent the shell but seldom the man inside. The smith who forged them charges extra for that sentence alone.

items.name: Chitin Greaves of the Boxer
items.desc: Rumour at the Legion Stadium holds that a middleweight once wore these into the ring on a bet. He was disqualified for having knees harder than the other fellow's jaw.

items.name: Chitin Greaves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Hauled cargo at San Pedro for ten years, the owner said, and nothing down there ever bit back. He wore these on the river camp's loading line and said it less often.

items.name: Superior Patent Leather Pumps
items.desc: Wardrobe at First National stopped ordering these for the stars once they proved too sensible. The stand-ins kept them.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of Intellect
items.desc: Last worn by a script girl at First National who kept continuity on eleven pictures at once and never lost a cigarette between takes. The heels are scuffed from pacing.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of Spirit
items.desc: Somebody danced till dawn in these in the Roosevelt's Blossom Room the night before the Dome came down. They still carry the tune, if not the partner.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of Stamina
items.desc: Built for a chorus line that did four shows a day at the Pantages and never once sat down. The soles have walked the Boulevard more often than the red car.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of the Engineer
items.desc: Salvaged from a Lockheed draughtswoman's locker, along with a slide rule and a ham sandwich of uncertain age. The heels were filed square so they would not catch on catwalk grating.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of the Doctor
items.desc: An aid-station nurse in Burbank swears by them: quiet on linoleum, quick on stairs and easy to wipe clean. She did not say clean of what.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday for nine years these walked a widow from Edendale to Angelus Temple and back, rain or none. They smell faintly of hymnals and shoe polish, and they do not hurry.

items.name: Superior Cavalry Boots
items.desc: Made to measure for a Universal cavalry picture that was shelved after the horses unionised. That last part is a rumour put about by the wranglers.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of Agility
items.desc: Tom Mix's stable hands say the man who broke these in could mount from a standing start and dismount at a gallop. Nobody has asked the horse.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Thirty miles a day along the border in 1916, if the tag stitched inside is honest. The leather has gone hard as a fence post and about as tired.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of Spirit
items.desc: Kept on a closet shelf in Los Feliz by a retired major who polished them every evening and never rode again. There is something calming in the shine.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: One Gower Gulch extra did his own falls from the saddle in these for five dollars a day and a box lunch. He took the boots when the picture wrapped; the star took the credit.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off a San Pedro cargo foreman who wore riding boots for reasons he never explained and kicked crates about like they owed him money. The toes are flattened from it.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of the Deacon
items.desc: Mud from three counties and a dozen camp meetings is worked into the welts. The circuit preacher who owned them held that a horse is the only congregation that never leaves early.

items.name: Superior Logger Boots
items.desc: Every seam is triple-stitched and every caulk hand-filed. Timber crews felling Valley oaks for barricades will trade a week's rations for a pair, and the bootmaker knows it.

items.name: Logger Boots of Agility
items.desc: A set carpenter at First National wore these up and down scaffolding forty feet above the stage floor and never once grabbed a rail. The foreman docked him for it anyway, on principle.

items.name: Logger Boots of Strength
items.desc: Built for a man who carried railroad ties on each shoulder at the Studio City lumberyard and complained they were uneven. The heels are worn flat from leaning into heavy loads.

items.name: Logger Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Whoever owned these walked the Los Angeles River bed from Laurel Canyon to Burbank twice a day running messages. The soles have been replaced three times; the man, never.

items.name: Logger Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Stadium sweepers swear a heavyweight wore these into the ring at the Legion one Friday night, lost on points, and refused to take them off for the photograph. The left toe has a dent shaped like somebody's chin.

items.name: Logger Boots of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner kept watch from the Burbank water tower with a Springfield and a thermos of coffee. The tally notched into the heel counts Spitters, and it ran out of room.

items.name: Logger Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: Sennett's people say these went off a rooftop on Ventura Boulevard, through an awning and onto a moving truck in one take. The stuntman walked away limping; the boots walked away fine.

items.name: Logger Boots of the Engineer
items.desc: Lockheed riggers favoured this pattern because the steel toe survived a dropped propeller hub and a pocket sewn inside the shaft held a slide rule. Two pencils are still in there, both chewed.

items.name: Superior Chitin-shod Boots
items.desc: Bench-forged at the First National machine shop back when it made scenery instead of barricades. The chitin studs are matched by size, which the foreman called excessive before ordering a pair.

items.name: Chitin-shod Boots of Strength
items.desc: Rumour on the Burbank line says a Veteran kicked a Brute's knee out from under it wearing these. The Brute's opinion went unrecorded.

items.name: Chitin-shod Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Forty pounds the pair, and the Legion sergeant who issued them swore a man could march to the Dome wall and back in them. Several tried. The boots made it every time.

items.name: Chitin-shod Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Taped at the ankles like a fighter's wrists and smelling of liniment and Legion Stadium cigars. Fight-night regulars swear they never lost a round, mainly because they were never allowed in the ring.

items.name: Chitin-shod Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shipped up from San Pedro before the Dome came down, made for men who walked cargo nets and hauled crates marked machine parts that sloshed. The customs men never looked closely, and nobody looks now.

items.name: Superior Opera Gloves
items.desc: Cut from the bolt Paramount was saving for a premiere gala that will not happen now. The wardrobe department called this a crime against satin and put it in writing.

items.name: Opera Gloves of Intellect
items.desc: Left on a seat at the Pantages by a lady who did the crossword in ink between acts and never once looked at the stage. The index fingertip is still faintly blue.

items.name: Opera Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Since 1921 they have gone to every Easter sunrise service at the Hollywood Bowl and come home a shade calmer. They still smell of cold morning air and violets.

items.name: Opera Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Eleven retakes and one hive raid, in that order, on the Sennett lot. The chorus girl who wore them insists the retakes were worse.

items.name: Opera Gloves of the Engineer
items.desc: Fitted with a brass thimble in each fingertip by a Lockheed draughtswoman who liked to tap every rivet before she trusted it. She trusted very few.

items.name: Opera Gloves of the Doctor
items.desc: Their owner ran an aid station out of a Burbank supper club cloakroom and refused to take them off. Scrubbing in, she said, was for people with running water.

items.name: Opera Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday the red cars ran, a deaconess carried these tucked in her hymnal from Echo Park to Burbank and back. The pages left a faint gilt line along the left cuff.

items.name: Superior Everlast Bag Gloves
items.desc: Fresh from a crate the Legion stadium ordered before the Dome came down and never got round to opening. The leather squeaks and the laces are still white.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of Agility
items.desc: Light enough for a flyweight who never stood still long enough to be hit. His trainer swore the kid could slip a punch before the other fellow had finished thinking of it.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Twelve rounds a night against a gym sandbag, then forty against a Drone in a Burbank alley. By the owner's reckoning the sandbag put up the better fight.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Saturday sparring and Sunday sermons got the same pair from an Eagle Rock parson, who argued that turning the other cheek came easier with your guard up.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: Circus tumbler, then stuntman, then this. The previous owner came off the Sennett water tower knuckles-first more often than he cared to count, and the left glove is patched where the mattress wasn't.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a longshoreman wore them under his cargo hooks to keep the nets from chewing his palms. Weekends he boxed to cover the rent.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: Kept in the vestry of a Burbank Methodist church for the young men's boxing club. Somebody folded a hymn sheet into the right cuff, and it has stayed through every fight since.

items.name: Superior Welder's Gauntlets
items.desc: Lined in good chrome leather the studios once kept for star wardrobe. Wardrobe objected to the transfer in writing; the welders used the memo to light a torch.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of Agility
items.desc: Cut a size under regulation for a Burbank welder who liked working high on ladders and coming down from them in a hurry.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of Strength
items.desc: Their last owner straightened a bent red-car rail on Ventura Boulevard by himself, or so the river camp tells it. The story grows a foot every time the coffee runs out.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of Stamina
items.desc: Found on a bench in the First National machine shop, beside a thermos and a lunch pail nobody came back for.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of the Boxer
items.desc: A Legion Stadium heavyweight wore these welding bleacher brackets on Saturday mornings to pay for his Friday-night losses. The left one still throws a fair uppercut.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of the Marksman
items.desc: Sewn with a thin trigger finger for a Lockheed inspector who spent his breaks shooting tin cans off the United Airport fence. He rarely missed and never let anyone forget it.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of the Acrobat
items.desc: Borrowed from the Sennett prop shop by a stuntman who welded his own wire rigs and trusted nobody else's seams. He fell off three roofs in them and kept both hands.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of the Engineer
items.desc: Pencil sums are scorched into the cuff, where an airframe man worked out load figures between welds. Most of them check out; the one that does not has been circled twice.

items.name: Superior Plated Gauntlets
items.desc: The First National machine shop in Burbank turned these out between hive surges, using steel meant for camera cranes. The fit is excellent. The requisition paperwork is missing.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of Strength
items.desc: Riveted together in the Columbia machine shop from a boiler hatch and the lining of two catcher's mitts. The carpenter who made them swears he bent a crowbar back straight while wearing them.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of Stamina
items.desc: Built for a Legion sergeant who held the Pass road for two nights without relief. He gave them up only when the nurse at the aid station insisted, and even then he kept the left one.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of the Boxer
items.desc: A Friday-night regular at the Legion Stadium had these made after the referee barred him from wearing them into the ring. Rosin dust from the canvas still sits in the knuckle seams.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a longshoreman wore them hooking banana crates and the occasional case of Canadian whisky that somehow never made the manifest.

items.name: Superior Cummerbund
items.desc: Lined in heavy grosgrain by a tailor who refused to discuss the price in front of the client. The client found out anyway.

items.name: Cummerbund of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a Universal story editor who read four hundred scripts a year and bought six. He kept notes in the pleats; a pencil stub still rides in the top fold.

items.name: Cummerbund of Spirit
items.desc: Worn to the last dance in the Roosevelt's Blossom Room before the Dome came down. Its owner kept dancing afterward, after a fashion, and swears a good sash settles the nerves.

items.name: Cummerbund of Stamina
items.desc: Recovered from a Burbank banquet hall where the head waiter held the kitchen door against three Drones for most of an evening. He maintains the sash did half the work.

items.name: Cummerbund of the Engineer
items.desc: A Lockheed draughtsman wore it to the company dinner, then straight back to the drafting room when the sirens went. Grease-pencil figures on the lining work out stress loads for a wing nobody built.

items.name: Cummerbund of the Doctor
items.desc: Cut from the evening clothes of a Vine Street surgeon called away from the Brown Derby mid-soup. Iodine stains along the hem suggest he never did get back to the soup.

items.name: Cummerbund of the Deacon
items.desc: Sister Aimee's ushers wore something like it on Sunday nights. This one made the long walk from Echo Park to the Burbank line and still smells of hymnals and lamp oil.

items.name: Superior Sam Browne Belt
items.desc: Bridle leather from a Burbank saddlery, oiled weekly by a quartermaster who considered a dull buckle a moral failing. He would have made a fine censor.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of Agility
items.desc: Off a Lockheed test pilot who walked away from three crashes and a breach-of-promise suit. The shoulder strap is cut short so nothing snags on the way out of a cockpit.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Issued to an LAPD motorcycle sergeant who patrolled Ventura Boulevard eleven days without relief. The leather is cracked across the back where he slept sitting up.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of Spirit
items.desc: Through Burbank's worst week a Salvation Army captain wore this while pouring coffee from a tin urn for anyone who asked. The strap still smells of grounds and gun oil.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taken off a Sennett stunt double who could fall down a staircase and bill for it twice. The buckle is padded with felt, which tells you how many staircases there were.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from San Pedro on a longshoreman who worked the lumber schooners. He wore the cross-strap to carry a cargo hook and called it the only uniform he ever liked.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of the Deacon
items.desc: Hung with a Bible, this strap rode the red cars from Angelus Temple out to the Valley every Sunday. The leather at the hip is worn smooth where the book bumped against it, mile after mile.

items.name: Superior Lineman's Belt
items.desc: Pigskin-faced and quilted with good duck canvas, made for the Bureau's foremen, who seldom climbed but liked to look ready.

items.name: Lineman's Belt of Agility
items.desc: Climbing spurs came with it once, along with a Pacific Electric wireman who went up a pole faster than most men take the stairs. The spurs were lost in Burbank. He was not.

items.name: Lineman's Belt of Strength
items.desc: Its owner carried a forty-pound transformer up a ladder on a dare, then charged the foreman a dollar to bring it back down.

items.name: Lineman's Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Worn through a triple shift restringing the Valley lines the week the Dome came down. The padding kept its shape better than the man did.

items.name: Lineman's Belt of the Boxer
items.desc: Off duty, the owner fought four-rounders at the Legion Stadium on Friday nights. The belt hung on the dressing-room hook and smelled of liniment until Monday.

items.name: Lineman's Belt of the Marksman
items.desc: A Studio City lineman shot spitters off the crossarms with a .30-06 rather than wait for them to leave. His rifle sling clipped neatly to the left D-ring.

items.name: Lineman's Belt of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taken from a former circus rigger who switched to telephone work in 1927, citing the steadier pay and the gentler public.

items.name: Lineman's Belt of the Engineer
items.desc: Pockets cut for a folded wiring diagram, a pencil stub and a pocket voltmeter. The Lockheed electrician who owned it read every specification before arguing with it.

items.name: Superior Cartridge Belt
items.desc: A Burbank machinist turned out a dozen of these before the hangars went quiet. The loops hold a cartridge as snug as a seven-year studio contract.

items.name: Cartridge Belt of Strength
items.desc: Loaded, it weighs about as much as a sack of cement, which was the point. A Post 43 sergeant wore it on route marches up Highland Avenue to keep his legs honest and his recruits quiet.

items.name: Cartridge Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Its last owner held the Cahuenga Pass road for two days and three nights with this buckled on. He slept in it too, judging by the smell, and nobody had the heart to tell him.

items.name: Cartridge Belt of the Boxer
items.desc: Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, a heavyweight from Pasadena hung this on his corner post between rounds. He lost on points every time and liked to say it was the only belt he ever won.

items.name: Cartridge Belt of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a crate stencilled as machine parts, alongside a good deal of Canadian whisky that was not. The longshoreman who kept it could sling a hundredweight one-handed.

items.name: Superior Sleeve Garters
items.desc: Silk-faced, with German-silver clasps, the sort a Roosevelt Hotel cashier wore to look honest. Bought at a Burbank haberdasher's closing-out sale, the closing having been arranged by the hive.

items.name: Sleeve Garters of Intellect
items.desc: A bookkeeper on the First National lot in Burbank wore these through three audits and one invasion. He still balances the commissary ledger by candlelight and has yet to be off by a cent.

items.name: Sleeve Garters of Spirit
items.desc: Found folded neatly on a pew in a boarded-up Burbank chapel. Whoever left them never came back, and the ladies who sweep the aisle insist that is a sign of peace rather than the other thing.

items.name: Sleeve Garters of Stamina
items.desc: Speakeasy barmen on the Strip worked double shifts in garters like these, pouring what the law said did not exist. The elastic outlasted the barmen, the raids and most of the clientele.

items.name: Sleeve Garters of the Engineer
items.desc: Lockheed riveters used them to keep sleeves out of the drill press, and one foreman swore they steadied his slide-rule hand. The grease stains came standard.

items.name: Sleeve Garters of the Doctor
items.desc: Rolled sleeves are the first thing a surgeon learns. A Studio City doctor kept these on through a long night of acid burns at the river camp and asked only that they be laundered before being passed along.

items.name: Sleeve Garters of the Deacon
items.desc: Choir directors favour them for keeping cuffs off the hymnal. These made the long walk to Angelus Temple and back more Sundays than anyone counted, and still smell faintly of lilies and lamp oil.

items.name: Superior Roping Cuffs
items.desc: Made at the Gower Gulch saddlery from the best hide left under the Dome, which these days is not saying as much as it used to.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of Agility
items.desc: Will Rogers could make a lariat spell a girl's name in midair. These belonged to the fellow who practised beside him at the Gower Gulch stables and got as far as the initials.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of Stamina
items.desc: Survived nine straight days of the same fall from the same horse for a Columbia serial. The horse quit before the cuffs did.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of Spirit
items.desc: Smells faintly of campfire smoke and saddle soap. The last owner sang to the cattle on night watch and claimed it calmed him more than it did them.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of the Acrobat
items.desc: A trick rider in Tom Mix's outfit wore these for every hang off a galloping horse. He retired the afternoon an invader flier took an interest in the horse.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of the Stevedore
items.desc: Brought up from San Pedro by a longshoreman who roped cargo nets before he roped steers for the pictures. The leather still carries a whiff of tar.

items.name: Roping Cuffs of the Deacon
items.desc: Folded inside the left cuff was a card from Angelus Temple bearing a verse about the lost sheep. The cowhand who owned them took it as professional advice.

items.name: Superior Quilted Cuffs
items.desc: Burbank piecework from a Lockheed upholsterer, who used aeroplane-seat batting and charged accordingly.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a second-unit rider who could drop from a galloping horse onto a moving stagecoach, then ask whether the take was any good. It always was.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of Strength
items.desc: A grip on the Universal backlot wore these hauling a Model T out of a hive pit by its bumper. The bumper gave up first.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of Stamina
items.desc: Padding thick as a hotel mattress and roughly as clean. The last owner stood night watch at the Universal front gate for eleven straight shifts and never once sat down.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of the Boxer
items.desc: Stitched from the wrist wraps of a Legion Stadium middleweight who took up invader work because it paid better than Friday nights and the crowd was friendlier.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of the Marksman
items.desc: Tight at the wrist so nothing shakes the sights. Found folded beside a Springfield on a Universal water tower, with forty spent casings and not one of them wasted.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of the Acrobat
items.desc: Survived four falls from the Notre Dame façade on the Universal backlot. The director wanted a fifth, with more feeling.

items.name: Quilted Cuffs of the Engineer
items.desc: Grease-stained along the seams and scorched at one edge where a studio generator argued back. A Stage 28 rigger swore by them, mostly while rewiring.

items.name: Superior Chitin Bracers
items.desc: Elder shell, cured a month over a river-camp fire. Veterans trade cigarettes for these and do not haggle.

items.name: Chitin Bracers of Strength
items.desc: Hammered flat on a Universal machine-shop anvil from Hardened Soldier shell. The smith says it fought back until the third blow.

items.name: Chitin Bracers of Stamina
items.desc: Thick enough to stop a mandible and heavy enough to make the walk home a long one.

items.name: Chitin Bracers of the Boxer
items.desc: Taped over at the knuckle end in Legion corner fashion. A former sparring partner wears them on the Pass road, where opponents never wait for the bell.

items.name: Chitin Bracers of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shipped up from the San Pedro docks inside a crate of bananas, which explains the smell and possibly the tarantula.

items.name: Pearl Choker of Strength
items.desc: Restrung on piano wire by a Universal grip who said silk kept snapping. The clasp is a cargo shackle filed down to size, and it has never once come undone.

items.name: Pearl Choker of Agility
items.desc: Worn by a backlot dancer who could clear a hive drone's reach with a single high kick. She kept the pearls; the drone kept its distance.

items.name: Pearl Choker of Stamina
items.desc: Recovered from a wardrobe trunk that sat nine days under the rubble of a Universal dressing room. The actress who owned it walked out of the same rubble on the tenth, and she credits the pearls.

items.name: Pearl Choker of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a First National script girl who carried every continuity note in her head. The pearls are graded so evenly that a Burbank jeweller suspected her of counting them.

items.name: Pearl Choker of Spirit
items.desc: Somebody's grandmother prayed on these when the rosary went missing. Three pearls near the clasp are worn flat and stay warm long after the necklace comes off.

items.name: Pearl Choker of the Boxer
items.desc: Hocked to a Legion Stadium promoter by a heavyweight's wife the night before he went down in the fourth. She never redeemed it, and the promoter called it the best purse he paid all year.

items.name: Pearl Choker of the Acrobat
items.desc: Wire-work girls on the Sennett lot wore these for a circus picture, since a choker stays put upside down. One snapped mid-swing, and the pearls turned up in the sawdust for weeks.

items.name: Pearl Choker of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a crate marked machine parts, off one of Cornero's boats. The longshoreman who lifted it wore it home under his collar and never explained himself.

items.name: Pearl Choker of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner shot clay pigeons off the United Airport fence and never wasted a shell. Every pearl sits dead level, as if strung along a rifle sight.

items.name: Pearl Choker of the Engineer
items.desc: Each knot was tied by a Lockheed draughtsman with the patience he usually saved for wing ribs. The clasp is machined to a thousandth of an inch, which is more than the pearls ever asked for.

items.name: Pearl Choker of the Doctor
items.desc: Found in a nurse's apron pocket at the Burbank aid station, wrapped in gauze like a patient. She wore it on night shifts, when the ward was quiet enough to need reminding of dances.

items.name: Pearl Choker of the Deacon
items.desc: Given to the Angelus Temple collection plate by a Glendale widow, then quietly returned by a deacon who thought it deserved another long walk out of Echo Park. It smells faintly of hymnals and lavender.

items.name: Wedding Band of Strength
items.desc: Pried off a knuckle the size of a walnut, it belonged to a blacksmith on the Universal backlot who shod horses for Westerns. His widow traded it for a sack of flour and said he would have approved of the bargain.

items.name: Wedding Band of Agility
items.desc: Slipped off its owner's finger halfway up a Burbank water tower, which happens to a man who climbs faster than the hive can follow. He kept climbing. The ring kept falling.

items.name: Wedding Band of Stamina
items.desc: Forty-one years of marriage in Studio City, through the 1914 flood, the Depression and now the Dome. The inside is worn nearly through where the engraving used to be, and still it has not cracked.

items.name: Wedding Band of Intellect
items.desc: A Lockheed draughtsman designed this himself and had it cast to the thousandth of an inch. His bride complained it pinched. He produced the calculations.

items.name: Wedding Band of Spirit
items.desc: Found on the floor of the set chapel on Universal's European street, where a plaster church briefly became a real one. Nobody claimed it, and the extras who prayed there swear it sits warmer than it ought to.

items.name: Wedding Band of the Boxer
items.desc: The bride made him take it off before every bout at the Legion Stadium, and he made her hold it ringside. Twelve years of Friday nights, no knockouts, one marriage.

items.name: Wedding Band of the Acrobat
items.desc: Carnival people married under canvas in 1922, and this went up the trapeze rigging tied to a ribbon so the groom could hand it over mid-swing. It has been dropped since. Never by him.

items.name: Wedding Band of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came over the side at San Pedro in a bale of Philippine hemp, or so the longshoreman who wore it liked to say. He married the customs clerk who failed to ask questions.

items.name: Wedding Band of the Marksman
items.desc: Engraved inside with two dates eleven years apart: the wedding, and the night a Hardened Spitter took her husband off the Cahuenga Pass road. She has not missed a shot since.

items.name: Wedding Band of the Engineer
items.desc: Melted down from a brass generator fitting by a Stage 28 electrician who could not afford gold but could wire anything. The marriage held. So did the fitting.

items.name: Wedding Band of the Doctor
items.desc: Ward rules forbade jewellery, so the Burbank aid-station nurse wore it on a string under her cap. Spitter burns make for long nights, and she wanted it near.

items.name: Wedding Band of the Deacon
items.desc: Married at Angelus Temple in 1927 with Sister Aimee's blessing, the couple walked home to Studio City afterward out of piety and poverty in equal measure. The ring still smells faintly of hymnals and shoe leather.

items.name: Superior M1905 Bayonet
items.desc: Reground and blued twice over in the First National machine shop. The armourer took it to the river camp and did not come back. The knife did, carried in by somebody else.

items.name: M1905 Bayonet of Agility
items.desc: A Universal stunt double learned to flip it end over end between takes of All Quiet on the Western Front. The picture wrapped in the spring. He never quite stopped flipping it.

items.name: M1905 Bayonet of Stamina
items.desc: It went from the Argonne to a Legion locker on Highland, then back out when the Dome came down. Its owner claimed it had outlasted three sergeants and one marriage.

items.name: M1905 Bayonet of the Acrobat
items.desc: A knife-thrower from a stranded circus closed every show by pinning an apple on his sister's head. She switched to pears afterward, which sit lower.

items.name: M1905 Bayonet of the Marksman
items.desc: Its first owner fixed it to his Springfield and rarely needed it, being the sort who hit what he aimed at from three hundred yards. The grips are worn only where he cleaned it.

items.name: M1905 Bayonet of the Stevedore
items.desc: Before the Dome it rode up from San Pedro in a longshoreman's boot, where it cut cargo netting, hawser line and the occasional argument about overtime.

items.name: Superior Weighted Gloves
items.desc: Every ounce of lead weighed and signed off by a Lockheed inspector who should have been checking rivets. Balanced as neatly as a propeller, and about as friendly.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of Agility
items.desc: Light enough to throw a punch and be somewhere else when the answer comes back. Taken off a Dragna gunman in Studio City who reached for his pocket a half-second too late.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Built for a long night. The last owner held the Laurel Canyon crossing until dawn, then handed these over with a yawn and the advice to keep the left one higher.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: A Sennett tumbler wore these for pratfalls that ended in punches. The palms are scuffed from catching himself off rooftops, which the studio called comedy and the insurance man called something else.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of the Marksman
items.desc: The right trigger finger is cut away, so the owner could punch with one hand and shoot with the other. He kept score in pencil on the cuff and never once rounded up.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks with a longshoreman who settled wage disputes before the union got around to it. They still smell of tar, hemp and bananas.

items.name: Superior Louisville Slugger
items.desc: Seasoned ash, turned true and oiled by a sporting-goods clerk on the Boulevard who swore it was game-ready. The game has changed somewhat since.

items.name: Louisville Slugger of Strength
items.desc: Taken from a batboy's rack at Wrigley Field after the Hollywood Stars' last home game. It has since sent a Drone's head farther than any ball that season, though the scorekeepers declined to count it.

items.name: Louisville Slugger of Stamina
items.desc: Its owner caught for eleven seasons in the Pacific Coast League and claimed nothing could hurt him after that many foul tips. He still sleeps with it under the cot.

items.name: Louisville Slugger of the Boxer
items.desc: Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, a heavyweight from Pasadena carried this into the ring as a gimmick. The referee never let him use it. The invaders have no referee.

items.name: Louisville Slugger of the Stevedore
items.desc: Longshoremen played pepper with it on the San Pedro wharf at lunch, and the bat picked up the habit of swinging at anything thrown its way. Drones count.

items.name: Superior Lineman's Wrench
items.desc: Drop-forged and heavy for its size, the kind the Bureau of Power and Light issued to men who climbed poles in the rain.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of Intellect
items.desc: A Warner Bros. electrician scratched wiring diagrams into the handle from memory, the night before the lot fell. Nobody else has been able to make sense of them.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of Spirit
items.desc: Kept in a toolbox beside a pocket Testament by a lineman who said a man forty feet up a pole needs a calm heart more than a good grip.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of the Engineer
items.desc: Union men at the IATSE hall called it the long argument, because it settled most of them. It has tightened a junction box on Stage 28 and loosened a Drone's jaw the same afternoon.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of the Doctor
items.desc: Borrowed from a lineman to open a jammed oxygen valve at an aid station, it was never returned. The handle still smells faintly of iodine and carbolic.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried on the long walk to Angelus Temple every Sunday, where its owner kept the KFSG transmitter humming between hymns. Sister Aimee was said to approve of practical faith.

items.name: Superior M1913 Cavalry Sabre
items.desc: Forged in a Burbank machine shop that used to turn out aeroplane fittings, to tolerances the cavalry never asked for and the invaders never respect.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of Strength
items.desc: Lieutenant Patton designed the blade for thrusting at a gallop. Without the horse, the arm has to supply all the momentum, and this one was ground for arms that could.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of Stamina
items.desc: Carried on the long road from Fort Riley to a Universal western, then on every retake after. Its owner claimed the horse tired first and the director second.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of the Boxer
items.desc: Hung for years over the bar at the Legion Stadium, where the Friday crowd swore it was kept there to settle decisions the judges got wrong.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a freighter at San Pedro in a crate marked as plumbing. The longshoreman who kept it used it on cargo netting first and on invaders later.

items.name: Superior Sledgehammer
items.desc: Studio carpenters can strike a whole Western town with one of these between lunch and quitting time. Hickory handle, an honest steel head, no pretensions.

items.name: Sledgehammer of Strength
items.desc: Swung on a Pacific Electric track gang laying rail toward Burbank, it drove spikes in two blows where other men needed five. The foreman docked its owner for showing off.

items.name: Sledgehammer of Stamina
items.desc: Nobody at the old Mulholland Dam quarry remembers the owner's name, only that he worked double shifts and never once sat down.

items.name: Sledgehammer of the Boxer
items.desc: Ringside at the Legion Stadium, a trainer kept it to ring the bell when the regular hammer went missing. Rumour holds his fighter did roadwork with it slung over one shoulder.

items.name: Sledgehammer of the Stevedore
items.desc: Dockside at San Pedro it knocked wedges loose for a gang that unloaded Tony Cornero's fish by moonlight. The fish never once needed ice.

items.name: Superior Colt Single Action Army
items.desc: Hand-fitted by the gunsmith at Stembridge's on Marathon Street, who swears the cylinder locks up tighter than the studio payroll.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of Agility
items.desc: Fanned from the hip in forty-one Westerns by a Gower Gulch extra who never once got a screen credit. The hammer moves before the thought does.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of Stamina
items.desc: Heavier than it looks, and carried by a Burbank night watchman who walked the First National lot eleven hours a shift without sitting down. The holster wore through twice. He never did.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of the Acrobat
items.desc: Twirled, tossed and caught behind the back at every rodeo matinee Tom Mix ever played, though never by Tom Mix. His stunt double kept it when the show folded.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of the Marksman
items.desc: Its owner split playing cards edgewise in the Hollywood Hotel bar for drinks that did not legally exist. The front sight has been filed to a needle by a patient thumb.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a crate stencilled as machine parts, and the longshoreman who pried it open decided he had found the best part. It settles cargo disputes quickly.

items.name: Superior Colt M1911
items.desc: Among Burbank machinists it is said the Lockheed shop turned this one between aircraft parts. Nobody has asked the Lockheed shop, which is now full of insects.

items.name: Colt M1911 of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch stunt rider who could draw, fire and fall off a horse in the same second. Only the falling ever made the picture.

items.name: Colt M1911 of Stamina
items.desc: Carried through the Argonne by a corporal who outlasted his regiment, his marriage and two landlords. The grips are worn smooth where he held on.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Tucked into the waistband of a wire-walker from the Christie lot, it has spent more time upside down than right side up. It fires either way.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner, a Legion range officer, hit what he aimed at and nothing else, a rarer gift on the Boulevard than a good speaking voice. A small notch is filed beside the rear sight.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shipped north from the San Pedro docks in a crate marked machine parts, by a longshoreman who thought the label accurate enough. Faint tar still darkens the grips.

items.name: Superior Springfield M1903
items.desc: Every screw indexed, every part hand-lapped, the work of a Paramount machinist with no sets left to build. He lends it out on one condition: it comes back clean.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of Agility
items.desc: Quick on the bolt. A Lockheed rigger could work it four times before a Flier finished its dive, and said so at the Brown Derby until somebody paid for his coffee.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of Stamina
items.desc: This one survived the Meuse-Argonne, a Mojave summer and a sergeant who used it as a tent pole. It still shoots straight, which is more than anyone said of the sergeant.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of the Acrobat
items.desc: A Mack Sennett stuntman slung it across his back for rooftop chase gags and once fired it upside down from a swinging ladder, mostly for the cameraman. The sling is sewn from old trapeze webbing.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of the Marksman
items.desc: Brought home from France with its telescopic sight still mounted and a notebook of ranges tucked in the butt trap. Its owner dropped a Spitter across Lake Hollywood and wrote down the yardage before he celebrated.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Longshoremen carried it on the San Pedro night shift to keep Cornero's boats honest, or at least punctual. Shoulders built on sugar sacks take the kick without comment.

items.name: Superior Remington Model 11
items.desc: The best the Valley gun rooms could turn out before factory stock ran dry. Stembridge would have rented it at double rates and called it a favour.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of Agility
items.desc: Lighter in the hands than it looks. Its last owner, a Gower Gulch rider, could swing it off a saddle horn and fire before the horse had noticed.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of Stamina
items.desc: Carried through three hive surges at the Universal front gate by a night watchman who refused to go home. The gate held. The watchman, eventually, went home.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of the Acrobat
items.desc: A Universal stuntman borrowed it from a western set and never returned it, on the grounds that it had done most of its rehearsing upside down.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of the Marksman
items.desc: Shotguns are not meant for picking a single Flier out of the sky at forty yards. Nobody told the Lake Hollywood duck hunter who filed this front bead by hand.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a lumber schooner at San Pedro wrapped in oilcloth, listed on the manifest as fence posts. The receiver still smells faintly of tar and harbour water.

items.name: Superior Thompson M1928
items.desc: Burbank machinists tuned the action to run as smooth as an aero engine. Since the hive moved into the Lockheed sheds, the men who did the work are not around to accept compliments.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of Agility
items.desc: One Strip bouncer swore by it: keep the feet moving and the muzzle down. He kept both, right up until the night a Flier came through a speakeasy skylight.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of Stamina
items.desc: Belonged to a night watchman at the Christie lot who held the paint-shop door for nine hours with it, then walked home for breakfast. Nobody has managed to make him tell it differently.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Rented for a rooftop chase picture in which the double leapt from the Taft Building onto a moving truck. He did it in one take, gun and all, and the director asked for another.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Marksman
items.desc: A Prohibition agent filed the front sight to his own taste and fired it in short, thrifty bursts of two rounds apiece. The Bureau never reimbursed him for the file.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a crate marked pianos, underneath four hundred pounds of actual pianos. The longshoreman who found it decided he had earned the commission.

items.name: Superior Riot Shield
items.desc: Legion armourers at Post 43 built a handful of these for the Pass road, each scratched with a mark by someone who expected to count them all back in.

items.name: Riot Shield of Strength
items.desc: Hynes's Red Squad carried this one through a Plaza meeting last March. The dents along the rim are the only minutes anyone kept.

items.name: Riot Shield of Stamina
items.desc: Patrolmen on the Boulevard beat swear it has outlasted three sergeants, two chiefs' speeches and a pension board.

items.name: Riot Shield of the Boxer
items.desc: Hung for a season behind the ring at the Legion Stadium, where it caught a flying stool most Friday nights and never once complained to the referee.

items.name: Riot Shield of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks after the '23 strike, still smelling of tarred rope and other men's opinions.

items.name: Superior Arc Lamp
items.desc: Polished reflector, ground-glass lens and a switch that clicks like a good cigarette case. Mack Sennett's electricians would have traded a custard pie for one.

items.name: Arc Lamp of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a gaffer on the First National lot who could recite the whole stage wiring diagram from memory, and frequently did, uninvited. The carbons still burn a clean, thinking white.

items.name: Arc Lamp of Spirit
items.desc: Kept lit through three nights on the Mount Lee ridge so the forward camp could see one another's faces. The men swear it warms a tent better than any stove, which the quartermaster disputes.

items.name: Arc Lamp of the Engineer
items.desc: Rewired at the Lockheed plant by a fellow who swore it could survive a drop from the top of a hangar door. He tested the theory twice and was asked to stop.

items.name: Arc Lamp of the Doctor
items.desc: A surgeon at the river camp clamped it over his table when the generator quit. Steady hands, a steady arc, and only one complaint about the smell of hot carbon.

items.name: Arc Lamp of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried at the head of a Sunday procession down Ventura Boulevard, a hymnal in the other hand. It still smells faintly of pew polish, and nobody argued with the deacon while it was lit.

items.name: Superior Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit
items.desc: Stocked at the Burbank aid station from the last good shipment before the Dome closed. Nurses sign it out by name and count the safety pins when it comes back.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of Intellect
items.desc: Its owner pencilled dosage tables inside the lid in a hand so small and so correct that the drugstore on Highland tried to hire her.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of Spirit
items.desc: Found on the Echo Park boathouse dock beside a thermos and a note promising back in ten minutes. Whoever left it never hurried, and it shows.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of the Engineer
items.desc: Rebuilt by a Lockheed fitter with a hinged tray and a socket wrench under the splints, since wounds and engines tend to fail at the same hour.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of the Doctor
items.desc: Lifted from a house-call bag on Los Feliz Boulevard, its stethoscope still coiled under the cotton wool. The physician got out. His Packard did not.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of the Deacon
items.desc: Smells of hymnals, liniment and the long walk to Angelus Temple. Somebody pressed a poppy between the bandage rolls and nobody has had the heart to remove it.

items.name: Superior Family Bible
items.desc: Printed in Philadelphia in 1871 and carried west by a family that later settled in Los Feliz, with an engraved plate for every chapter of Exodus. The plague of locusts reads differently these days.

items.name: Family Bible of Intellect
items.desc: The margins are crowded with pencilled cross-references in a schoolteacher's hand, Leviticus argued against Luke. Whoever owned it read the whole thing twice and the concordance three times.

items.name: Family Bible of Spirit
items.desc: Pressed between the pages are a dried orange blossom from a 1903 wedding and a lock of baby hair folded in wax paper. It is calmer to hold than it has any right to be.

items.name: Family Bible of the Engineer
items.desc: A Lockheed riveter carried it in his lunch pail for eleven years. The cover is dented where a falling bucking bar found it instead of him, which he took as a plain answer to prayer.

items.name: Family Bible of the Doctor
items.desc: Kept in the waiting room of a Vermont Avenue physician, who wrote dosages on the flyleaf whenever his prescription pad ran out. Half his patients came for the doctor and half for Ecclesiastes.

items.name: Family Bible of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried on foot from Edendale to Angelus Temple every Sunday for nine years, and it smells of hymnals and wet wool. Sister Aimee is said to have signed the flyleaf; the deacon never let anyone check.

items.name: Chitin-lined Silk Top Hat
items.desc: A Burbank milliner stitched shell into the crown after a Flier took the hat off a banker, and the top of the banker with it. Opening nights now come with precautions.

items.name: Silk Top Hat of Intellect
items.desc: Left on a hook at the Writers' table in Musso & Frank's. The lining holds four pencil stubs and a contract with every clause underlined twice.

items.name: Silk Top Hat of Spirit
items.desc: A retired tenor wore it to every Greek Theatre concert that first summer and hummed all the way home. Something of the humming seems to have stayed in the crown.

items.name: Silk Top Hat of Stamina
items.desc: Its last owner stood through a six-hour premiere line at Grauman's, a three-reel speech and a hive surge on the forecourt. The hat was the only one who complained less.

items.name: Silk Top Hat of the Engineer
items.desc: Belonged to a Lockheed draughtsman who wore it to the office on principle. A slide rule fits the crown exactly, which he claimed was the whole point.

items.name: Silk Top Hat of the Doctor
items.desc: House calls on the Hollywood Hills meant a hat that commanded the door. The doctor kept a tongue depressor in the band and a calm voice for frightened maids.

items.name: Silk Top Hat of the Deacon
items.desc: Worn every Sunday on the long walk to Angelus Temple and lifted to every widow along the way. The brim still smells faintly of hymnals and lilies.

items.name: Chitin-lined Stunt Rider's Helmet
items.desc: Under the leather sits a curved plate of Drone shell, boiled soft and pressed to shape. Riders swear it rings like a bell when a branch catches it, and stops the branch cold.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Helmet of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a motorcycle man who jumped the canal on Universal's European street twice a day for the camera and once for a bet. The bet paid better.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Helmet of Stamina
items.desc: Dented in eleven places, each one a fall the wearer got up from. The studio paid him for nine of them.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Helmet of Spirit
items.desc: Stitched inside the lining is a St. Christopher medal, put there by a rider's mother. He never once wrote home about the work, and she never once asked.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Helmet of the Acrobat
items.desc: Tumbling from a galloping horse onto a moving red car made its owner famous on Poverty Row, at seven-fifty a day plus bruises.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Helmet of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off the San Pedro docks with a longshoreman who took up stunt riding because it paid better and the bosses shouted less. Both claims proved half true.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Helmet of the Deacon
items.desc: Smells faintly of hymnal paper and motor oil. Its owner rode a sidecar rig to Angelus Temple every Sunday and claimed the Lord did the steering on the hairpins.

items.name: Chitin-lined Quilted Aviator Helmet
items.desc: Between the quilting layers someone slipped thin panes of Flier wing, which turn a Spitter's acid and hum faintly in a crosswind. The hum takes getting used to.

items.name: Quilted Aviator Helmet of Agility
items.desc: A wing-walker wore this crossing from one biplane to another over Burbank for a newsreel. She kept the fee in coins so she could hear it.

items.name: Quilted Aviator Helmet of Strength
items.desc: Hand-cranking aero engines at United Airport builds the shoulders of a blacksmith. The mechanic who owned this one could swing a propeller and a grudge with equal ease.

items.name: Quilted Aviator Helmet of Stamina
items.desc: Recovered from a Fokker that came down hard during the Hell's Angels shoot. The pilot recovered too, eventually, and still will not discuss the dailies.

items.name: Quilted Aviator Helmet of the Boxer
items.desc: Friday nights at the Legion Stadium and mail runs on weekdays: its owner reasoned a man used to being hit could survive a bad landing. He had a point, briefly.

items.name: Quilted Aviator Helmet of the Marksman
items.desc: Goggle straps are cut to sit clear of a rifle stock. Its owner rode the rear cockpit over Burbank and could put a camera, or a bullet, exactly where the director pointed.

items.name: Quilted Aviator Helmet of the Acrobat
items.desc: Padded thickly at the temples for a barnstormer who hung by his knees from a landing gear over Glendale, smiling for the photographers upside down.

items.name: Quilted Aviator Helmet of the Engineer
items.desc: Pencil stubs and a feeler gauge rattle in the ear-flap pocket. It belonged to a Lockheed draughtsman who test-flew his own designs on the theory that it kept him honest.

items.name: Chitin-lined Chitin-crested Helmet
items.desc: Shell outside, shell inside, and a soldier somewhere between. The lining keeps acid off the scalp and keeps the wearer from forgetting what it used to be.

items.name: Chitin-crested Helmet of Strength
items.desc: Its last owner pried a Brute's jaws apart on Olive Avenue and wore this to do it. The dent over the left ear is the Brute's side of the story.

items.name: Chitin-crested Helmet of Stamina
items.desc: Taken off a Legion corporal who held the Lockheed fence for two days without sleep. He kept the helmet on the whole time and asked for it back afterwards. The answer was no.

items.name: Chitin-crested Helmet of the Boxer
items.desc: Painted inside with the dates of nine Friday nights at the Legion Stadium. The crest was added after the tenth, when the opponent had six legs.

items.name: Chitin-crested Helmet of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up the coast in a crate marked machine parts and smells faintly of San Pedro tar. Dockmen say the crest was meant for catching swung cargo hooks, and occasionally does.

items.name: Chitin-lined Opening Night Tailcoat
items.desc: Wardrobe in Burbank sewed shell plates under the silk after the drones began attending premieres uninvited. It rustles when it bows.

items.name: Opening Night Tailcoat of Intellect
items.desc: Its last owner was a scenario writer who read every contract twice and still got no screen credit. The inside pocket holds a pencil stub and a grudge.

items.name: Opening Night Tailcoat of Spirit
items.desc: Worn to the Hell's Angels premiere in May, when searchlights crossed the sky over Grauman's. Whoever owned it kept the programme folded in the lining like a pressed flower.

items.name: Opening Night Tailcoat of Stamina
items.desc: A doorman stood in this through eleven hours of premiere and two fistfights over seating. The seams have never once complained.

items.name: Opening Night Tailcoat of the Engineer
items.desc: Borrowed off a First National wardrobe rack by a Lockheed draughtsman who needed something decent for a banquet. He returned it with oil on one cuff and a wing-spar sketch in the pocket.

items.name: Opening Night Tailcoat of the Doctor
items.desc: On call through every first night of the season, its owner left before the second reel whenever a telephone rang. The left pocket still smells of ether and good cigars.

items.name: Opening Night Tailcoat of the Deacon
items.desc: Angelus Temple's choir director wore it for broadcasts over KFSG, where no listener could see him. He dressed properly regardless, on the principle that the Lord has excellent reception.

items.name: Chitin-lined Pendleton-lined Riding Coat
items.desc: Somewhere under the plaid, a sheet of invader shell rides against the ribs. It creaks in cold weather, and horses do not care for the smell.

items.name: Pendleton-lined Riding Coat of Agility
items.desc: Rode with a trick rider from the Tom Mix outfit, a man who could drop off one side of a galloping horse and come up the other with his hat still on.

items.name: Pendleton-lined Riding Coat of Stamina
items.desc: Built for night herding across the Burbank flats, where the wind comes cold off the Dome and the coyotes sing until dawn. The lining is thick enough to sleep in, and someone did.

items.name: Pendleton-lined Riding Coat of Spirit
items.desc: A circuit rider's coat, worn through three revivals and one flood. The inside pocket holds the shape of a small Testament, and the lining smells faintly of woodsmoke and patience.

items.name: Pendleton-lined Riding Coat of the Acrobat
items.desc: Stuntmen at the Mack Sennett lot favoured it for falls off moving buckboards: the wool lining eats the landing and the leather shrugs off the gravel.

items.name: Pendleton-lined Riding Coat of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from San Pedro on a lumber truck, its owner hired to wrangle horses and paid to unload hay. He said the horses were easier to talk to.

items.name: Pendleton-lined Riding Coat of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday its owner rode from Studio City to Angelus Temple on a slow mare, rehearsing hymns the whole way. The mare learned the tunes first.

items.name: Chitin-lined Football Shoulder Pads
items.desc: Behind the felt sits a curved slab of soldier shell, cut to fit the collarbone. The equipment manager who made them still will not say where he got the template.

items.name: Football Shoulder Pads of Agility
items.desc: Off a USC halfback who ran the Coliseum sideline like it owed him money. Howard Jones would have liked him faster; the invaders would have liked him slower.

items.name: Football Shoulder Pads of Strength
items.desc: Lineman's pads, broad as a door and nearly as heavy. The previous owner pushed a stalled red car half a block in these, then complained about his lunch.

items.name: Football Shoulder Pads of Stamina
items.desc: Sixty minutes both ways was the rule, and these pads played every one of them. The leather is cracked at the seams from a season that never quite ended.

items.name: Football Shoulder Pads of the Boxer
items.desc: Under a sweater at Legion Stadium, a heavyweight wore these and claimed it was for his posture. The referee let it go, having seen him punch.

items.name: Football Shoulder Pads of the Marksman
items.desc: Its quarterback could hit a receiver's hands at forty yards in a crosswind. Now he hits spitters at the same range with a Springfield and says the spiral matters less.

items.name: Football Shoulder Pads of the Acrobat
items.desc: Taken off a stunt double who stood in for players because nobody else would tumble on frozen sod for scale. Flexible at the shoulder, forgiving at the landing.

items.name: Football Shoulder Pads of the Engineer
items.desc: Lockheed draughtsmen played Saturday ball against the Burbank firemen, and one reworked the hinge on these with a slide rule. He lost the game but won the argument.

items.name: Chitin-lined Chitin-plated Cuirass
items.desc: Shell outside, shell inside. The armourers at the forward camp ran out of horsehair padding and concluded the invaders had already solved the problem.

items.name: Chitin-plated Cuirass of Strength
items.desc: Taken off a Legion man at the Lockheed plant who could lift a crated propeller without help. The plates are dented inward in two places, and he walked away from both.

items.name: Chitin-plated Cuirass of Stamina
items.desc: Its first owner wore it through a three-day siege of Burbank town centre, slept in it, and refused to take it off for the doctor. The lining still smells of coffee and Lysol.

items.name: Chitin-plated Cuirass of the Boxer
items.desc: A Legion Stadium trainer laced it together from salvaged shell and the canvas of a burst heavy bag. On Friday nights he still offers to tape the wearer's knuckles, out of habit.

items.name: Chitin-plated Cuirass of the Stevedore
items.desc: Belonged to a San Pedro longshoreman who came up to Studio City for a funeral and stayed for the Dome. He fitted cargo-hook loops under both arms, and nobody has worked out why.

items.name: Chitin-lined Striped Morning Trousers
items.desc: Between the wool and the silk lining lies a layer of shell, cut thin by a wardrobe girl at First National. The trousers rustle at every step, like someone turning a page behind you.

items.name: Striped Morning Trousers of Intellect
items.desc: Carl Laemmle's front office kept a rack of these for executives who read a contract twice before signing it. One pair still carries a leaked fountain pen's worth of ink in the watch pocket.

items.name: Striped Morning Trousers of Spirit
items.desc: Pressed for a church wedding on Highland that was set for the Saturday the Dome came down. The groom gave them away afterward, which seemed the decent thing.

items.name: Striped Morning Trousers of Stamina
items.desc: Undertakers at Hollywood Cemetery wear one pair from first service to the last shovel. These have stood through a hard autumn of both and never once sagged at the knee.

items.name: Striped Morning Trousers of the Engineer
items.desc: A Lockheed draughtsman wore them to the plant daily, on the theory that a man in morning dress looks too important to eat. The theory held until Tuesday.

items.name: Striped Morning Trousers of the Doctor
items.desc: Smells faintly of ether and carbolic soap. Their owner, a Burbank surgeon, held that formal dress calmed a patient, and swore by it right up to the operating table.

items.name: Striped Morning Trousers of the Deacon
items.desc: Sunday best for the trip from Burbank to Angelus Temple, which these days takes two red cars and one rifle. Folded hymnal pages still sit in the hip pocket.

items.name: Chitin-lined Stunt Rider's Leggings
items.desc: Shell from an Elder Spitter backs the leather now, since acid eats hide and slides off chitin. Nobody at the Burbank camp asks where the horse went.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Leggings of Agility
items.desc: Tom Mix's stand-in wore these for the leap across a backlot gully, then wore them again because the director wanted it from a second angle.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Leggings of Stamina
items.desc: Twenty-two falls from a galloping horse and the leather never split. The man inside fared worse, but he signed up for the twenty-third.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Leggings of Spirit
items.desc: An extra from Gower Gulch said his rosary on the long rides between takes. The leather has gone soft and quiet from all that patience.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Leggings of the Acrobat
items.desc: Cut loose at the knee for vaulting from a balcony onto a moving horse, a stunt the Chaplin lot paid five dollars for and filmed nine times.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Leggings of the Stevedore
items.desc: Made for riding, but they spent a lean year hauling feed sacks off the San Pedro boats when picture work dried up. The cuffs still hold a dusting of barley and salt.

items.name: Stunt Rider's Leggings of the Deacon
items.desc: Worn by a cowboy preacher who rode the Valley circuit with a sermon in one saddlebag and a Winchester in the other. He held that both were scripture in the right hands.

items.name: Chitin-lined Quilted Leggings
items.desc: Between canvas and batting runs a layer of Drone wing, thin as cellophane and twice as stubborn. It rustles whenever the wearer sits down.

items.name: Quilted Leggings of Agility
items.desc: Stuntmen at the Sennett lot wore these for pratfalls off rooftops, back when the worst thing on a roof was a custard pie. The padding has learned a few new falls since.

items.name: Quilted Leggings of Strength
items.desc: Cut for a Lockheed riveter with thighs like bridge pilings. The tailor took the measurements twice and still had to let the seams out.

items.name: Quilted Leggings of Stamina
items.desc: The previous owner walked from Burbank to the river camp in these with a Spitter on his heels, then sat down on a crate and ate his lunch.

items.name: Quilted Leggings of the Boxer
items.desc: Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, a heavyweight's cornerman wore these and took more punishment from the cheap seats than his fighter ever took in the ring.

items.name: Quilted Leggings of the Marksman
items.desc: Belonged to a Stembridge armourer who hit what he aimed at and did his windage sums in pencil on the left thigh. The kneeling knee is worn nearly through.

items.name: Quilted Leggings of the Acrobat
items.desc: Quilting this loose was meant for circus pictures at Universal, where a trapeze man had to fold in half and land standing. The circus folded first.

items.name: Quilted Leggings of the Engineer
items.desc: Pockets on both thighs hold a slide rule, a test lamp and three spare fuses. A Lockheed draughtsman designed them on company time and filed it as research.

items.name: Chitin-lined Chitin Greaves
items.desc: Armourers ran short of steel somewhere around Burbank and began lining shell with more shell. It works, which annoys them considerably.

items.name: Chitin Greaves of Strength
items.desc: A Post 43 machine-gunner had these made to carry a Browning up the Pass without stopping. He stopped once, to argue about the route.

items.name: Chitin Greaves of Stamina
items.desc: Elder Brute knockbacks dent the shell but seldom the man inside. The smith who forged them charges extra for that sentence alone.

items.name: Chitin Greaves of the Boxer
items.desc: Rumour at the Legion Stadium holds that a middleweight once wore these into the ring on a bet. He was disqualified for having knees harder than the other fellow's jaw.

items.name: Chitin Greaves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Hauled cargo at San Pedro for ten years, the owner said, and nothing down there ever bit back. He wore these on the river camp's loading line and said it less often.

items.name: Chitin-lined Patent Leather Pumps
items.desc: Under the patent shine, a lining of pared Spitter shell keeps the acid off the stockings. Fashion columnists have been asked not to look too closely.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of Intellect
items.desc: Last worn by a script girl at First National who kept continuity on eleven pictures at once and never lost a cigarette between takes. The heels are scuffed from pacing.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of Spirit
items.desc: Somebody danced till dawn in these in the Roosevelt's Blossom Room the night before the Dome came down. They still carry the tune, if not the partner.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of Stamina
items.desc: Built for a chorus line that did four shows a day at the Pantages and never once sat down. The soles have walked the Boulevard more often than the red car.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of the Engineer
items.desc: Salvaged from a Lockheed draughtswoman's locker, along with a slide rule and a ham sandwich of uncertain age. The heels were filed square so they would not catch on catwalk grating.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of the Doctor
items.desc: An aid-station nurse in Burbank swears by them: quiet on linoleum, quick on stairs and easy to wipe clean. She did not say clean of what.

items.name: Patent Leather Pumps of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday for nine years these walked a widow from Edendale to Angelus Temple and back, rain or none. They smell faintly of hymnals and shoe polish, and they do not hurry.

items.name: Chitin-lined Cavalry Boots
items.desc: Burrowers strike from below, so a Burbank saddler started stitching shell between sole and insole. Riders are scarce now; the boots get walked into the ground instead.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of Agility
items.desc: Tom Mix's stable hands say the man who broke these in could mount from a standing start and dismount at a gallop. Nobody has asked the horse.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Thirty miles a day along the border in 1916, if the tag stitched inside is honest. The leather has gone hard as a fence post and about as tired.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of Spirit
items.desc: Kept on a closet shelf in Los Feliz by a retired major who polished them every evening and never rode again. There is something calming in the shine.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: One Gower Gulch extra did his own falls from the saddle in these for five dollars a day and a box lunch. He took the boots when the picture wrapped; the star took the credit.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off a San Pedro cargo foreman who wore riding boots for reasons he never explained and kicked crates about like they owed him money. The toes are flattened from it.

items.name: Cavalry Boots of the Deacon
items.desc: Mud from three counties and a dozen camp meetings is worked into the welts. The circuit preacher who owned them held that a horse is the only congregation that never leaves early.

items.name: Chitin-lined Logger Boots
items.desc: Somebody in a Burbank cobbler's shop discovered that invader shell, boiled and shaved thin, keeps acid out better than any oilskin. Nobody asked where the shell came from, and he did not volunteer it.

items.name: Logger Boots of Agility
items.desc: A set carpenter at First National wore these up and down scaffolding forty feet above the stage floor and never once grabbed a rail. The foreman docked him for it anyway, on principle.

items.name: Logger Boots of Strength
items.desc: Built for a man who carried railroad ties on each shoulder at the Studio City lumberyard and complained they were uneven. The heels are worn flat from leaning into heavy loads.

items.name: Logger Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Whoever owned these walked the Los Angeles River bed from Laurel Canyon to Burbank twice a day running messages. The soles have been replaced three times; the man, never.

items.name: Logger Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Stadium sweepers swear a heavyweight wore these into the ring at the Legion one Friday night, lost on points, and refused to take them off for the photograph. The left toe has a dent shaped like somebody's chin.

items.name: Logger Boots of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner kept watch from the Burbank water tower with a Springfield and a thermos of coffee. The tally notched into the heel counts Spitters, and it ran out of room.

items.name: Logger Boots of the Acrobat
items.desc: Sennett's people say these went off a rooftop on Ventura Boulevard, through an awning and onto a moving truck in one take. The stuntman walked away limping; the boots walked away fine.

items.name: Logger Boots of the Engineer
items.desc: Lockheed riggers favoured this pattern because the steel toe survived a dropped propeller hub and a pocket sewn inside the shaft held a slide rule. Two pencils are still in there, both chewed.

items.name: Chitin-lined Chitin-shod Boots
items.desc: Twice the shell for twice the trouble: carapace on the sole and more of it sewn inside against Spitter acid. Quartermasters at the river camp call them double-bugged and keep a straight face.

items.name: Chitin-shod Boots of Strength
items.desc: Rumour on the Burbank line says a Veteran kicked a Brute's knee out from under it wearing these. The Brute's opinion went unrecorded.

items.name: Chitin-shod Boots of Stamina
items.desc: Forty pounds the pair, and the Legion sergeant who issued them swore a man could march to the Dome wall and back in them. Several tried. The boots made it every time.

items.name: Chitin-shod Boots of the Boxer
items.desc: Taped at the ankles like a fighter's wrists and smelling of liniment and Legion Stadium cigars. Fight-night regulars swear they never lost a round, mainly because they were never allowed in the ring.

items.name: Chitin-shod Boots of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shipped up from San Pedro before the Dome came down, made for men who walked cargo nets and hauled crates marked machine parts that sloshed. The customs men never looked closely, and nobody looks now.

items.name: Chitin-lined Opera Gloves
items.desc: The satin is genuine. So is the lining, peeled from a dead Spitter's wing case and shaved thin enough to bend, so that acid beads off it like rain on a windshield.

items.name: Opera Gloves of Intellect
items.desc: Left on a seat at the Pantages by a lady who did the crossword in ink between acts and never once looked at the stage. The index fingertip is still faintly blue.

items.name: Opera Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Since 1921 they have gone to every Easter sunrise service at the Hollywood Bowl and come home a shade calmer. They still smell of cold morning air and violets.

items.name: Opera Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Eleven retakes and one hive raid, in that order, on the Sennett lot. The chorus girl who wore them insists the retakes were worse.

items.name: Opera Gloves of the Engineer
items.desc: Fitted with a brass thimble in each fingertip by a Lockheed draughtswoman who liked to tap every rivet before she trusted it. She trusted very few.

items.name: Opera Gloves of the Doctor
items.desc: Their owner ran an aid station out of a Burbank supper club cloakroom and refused to take them off. Scrubbing in, she said, was for people with running water.

items.name: Opera Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: Every Sunday the red cars ran, a deaconess carried these tucked in her hymnal from Echo Park to Burbank and back. The pages left a faint gilt line along the left cuff.

items.name: Chitin-lined Everlast Bag Gloves
items.desc: Inside, a sleeve of thinned Drone shell keeps the knuckles from splitting on harder shell. Burbank fight crowds call that fair play.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of Agility
items.desc: Light enough for a flyweight who never stood still long enough to be hit. His trainer swore the kid could slip a punch before the other fellow had finished thinking of it.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Twelve rounds a night against a gym sandbag, then forty against a Drone in a Burbank alley. By the owner's reckoning the sandbag put up the better fight.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of Spirit
items.desc: Saturday sparring and Sunday sermons got the same pair from an Eagle Rock parson, who argued that turning the other cheek came easier with your guard up.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: Circus tumbler, then stuntman, then this. The previous owner came off the Sennett water tower knuckles-first more often than he cared to count, and the left glove is patched where the mattress wasn't.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a longshoreman wore them under his cargo hooks to keep the nets from chewing his palms. Weekends he boxed to cover the rent.

items.name: Everlast Bag Gloves of the Deacon
items.desc: Kept in the vestry of a Burbank Methodist church for the young men's boxing club. Somebody folded a hymn sheet into the right cuff, and it has stayed through every fight since.

items.name: Chitin-lined Welder's Gauntlets
items.desc: Invader shell sewn inside the palm turns heat better than asbestos and smells faintly of the hive on a warm afternoon. The Burbank shops stopped asking where the scraps came from.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of Agility
items.desc: Cut a size under regulation for a Burbank welder who liked working high on ladders and coming down from them in a hurry.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of Strength
items.desc: Their last owner straightened a bent red-car rail on Ventura Boulevard by himself, or so the river camp tells it. The story grows a foot every time the coffee runs out.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of Stamina
items.desc: Found on a bench in the First National machine shop, beside a thermos and a lunch pail nobody came back for.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of the Boxer
items.desc: A Legion Stadium heavyweight wore these welding bleacher brackets on Saturday mornings to pay for his Friday-night losses. The left one still throws a fair uppercut.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of the Marksman
items.desc: Sewn with a thin trigger finger for a Lockheed inspector who spent his breaks shooting tin cans off the United Airport fence. He rarely missed and never let anyone forget it.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of the Acrobat
items.desc: Borrowed from the Sennett prop shop by a stuntman who welded his own wire rigs and trusted nobody else's seams. He fell off three roofs in them and kept both hands.

items.name: Welder's Gauntlets of the Engineer
items.desc: Pencil sums are scorched into the cuff, where an airframe man worked out load figures between welds. Most of them check out; the one that does not has been circled twice.

items.name: Chitin-lined Plated Gauntlets
items.desc: Lined with shaved invader shell, which turns a sting better than horsehide ever did. Nobody has explained why the lining is warm in the morning.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of Strength
items.desc: Riveted together in the Columbia machine shop from a boiler hatch and the lining of two catcher's mitts. The carpenter who made them swears he bent a crowbar back straight while wearing them.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of Stamina
items.desc: Built for a Legion sergeant who held the Pass road for two nights without relief. He gave them up only when the nurse at the aid station insisted, and even then he kept the left one.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of the Boxer
items.desc: A Friday-night regular at the Legion Stadium had these made after the referee barred him from wearing them into the ring. Rosin dust from the canvas still sits in the knuckle seams.

items.name: Plated Gauntlets of the Stevedore
items.desc: Off the San Pedro docks, where a longshoreman wore them hooking banana crates and the occasional case of Canadian whisky that somehow never made the manifest.

items.name: Chitin-lined Cummerbund
items.desc: Wardrobe at the Sennett lot sewed shell scraps behind the pleats once the satin ran out of arguments. It creaks at the waist like a cheap chair.

items.name: Cummerbund of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a Universal story editor who read four hundred scripts a year and bought six. He kept notes in the pleats; a pencil stub still rides in the top fold.

items.name: Cummerbund of Spirit
items.desc: Worn to the last dance in the Roosevelt's Blossom Room before the Dome came down. Its owner kept dancing afterward, after a fashion, and swears a good sash settles the nerves.

items.name: Cummerbund of Stamina
items.desc: Recovered from a Burbank banquet hall where the head waiter held the kitchen door against three Drones for most of an evening. He maintains the sash did half the work.

items.name: Cummerbund of the Engineer
items.desc: A Lockheed draughtsman wore it to the company dinner, then straight back to the drafting room when the sirens went. Grease-pencil figures on the lining work out stress loads for a wing nobody built.

items.name: Cummerbund of the Doctor
items.desc: Cut from the evening clothes of a Vine Street surgeon called away from the Brown Derby mid-soup. Iodine stains along the hem suggest he never did get back to the soup.

items.name: Cummerbund of the Deacon
items.desc: Sister Aimee's ushers wore something like it on Sunday nights. This one made the long walk from Echo Park to the Burbank line and still smells of hymnals and lamp oil.

items.name: Chitin-lined Sam Browne Belt
items.desc: Somebody in the Universal leather shop found that Spitter shell turns acid better than cowhide and sewed a lining of it inside the strap. It fits close and sweats cold.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of Agility
items.desc: Off a Lockheed test pilot who walked away from three crashes and a breach-of-promise suit. The shoulder strap is cut short so nothing snags on the way out of a cockpit.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of Stamina
items.desc: Issued to an LAPD motorcycle sergeant who patrolled Ventura Boulevard eleven days without relief. The leather is cracked across the back where he slept sitting up.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of Spirit
items.desc: Through Burbank's worst week a Salvation Army captain wore this while pouring coffee from a tin urn for anyone who asked. The strap still smells of grounds and gun oil.

items.name: Sam Browne Belt of the Acrobat
