items.name: Diamond Pinky Ring of the Engineer
items.desc: Bought after a Lockheed draughtsman's first patent and worn while drawing wing ribs. Diamond scratches glass, so when paper ran short he marked measurements on the plant windows.

items.name: Diamond Pinky Ring of the Doctor
items.desc: House calls on Whitley Heights were its old beat, worn by a physician who considered it part of the bedside manner. Since the Dome he has worked a Burbank aid station, and the stone has seen more stitches than champagne.

items.name: Diamond Pinky Ring of the Deacon
items.desc: Pledged at Angelus Temple during a Sunday offering and never redeemed. The deacon who carried it up to the camp below the sign walks the long way round, and says the walk is the point.

items.name: Chitin-plated Trench Knife
items.desc: Plated along the spine with shell cut on the ridge below the sign. The men at the Mount Lee forward camp call it the souvenir that bites back.

items.name: Trench Knife of Agility
items.desc: Carried over the top at Saint-Mihiel by a lance corporal who later worked falls for Fox. He said the trick was the same in both trades: be somewhere else when it lands.

items.name: Trench Knife of Stamina
items.desc: Its owner held a doorway at the Lockheed plant for most of one night with this and a bad leg. The Legion kept the knife. The doorway is still disputed.

items.name: Trench Knife of the Acrobat
items.desc: A Universal stunt rider kept it in his boot through forty-one falls off the backlot church tower and one off a real roof. The insurance men never did hear about the knife.

items.name: Trench Knife of the Marksman
items.desc: Notches on the knuckle bow count shots, not stabs. The previous owner preferred a rifle and kept this for when the rifle ran dry above Burbank. Twelve notches, room for more.

items.name: Trench Knife of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a San Pedro lighter wrapped in oilcloth, alongside a crate of Cornero's Scotch that never reached Hollywood. Dock men used it to open crates, then to settle arguments about them.

items.name: Chitin-plated Weighted Gloves
items.desc: Plates of drone carapace are bolted across the knuckles, still faintly warm on cold mornings. Men at the forward camp below the sign sleep in them, and nobody makes jokes about it anymore.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of Agility
items.desc: Light enough to throw a punch and be somewhere else when the answer comes back. Taken off a Dragna gunman in Studio City who reached for his pocket a half-second too late.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of Stamina
items.desc: Built for a long night. The last owner held the Laurel Canyon crossing until dawn, then handed these over with a yawn and the advice to keep the left one higher.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of the Acrobat
items.desc: A Sennett tumbler wore these for pratfalls that ended in punches. The palms are scuffed from catching himself off rooftops, which the studio called comedy and the insurance man called something else.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of the Marksman
items.desc: The right trigger finger is cut away, so the owner could punch with one hand and shoot with the other. He kept score in pencil on the cuff and never once rounded up.

items.name: Weighted Gloves of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks with a longshoreman who settled wage disputes before the union got around to it. They still smell of tar, hemp and bananas.

items.name: Chitin-plated Louisville Slugger
items.desc: Every inch of the ash is sheathed in plates cut from a Soldier's back. The league would have suspended it. The man who carried it into the Hive Tunnels never came out to argue the point.

items.name: Louisville Slugger of Strength
items.desc: Taken from a batboy's rack at Wrigley Field after the Hollywood Stars' last home game. It has since sent a Drone's head farther than any ball that season, though the scorekeepers declined to count it.

items.name: Louisville Slugger of Stamina
items.desc: Its owner caught for eleven seasons in the Pacific Coast League and claimed nothing could hurt him after that many foul tips. He still sleeps with it under the cot.

items.name: Louisville Slugger of the Boxer
items.desc: Friday nights at the Legion Stadium, a heavyweight from Pasadena carried this into the ring as a gimmick. The referee never let him use it. The invaders have no referee.

items.name: Louisville Slugger of the Stevedore
items.desc: Longshoremen played pepper with it on the San Pedro wharf at lunch, and the bat picked up the habit of swinging at anything thrown its way. Drones count.

items.name: Chitin-plated Lineman's Wrench
items.desc: Pried from the Lockheed plant after the hive moved in, it now wears scales the colour of an oil slick. It hums against live wire in a way no lineman can explain.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of Intellect
items.desc: A Warner Bros. electrician scratched wiring diagrams into the handle from memory, the night before the lot fell. Nobody else has been able to make sense of them.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of Spirit
items.desc: Kept in a toolbox beside a pocket Testament by a lineman who said a man forty feet up a pole needs a calm heart more than a good grip.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of the Engineer
items.desc: Union men at the IATSE hall called it the long argument, because it settled most of them. It has tightened a junction box on Stage 28 and loosened a Drone's jaw the same afternoon.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of the Doctor
items.desc: Borrowed from a lineman to open a jammed oxygen valve at an aid station, it was never returned. The handle still smells faintly of iodine and carbolic.

items.name: Lineman's Wrench of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried on the long walk to Angelus Temple every Sunday, where its owner kept the KFSG transmitter humming between hymns. Sister Aimee was said to approve of practical faith.

items.name: Chitin-plated M1913 Cavalry Sabre
items.desc: Guard and spine are clad in plates cut from a Brute's back. It weighs less than it should and bites deeper than it ought to, and the men camped below the sign have stopped wondering why.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of Strength
items.desc: Lieutenant Patton designed the blade for thrusting at a gallop. Without the horse, the arm has to supply all the momentum, and this one was ground for arms that could.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of Stamina
items.desc: Carried on the long road from Fort Riley to a Universal western, then on every retake after. Its owner claimed the horse tired first and the director second.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of the Boxer
items.desc: Hung for years over the bar at the Legion Stadium, where the Friday crowd swore it was kept there to settle decisions the judges got wrong.

items.name: M1913 Cavalry Sabre of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a freighter at San Pedro in a crate marked as plumbing. The longshoreman who kept it used it on cargo netting first and on invaders later.

items.name: Chitin-plated Sledgehammer
items.desc: Plated head to haft in Brute carapace, it weighs more than the smith who made it would admit. It was last seen going up the Mount Lee ridge toward the sign.

items.name: Sledgehammer of Strength
items.desc: Swung on a Pacific Electric track gang laying rail toward Burbank, it drove spikes in two blows where other men needed five. The foreman docked its owner for showing off.

items.name: Sledgehammer of Stamina
items.desc: Nobody at the old Mulholland Dam quarry remembers the owner's name, only that he worked double shifts and never once sat down.

items.name: Sledgehammer of the Boxer
items.desc: Ringside at the Legion Stadium, a trainer kept it to ring the bell when the regular hammer went missing. Rumour holds his fighter did roadwork with it slung over one shoulder.

items.name: Sledgehammer of the Stevedore
items.desc: Dockside at San Pedro it knocked wedges loose for a gang that unloaded Tony Cornero's fish by moonlight. The fish never once needed ice.

items.name: Chitin-plated Colt Single Action Army
items.desc: Mount Lee's forward camp plates the frames now, since steel ran short and dead invaders did not. Fifty-seven years after it first came out of Hartford, the Peacemaker is earning the name the hard way.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of Agility
items.desc: Fanned from the hip in forty-one Westerns by a Gower Gulch extra who never once got a screen credit. The hammer moves before the thought does.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of Stamina
items.desc: Heavier than it looks, and carried by a Burbank night watchman who walked the First National lot eleven hours a shift without sitting down. The holster wore through twice. He never did.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of the Acrobat
items.desc: Twirled, tossed and caught behind the back at every rodeo matinee Tom Mix ever played, though never by Tom Mix. His stunt double kept it when the show folded.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of the Marksman
items.desc: Its owner split playing cards edgewise in the Hollywood Hotel bar for drinks that did not legally exist. The front sight has been filed to a needle by a patient thumb.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a crate stencilled as machine parts, and the longshoreman who pried it open decided he had found the best part. It settles cargo disputes quickly.

items.name: Chitin-plated Colt M1911
items.desc: Every surface the bluing once covered is now shell, peeled off a Soldier on Mount Lee and bolted down with stove screws. Under the Dome, that passes for progress.

items.name: Colt M1911 of Agility
items.desc: Belonged to a Gower Gulch stunt rider who could draw, fire and fall off a horse in the same second. Only the falling ever made the picture.

items.name: Colt M1911 of Stamina
items.desc: Carried through the Argonne by a corporal who outlasted his regiment, his marriage and two landlords. The grips are worn smooth where he held on.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Tucked into the waistband of a wire-walker from the Christie lot, it has spent more time upside down than right side up. It fires either way.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Marksman
items.desc: Its last owner, a Legion range officer, hit what he aimed at and nothing else, a rarer gift on the Boulevard than a good speaking voice. A small notch is filed beside the rear sight.

items.name: Colt M1911 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Shipped north from the San Pedro docks in a crate marked machine parts, by a longshoreman who thought the label accurate enough. Faint tar still darkens the grips.

items.name: Chitin-plated Springfield M1903
items.desc: Wartime issue, refitted for a stranger war. The stock is sheathed in plates from the Hive Tunnels, and the rifleman who finished it swears it hums near the queen's chambers, as if it remembers where it came from.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of Agility
items.desc: Quick on the bolt. A Lockheed rigger could work it four times before a Flier finished its dive, and said so at the Brown Derby until somebody paid for his coffee.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of Stamina
items.desc: This one survived the Meuse-Argonne, a Mojave summer and a sergeant who used it as a tent pole. It still shoots straight, which is more than anyone said of the sergeant.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of the Acrobat
items.desc: A Mack Sennett stuntman slung it across his back for rooftop chase gags and once fired it upside down from a swinging ladder, mostly for the cameraman. The sling is sewn from old trapeze webbing.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of the Marksman
items.desc: Brought home from France with its telescopic sight still mounted and a notebook of ranges tucked in the butt trap. Its owner dropped a Spitter across Lake Hollywood and wrote down the yardage before he celebrated.

items.name: Springfield M1903 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Longshoremen carried it on the San Pedro night shift to keep Cornero's boats honest, or at least punctual. Shoulders built on sugar sacks take the kick without comment.

items.name: Chitin-plated Remington Model 11
items.desc: Plated in Elder Soldier shell from receiver to butt, it looks less like a Remington every week. Men at the forward camp beneath the sign swear it hums when the hive is close.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of Agility
items.desc: Lighter in the hands than it looks. Its last owner, a Gower Gulch rider, could swing it off a saddle horn and fire before the horse had noticed.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of Stamina
items.desc: Carried through three hive surges at the Universal front gate by a night watchman who refused to go home. The gate held. The watchman, eventually, went home.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of the Acrobat
items.desc: A Universal stuntman borrowed it from a western set and never returned it, on the grounds that it had done most of its rehearsing upside down.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of the Marksman
items.desc: Shotguns are not meant for picking a single Flier out of the sky at forty yards. Nobody told the Lake Hollywood duck hunter who filed this front bead by hand.

items.name: Remington Model 11 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came off a lumber schooner at San Pedro wrapped in oilcloth, listed on the manifest as fence posts. The receiver still smells faintly of tar and harbour water.

items.name: Chitin-plated Thompson M1928
items.desc: Plated end to end in salvaged shell at the forward camp below the sign, by men who had stopped caring how a gun looked. On Mount Lee, anything that survives a Brute's charge is handsome enough.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of Agility
items.desc: One Strip bouncer swore by it: keep the feet moving and the muzzle down. He kept both, right up until the night a Flier came through a speakeasy skylight.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of Stamina
items.desc: Belonged to a night watchman at the Christie lot who held the paint-shop door for nine hours with it, then walked home for breakfast. Nobody has managed to make him tell it differently.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Acrobat
items.desc: Rented for a rooftop chase picture in which the double leapt from the Taft Building onto a moving truck. He did it in one take, gun and all, and the director asked for another.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Marksman
items.desc: A Prohibition agent filed the front sight to his own taste and fired it in short, thrifty bursts of two rounds apiece. The Bureau never reimbursed him for the file.

items.name: Thompson M1928 of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came ashore at San Pedro in a crate marked pianos, underneath four hundred pounds of actual pianos. The longshoreman who found it decided he had earned the commission.

items.name: Chitin-plated Riot Shield
items.desc: Faced entirely in shell taken off Elder Soldiers below Mount Lee. The hive seems to recognise its own and strikes it twice as hard out of spite.

items.name: Riot Shield of Strength
items.desc: Hynes's Red Squad carried this one through a Plaza meeting last March. The dents along the rim are the only minutes anyone kept.

items.name: Riot Shield of Stamina
items.desc: Patrolmen on the Boulevard beat swear it has outlasted three sergeants, two chiefs' speeches and a pension board.

items.name: Riot Shield of the Boxer
items.desc: Hung for a season behind the ring at the Legion Stadium, where it caught a flying stool most Friday nights and never once complained to the referee.

items.name: Riot Shield of the Stevedore
items.desc: Came up from the San Pedro docks after the '23 strike, still smelling of tarred rope and other men's opinions.

items.name: Chitin-plated Arc Lamp
items.desc: Plated in shell cut from a Hive Tunnels soldier, it weighs as much as a newsreel camera and takes a blow better than one. Whatever grew that armour was never meant to carry light.

items.name: Arc Lamp of Intellect
items.desc: Belonged to a gaffer on the First National lot who could recite the whole stage wiring diagram from memory, and frequently did, uninvited. The carbons still burn a clean, thinking white.

items.name: Arc Lamp of Spirit
items.desc: Kept lit through three nights on the Mount Lee ridge so the forward camp could see one another's faces. The men swear it warms a tent better than any stove, which the quartermaster disputes.

items.name: Arc Lamp of the Engineer
items.desc: Rewired at the Lockheed plant by a fellow who swore it could survive a drop from the top of a hangar door. He tested the theory twice and was asked to stop.

items.name: Arc Lamp of the Doctor
items.desc: A surgeon at the river camp clamped it over his table when the generator quit. Steady hands, a steady arc, and only one complaint about the smell of hot carbon.

items.name: Arc Lamp of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried at the head of a Sunday procession down Ventura Boulevard, a hymnal in the other hand. It still smells faintly of pew polish, and nobody argued with the deacon while it was lit.

items.name: Chitin-plated Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit
items.desc: Plated in carapace from the Hive Tunnels, it has been dropped off a ridge, stepped on by a Brute and slept on as a pillow. The splints inside are cut from the same shell, which nobody likes to mention.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of Intellect
items.desc: Its owner pencilled dosage tables inside the lid in a hand so small and so correct that the drugstore on Highland tried to hire her.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of Spirit
items.desc: Found on the Echo Park boathouse dock beside a thermos and a note promising back in ten minutes. Whoever left it never hurried, and it shows.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of the Engineer
items.desc: Rebuilt by a Lockheed fitter with a hinged tray and a socket wrench under the splints, since wounds and engines tend to fail at the same hour.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of the Doctor
items.desc: Lifted from a house-call bag on Los Feliz Boulevard, its stethoscope still coiled under the cotton wool. The physician got out. His Packard did not.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson First Aid Kit of the Deacon
items.desc: Smells of hymnals, liniment and the long walk to Angelus Temple. Somebody pressed a poppy between the bandage rolls and nobody has had the heart to remove it.

items.name: Chitin-plated Family Bible
items.desc: Plated front and back in soldier chitin, the family record copied onto fresh paper because the old pages smelled of the hive. The last entry lists three names taken to Burbank, with no date beside them.

items.name: Family Bible of Intellect
items.desc: The margins are crowded with pencilled cross-references in a schoolteacher's hand, Leviticus argued against Luke. Whoever owned it read the whole thing twice and the concordance three times.

items.name: Family Bible of Spirit
items.desc: Pressed between the pages are a dried orange blossom from a 1903 wedding and a lock of baby hair folded in wax paper. It is calmer to hold than it has any right to be.

items.name: Family Bible of the Engineer
items.desc: A Lockheed riveter carried it in his lunch pail for eleven years. The cover is dented where a falling bucking bar found it instead of him, which he took as a plain answer to prayer.

items.name: Family Bible of the Doctor
items.desc: Kept in the waiting room of a Vermont Avenue physician, who wrote dosages on the flyleaf whenever his prescription pad ran out. Half his patients came for the doctor and half for Ecclesiastes.

items.name: Family Bible of the Deacon
items.desc: Carried on foot from Edendale to Angelus Temple every Sunday for nine years, and it smells of hymnals and wet wool. Sister Aimee is said to have signed the flyleaf; the deacon never let anyone check.

items.name: Grauman's Usher Coat
items.desc: Sid Grauman dressed his ushers like palace guards and drilled them like a regiment. This one held his post through the first night of the invasion, seating patrons by flashlight until there were no patrons left to seat.

items.name: Brood Keeper's Carapace Vest
items.desc: Somebody quilted a canvas vest and stitched a drone's back-plate over the heart. The thing it came off had been guarding eggs in the Egyptian's basement, and the vest still twitches faintly when the house lights go down.

items.name: Projectionist's Eyeshade
items.desc: Up in the booth, a projectionist threads reels by the glare of a carbon arc and keeps one eye on the fire bucket. Nitrate film forgives nobody, and the men who wore these learned to think fast and talk little.

items.name: Warden's Chitin Helm
items.desc: An M1917 doughboy helmet, its dents filled with a plate of invader shell hammered to the curve. The Legion armourer who made it called it the first good use anybody had found for the things.

items.name: Matriarch's Acid-etched Gloves
items.desc: Brown kid gloves that went into the hive and came out pocked and pale wherever the spit landed. The acid left the leather tougher than before, which the glovemaker on Highland takes as a personal insult.

items.name: Stagehand's Rigging Gloves
items.desc: Fly-gallery men haul sandbags and backdrops forty feet above the stage on hemp line, and a slipped grip means a lawsuit or a funeral. These have rope burns worn straight into the palms.

items.name: Egyptian Court Sandals
items.desc: Worn by a dancing girl in the stage prologue Grauman ran before every feature, back when a picture needed a pageant to sell it. Each step still sounds like a small curtain call.

items.name: Hive Mother's Girdle
items.desc: Cut from the belly-band of the brood mother nesting beneath the Egyptian's stage. It tightens slightly when insects are near, which some wearers find useful and others find reason to sleep in another room.

items.name: Robin Hood's Prop Tights
items.desc: Douglas Fairbanks opened the Egyptian in 1922 with Robin Hood, and wardrobe never threw anything away. A dozen stuntmen went down a dozen castle walls in these, and the seat is patched exactly where you would expect.

items.name: Orchestra Pit Trousers
items.desc: The house orchestra played on the night the Dome came down, right up until the brass section was carried off. A violinist kept these, along with his low opinion of the conductor's tempo.

items.name: Sid's Opening Night Cufflinks
items.desc: Grauman wore these to the 1922 premiere and every one after it, until he swore they had turned unlucky. He gave them away the week the Dome went up, which rather settled the argument.

items.name: Scarab Signet
items.desc: Bought from a curio stall on the Boulevard the year everyone went mad for King Tut. The seller swore it came out of a real tomb; the brass showing under the green glaze suggests Pasadena.

items.name: Pharaoh's Paste Necklace
items.desc: Every stone in it is glass and every inch of gilt is paint, built to read as a king's ransom from row thirty. Studio jewellers call that honesty, of a sort.

items.name: Usher's Brass Whistle Chain
items.desc: Ushers carried these to whistle down rowdy patrons and runaway children. Lately the shrill blast scatters broodlings too, and the head usher counts that as a promotion.

items.name: Crypt Keeper's Shroud
items.desc: Linen wrappings from a keeper who watched over the Hollywood Cemetery crypts long after the mourners stopped coming. It smells of lilies, damp stone and something chemical underneath that the mortuary staff decline to discuss.

items.name: Sexton's Mud Boots
items.desc: Twenty years the sexton dug graves at Hollywood Cemetery, and this autumn he filled them faster than ever. His boots never once stuck in the clay, which he credited to clean living and a pint of dubbin a week.

items.name: Warner Grip's Harness
items.desc: A grip on the Sunset lot buckled this on to climb the catwalks and rig lamps for Warner pictures. The invaders kept the stages running after he was gone; the harness turned up hanging from a scaffold, still clipped.

items.name: Vitaphone Engineer's Headset
items.desc: Built for the Warner sound stages, where a cough in the third row could cost a day's shooting. The engineer who wore it heard everything when the hive came through the soundproofing. He wrote it all down, in a very steady hand.

items.name: Rin Tin Tin's Collar
items.desc: Warner Bros. paid the dog better than most of its writers, and nobody on the lot thought that unfair. He wears a spare these days; this one was retired after he took a Drone by the leg on Sunset.

items.name: Zookeeper's Bite Sleeve
items.desc: Thick canvas and horsehair, laced to the elbow, made for the morning feed at the bear grottoes. Since the invasion, the keepers at Griffith Park have learned that the lions were the polite ones.

items.name: Greek Theatre Chorus Robe
items.desc: Sewn for the first season of the new Greek Theatre, when the hills filled with people come to hear tragedy in the open air. The chorus still sings up there some nights, to coyotes and the Dome.

items.name: The Gag Man's Derby
items.desc: Every gag man on the Chaplin lot kept one hat for thinking and one for falling down in. This is the second kind, dented in nine places and blocked back into shape eight times.

items.name: Cornero's Rum-Runner Slicker
items.desc: Tony Cornero wore it on the deck of a rum boat off Santa Monica Bay, running Canadian whisky past the Coast Guard in the fog. The oiled hide still smells of brine and good rye. Under the Dome there is no sea left to run, which he takes personally.

items.name: Fairbanks' Fencing Jacket
items.desc: Cut close for The Black Pirate, so the star could ride a knife down a sail and look good doing it. The lining is padded at the ribs, where the prop sabres landed more often than the publicity department admitted.

items.name: Dam Keeper's Waders
items.desc: Since St. Francis went, the keeper has walked the toe of Mulholland Dam each dawn, listening for water where water should not be. He still walks it. Now he listens for chewing.

items.name: Krotona Initiate's Sash
items.desc: Krotona's Theosophists left Beachwood Canyon for Ojai years ago, but some of their silk stayed behind in a cedar chest. The colours are meant to aid meditation. They also hide resin stains rather well.

items.name: Stembridge Armourer's Apron
items.desc: Worn behind the counter at 5451 Marathon, where every Thompson in pictures went out on loan and came back to be cleaned. The canvas is burned in neat rows from hot brass. Armourers count every gun out and every round back.

items.name: Bronson Gate Guard Cap
items.desc: Nobody passed the Bronson Gate without a name on the list, and the man under this cap once turned away a director's mother on her birthday. When the hive came, he asked for their names too.

items.name: Marathon Street Queen's Mantle
items.desc: Woven by captured wardrobe girls on the Paramount stages, in silk and something the Queen secreted for the purpose. It hums under hot lamps. The women were promised screen credit, which suggests the hive already understands Hollywood.

items.name: Dragna Lieutenant's Spats
items.desc: Dragna's man in the Paramount gun room kept his spats whiter than the Production Code requires. A dead man's shoes are bad luck, the boys say, but his spats are merely fashionable.

items.name: Chaney's Greasepaint Kit
items.desc: The Man of a Thousand Faces carries his make-up on a cord round his neck these days, in case he must become somebody else in a hurry. Inside: crepe hair, collodion, fish skin and a little wire for the nose. He does not lend it lightly.

items.name: Phantom's Opera Cloak
items.desc: Made for the Red Death masquerade in 1925 and kept on Stage 28 ever since, beside the opera house nobody dared strike. Something from the hive has taken to the set. The cloak came off its shoulders.

items.name: Laemmle's Lucky Watch Chain
items.desc: Uncle Carl kept a horseshoe charm on it and swore the thing had paid for Universal City twice over. He has given it to whoever keeps the backlot standing longest; luck, he says, is wasted on a man indoors.

items.name: Keystone Kop Helmet
items.desc: Mack Sennett's Kops mostly wore felt; this one was beaten from steel for a gag that called for a piano to land on it. The stuntman lived. The piano did not. A Brute's blow, it turns out, is easier.

items.name: Bathing Beauty's Slippers
items.desc: Sennett's girls never got these wet; the studio paid for sunshine, not seawater. Found on a dressing-room floor at the Studio City lot, still dusted with talc and pointed toward the door.

items.name: Lockheed Riveter's Gauntlets
items.desc: Built to hold a bucking bar against a wing spar for a ten-hour shift. The plant's new owners work the line with mandibles now, and the old crew's gloves turned up stacked by the time clock, untouched.

items.name: Test Pilot's Goggles
items.desc: Every test pilot at United swore these lenses were lucky, which is what test pilots say about anything they come home wearing. A film of amber resin clouds one rim, where something flew alongside a little too long.

items.name: Vega Mechanic's Coveralls
items.desc: Oil-black at the knees and pocketed for every wrench in the Burbank shop. The man who wore them knew a Vega's engine by its sound alone, which is exactly why the hive decided to keep him.

items.name: Hive Queen's Chitin Crown
items.desc: Not a crown, strictly, but the hard ridge of the Mount Lee queen's brow, cut free and lined with felt by a Legion armourer who will not discuss it. It still hums when the hills go quiet.

items.name: Mantle of the Thirteen Letters
items.desc: Woven on the ridge behind the sign from hive silk and sheet metal stripped off all thirteen letters. The realtors paid a fortune to light HOLLYWOODLAND at night; the mantle still flickers faintly, as if remembering the bill.

items.name: Aviatrix's Flight Jacket
items.desc: Women flew out of United farther and faster than the newsreels admitted. This jacket came back from the hangars with a torn sleeve and a cracked compass in the pocket, and the women at the field still keep its owner's seat.

items.name: Hangar Mother's Carapace
items.desc: Something in the United hangars laid its brood in the cabins of grounded airliners. Its back plate, riveted to a steel vest by men who had flown with nothing beneath them but air, turns a bullet the way a hangar door turns rain.

items.name: Architect's Drafting Gloves
items.desc: Fine kid gloves smudged with graphite, recovered from the hangar office where the hive laid out its tunnels in pencil on real blueprints. Someone up there taught them to draw. Nobody wants to learn who.

items.name: King Consort's Greaves
items.desc: Her Majesty's consort guarded the chamber for years and was never once asked his opinion, a position familiar to several husbands on the Boulevard. His leg shells, strapped over steel, hold firm when the mountain shakes.

items.name: Trimotor Pilot's Boots
items.desc: Fleece-lined for the cold over the Tehachapis, back when there was somewhere to fly. The pilot left them on the rudder pedals of a Ford Trimotor in the end hangar; the plane is still there, full of eggs.

items.name: Heart Chamber Signet
items.desc: Pried from the wall of the innermost chamber on Mount Lee, where the resin pulses slowly like a sleeper breathing. Preachers wear it and swear the ring prays along with them. Nobody has asked to whom.

items.name: Beery's Barnstormer Scarf
items.desc: Wallace Beery flew his own plane and described it at length to anyone at the airport lunch counter. He gave this scarf to the first crew back from the hangars, asked for it back, then thought better of it.

items.name: Runway Queen's Sash
items.desc: Its first owner won the airport's opening-day pageant and wore it for one afternoon. The hive moved into the hangars soon after, and the sash went to work; backed in tooled leather, it holds a holster better than it ever held a title.

items.name: Deacon's Revival Vestments
items.desc: Stitched for the tent revivals Angelus Temple carried into the hills, heavy enough to stop a spitter's acid and plain enough to satisfy the deacons. The collar still smells of lamp oil and five thousand hymnals.

items.name: Chorus Conductor's Cuffs
items.desc: Starched linen worn by the choirmaster at the Hollywood Bowl's Easter sunrise service. He kept conducting the night the swarm came over the Pass, and the hymn held just long enough for the crowd to reach the road.

items.name: Usher's Flashlight Baton
items.desc: Grauman's ushers were drilled like Marines, and this one cleared a Drone from the Egyptian's forecourt with the same nickel-plated torch he used to find patrons their seats. The bulb still works, which is more than the Drone can say.

items.name: Hive Warden's Mandible
items.desc: Pried from the thing that guarded the hive chamber under the Egyptian. The jaw is serrated like a bread knife and twice as hungry, and somebody has wrapped the hinge in friction tape and called it a handle.

items.name: Egyptian Prop Khopesh
items.desc: Carved for a stage prologue in 1922 and sharpened for the first time in 1930. The gilt paint flakes off in the scabbard; the edge, somebody discovered the hard way, does not.

items.name: Projection Booth Arc Lamp
items.desc: Carbon rods hiss inside the housing the way they did through every reel of the opening run. The projectionist claimed it could throw a picture through cigar smoke and a bad review.

items.name: Matriarch's Spitting Gland Sprayer
items.desc: A Colt frame married to an invader gland by a stagehand with steady nerves and no medical training. It fires what the Matriarch used to spit, and it smells exactly like it.

items.name: Stage Brace
items.desc: Every flat on the Egyptian's stage leaned on a few of these hardwood braces. Unbolted from the scenery, it props up a fight just as well, though the set has never quite stood straight since.

items.name: Lighting Rigger's Wrench
items.desc: Its owner tightened clamps forty feet above the stage and never once dropped a tool on an actor, a record he considered the finest achievement in pictures.

items.name: Robin Hood's Prop Quarterstaff
items.desc: Douglas Fairbanks's Robin Hood opened the Egyptian in 1922, and this staff came out of the storage room still waiting for its cue. Light enough to vault with, which the stuntmen did, and heavy enough to matter.

items.name: Sexton's Spade
items.desc: Hollywood Cemetery's old sexton kept the edge keen and the handle oiled through forty years of quiet work. Since the crypts went bad the work has been noisier, and the spade has had to dig faster.

items.name: Stembridge Rental Thompson
items.desc: Checked out of the gun room at 5451 Marathon for a gangster picture and never returned. The rental slip is still tucked under the stock, and the late fee now exceeds the picture's budget.

items.name: Tom Mix's Peacemaker
items.desc: Tom Mix swears he only fired it for the cameras, the crowds at the Gower stables and one very insistent rattlesnake. The ivory grips have picked up a few new scratches he would rather not explain.

items.name: Chandelier Chain
items.desc: Links of a lobby chandelier's brass chain, wound around a lead counterweight. The hive had nested in the crystal; the chandelier came down, and the chain stayed on to be useful.

items.name: Post 43 Springfield
items.desc: The men at Post 43 hand this rifle only to someone they would share a foxhole with, and they are particular. Its stock is scored with a tally that began in the Argonne and continues on Mount Lee.

items.name: Crawford's Thompson
items.desc: Charlie Crawford keeps a violin case in his Sunset office that has never held a violin. When he opens it for someone, it means the syndicate trusts them, or wants them where the trouble is.

items.name: Letter H Girder
items.desc: Torn from the HOLLYWOODLAND sign when the hive climbed Mount Lee, the steel still carries a strip of white sheet metal and a few dead bulbs. The realtors would like it back. The hive would like whoever is holding it.

items.name: Hive Queen's Stinger
items.desc: Taken from the queen of the Mount Lee Hive, who used it to decide which of the taken stayed awake for the cameras. Amber venom still beads at the tip, slow as honey and nowhere near as kind.

items.name: Tower Beacon
items.desc: Pulled from United Airport's control tower and rewired to run off a battery pack and sheer spite. It once guided mail planes over the Valley; now it guides the living out of the hangars.

items.name: Architect's T-Square
items.desc: Belonged to the draughtsman who laid out the Lockheed plant, and later to the hive, which studied his plans with alarming interest. One edge is ruled in inches; the other in something no surveyor recognises.

items.name: Sister Aimee's Pulpit Bible
items.desc: Sister Aimee preached from this Bible to five thousand at Angelus Temple and to every radio in the basin over KFSG. The margins are crowded with her notes; the cover is scorched where it stopped something with too many legs.

items.name: Kop Captain's Nightstick
items.desc: Mack Sennett's Keystone captain waved it through two hundred chases and never hit anybody on purpose. The hive took over the studio and missed the joke entirely, so the stick has had a busier year.

items.name: Belleau Wood Trench Club
items.desc: Marines carried clubs like this into the wheat at Belleau Wood in June of 1918. Its owner drank at Post 43 and never spoke of the wood, except to say the insects at least make noise coming.

items.name: Stunt Double's Weighted Gloves
items.desc: Lead shot is sewn across the knuckles, a trick from a double who took Fairbanks's punches for eleven pictures and never once got billing. The studio paid him seven-fifty a day. The invaders pay nothing, but they fall down convincingly.

items.name: Studio Armourer's Winchester
items.desc: Stembridge's gun room rented this Winchester to forty westerns, always loaded with blanks. When the Dome came down, an armourer on Marathon Street pulled the blank adapter, fed it live rounds and found the old rifle remembered how.

items.name: Klieg Light Reflector
items.desc: Polished to throw a carbon arc across a soundstage, the dish still catches whatever light is going and hands it back hotter. Actresses blamed it for klieg eyes. The insects take it worse.

items.name: Powder Monkey's Tamping Bar
items.desc: Brass and hickory, because steel strikes sparks and powder men who forget that end up as a line in the trade papers. An effects crew at the Egyptian packed charges with it for a Nile picture that never finished shooting.

items.name: Queen of Angels Field Satchel
items.desc: Stitched for the sisters at Queen of Angels Hospital and carried up Bellevue Avenue on calls the ambulance would not make. Iodine, gauze, a rosary in the side pocket and a prayer card nobody has the heart to throw out.

items.name: Circuit Rider's Saddle Bible
items.desc: Some Methodist preacher rode a thousand miles of Arizona with this in a saddlebag, and the cover shows every one. The margins hold pencilled names of baptisms, burials and a horse thief he forgave. Sister Aimee approved of the mileage.

items.name: Model T Crank Handle
items.desc: Every Ford owner in Los Angeles knew the crank kicked back hard enough to break a wrist; doctors called it chauffeur's fracture. A garage man on Cahuenga swears it kicks harder now, and only at things with six legs.

items.name: Zip Gun
items.desc: Pipe, a door bolt and rubber strapping, put together in a Gower Gulch alley by a boy who has since gone missing. It fires roughly where it points, most days.

items.name: Sawed-off Coach Gun
items.desc: Wells Fargo guards rode shotgun with something like it, until a bootlegger on the Strip took a hacksaw to both ends. Now it fits under an overcoat and clears a speakeasy doorway in one argument.

items.name: Hot Dog
items.desc: Bought from a cart at Hollywood and Highland whose owner refused to close for the end of the world. Mustard, onions and no questions.

items.name: Coffee
items.desc: Black, hot and boiling since dawn in an aid-station pot. Nobody drinks it for the taste.

items.name: Ham Sandwich
items.desc: Rye bread, mustard and ham sliced thin enough to read a contract through. The studio commissary wraps them for extras who were told lunch was an hour ago.

items.name: Coca-Cola
items.desc: Ice cold from the drugstore cooler on Highland, where the soda jerk still counts the empties. No trucks get through the Dome, so every bottle opened is one fewer.

items.name: Blue Plate Special
items.desc: Meat loaf, mashed potatoes and peas sharing a divided plate at a Cahuenga lunch counter. The waitress calls everyone honey, the Legion sergeant included.

items.name: Hires Root Beer
items.desc: Sassafras, sarsaparilla and a foam head a temperance lady can admire in public. The Legion keeps a crate behind the bar it officially does not have.

items.name: Chili Size
items.desc: An open hamburger drowned in chili beans and onions, the house dish of every all-night stand south of Sunset. Eaten with a fork, a spoon and some resolve.

items.name: Egg Cream
items.desc: A New York soda-fountain drink with neither egg nor cream in it, brought west by a Brooklyn screenwriter who complains about the coast in every letter home.

items.name: Cobb Salad
items.desc: Chopped bacon, avocado, egg and chicken lined up in rows like a chorus line. A kitchen trick for clearing out the icebox, which under the Dome describes most of the menu.

items.name: Orange Julep
items.desc: Valley oranges whipped frothy with ice at a stand on the road to Studio City. The groves beyond it are going to seed under the Dome, so the stand squeezes while the fruit lasts.

items.name: Musso & Frank Steak Dinner
items.desc: Grilled over open flame on the Boulevard since 1919 and carried out by waiters who have outlasted three studio heads. They see no reason the insects should rate a hurry. Charge it to the picture.

items.name: Brown Derby Coffee
items.desc: Poured at the Brown Derby on Vine, where the cream comes in silver and the booths face the door so nobody misses an entrance. Agents drink it by the gallon and bill the client.

items.name: Linen Bandage
items.desc: Torn from bedsheets donated to the aid station by a Whitley Heights landlady who would like them back.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson Gauze Roll
items.desc: Sterile, wrapped and sealed, shipped from New Jersey before the Dome came down and rationed ever since. Nurses count the rolls twice a shift.

items.name: Bootleg Gin
items.desc: Cut in an Edendale bathtub and bottled in whatever the drugstores threw out. Crawford's men swear it is genuine; the label swears it is hair tonic.

items.name: Mk II Fragmentation Grenade
items.blurb: Army surplus "pineapple". Thrown at your target: damages every invader within 6 m of it.

items.name: Smoke Pot
items.blurb: A stage effects pot. Everything fighting you within 30 m loses track of you.

items.name: Smelling Salts
items.blurb: Clears the head: removes stuns, dazes and slows.

items.name: Patent Tonic
items.blurb: "Cures what ails you." Restores 30% of your health at once.

items.name: .38 Special Lead Round-Nose
items.blurb: Fits revolvers, automatic pistols and the Thompson. +0.5 damage per second. Used one round per shot.
items.desc: The patrolman's round. Every Colt Police Positive on the Boulevard eats these, and the station sergeant counts them back in at the end of each shift like a bank teller with a grudge.

items.name: .45 ACP Full Metal Jacket
items.blurb: Fits revolvers, automatic pistols and the Thompson. Hits harder. +1.4 damage per second. Used one round per shot.
items.desc: Stembridge used to lend these out by the case for gangster pictures, blanks mostly. The live ones in the back room went quietly missing the week the Dome came down.

items.name: .30-30 Winchester Soft-Point
items.blurb: Fits lever-action and bolt rifles. +0.6 damage per second. Used one round per shot.
items.desc: Deer cartridges from a Glendale hardware store, built to drop a mule deer at a hundred yards. A bug the size of a Model A is somewhat outside their experience.

items.name: .30-06 Springfield Ball
items.blurb: Fits lever-action and bolt rifles. Army surplus. +1.6 damage per second. Used one round per shot.
items.desc: Surplus from the war, crated in 1918 and sold off cheap after the Armistice. Post 43 men handle it like an old acquaintance they never much liked.

items.name: 12-Gauge Birdshot Shells
items.blurb: Fits pump and auto shotguns. +0.6 damage per second. Used one round per shot.
items.desc: Meant for quail in the Verdugo foothills. Against an invader it mostly stings, though stinging is a start.

items.name: 12-Gauge 00 Buckshot Shells
items.blurb: Fits pump and auto shotguns. Stops a charging drone. +1.6 damage per second. Used one round per shot.
items.desc: Nine lead balls the size of peas in every shell. The Hollywood desk sergeant keeps a box beside the telephone and no longer answers it without one in his hand.

items.name: Cracked Mandible
items.desc: Half a jaw that once worked through plaster, lath and a studio carpenter's lunch pail. The junkman on Cahuenga pays by the pound and asks no questions.

items.name: Bent Antenna
items.desc: Kinked at the middle like a rabbit-ear aerial after a bad night. Radio men swear these things hum on the KFSG frequency.

items.name: Dull Chitin Flake
items.desc: Too thin for armour, too ugly for jewellery. Somebody on the Boulevard is surely selling them as lucky charms.

items.name: Matted Fur
items.desc: A clump of coyote coat, burrs included at no extra charge. The Gower Gulch saddlery won't touch it.

items.name: Chewed Bone
items.desc: Something gnawed it clean and then lost interest. Best not to wonder what it came from.

items.name: Empty Hip Flask
items.desc: Dry as the Volstead Act intended. It still smells of rye and poor decisions.

items.name: Pawn Ticket
items.desc: Redeemable for one gold watch at a shop on Cahuenga that the hive took in its first week. The interest keeps accruing regardless.

items.name: Broodling Husk
items.desc: The shed skin of a young one, light as tissue paper and still faintly warm. It crackles when picked up, which nobody enjoys.

items.name: Acid-pitted Scale
items.desc: Spitter acid ate a constellation of holes clean through it. Worth nothing, though it does make a fine cheese grater for the desperate.

items.name: Torn Movie Ticket
items.desc: Half an admission to Grauman's Chinese, from the night before the Dome came down. Hell's Angels is still playing, which hardly seems fair.

items.name: Scrap Metal
items.blurb: Salvaged from wrecks. Used in Gunsmithing and Metalworking.
items.desc: Fender, bedspring and somebody's Model T door, beaten flat enough to carry. Every machine shop on the lot will take it, no questions about where it came from.

items.name: Chitin Shard
items.desc: Lighter than tin and harder than a landlord's heart. It still rattles faintly when the wind comes off the hills.

items.name: Coyote Pelt
items.desc: Burrs in the fur and a smell of chaparral. The Gower Gulch saddlery pays fair, and the coyotes have stopped complaining.

items.name: Invader Gland
items.blurb: Salvaged from Spitters. Used in Pharmacy.
items.desc: Wrap it twice and keep it upright. The Boulevard druggists swear it is medicine once boiled, and nobody has asked them to swear twice.

items.name: Brass Casings
items.desc: Swept from the Legion firing line and the gutters of Hollywood and Vine alike. Brass is brass, and Stembridge reloads anything.

items.name: Wool Cloth
items.desc: Cut from a bolt the wardrobe department never got to bill anyone for. Plain charcoal, the colour of half the extras' suits in town.

items.name: White Sage
items.desc: Picked on the dry slopes above the Vermont Canyon camp. Burn a sprig and the hut smells like church; boil it and the nurses have their uses.

items.name: Hive Resin
items.desc: Warm to the touch long after it should have cooled, and something small is set inside it like a fly in amber. Men who dig it out of the Tunnels do not talk much afterward.

items.name: Elder Chitin Plate
items.desc: Thick as a church door and twice as stubborn. It took a crowbar, a hacksaw and a bad afternoon on Mount Lee to pry this one loose.
